!TOPIC 101 General
{red}General Remarks{/red}
                                                 {link}102{-link}-> Deutscher Text{/link}
                                                 {link}122{-link}-> SOFiSTiK-Data{/link}


The database for the SOFiSTiK programs is a proprietary system based on
an indexsequential philosophy. This stands for an sequential access to
data organized in logical records adressed by a key formed by two
Integers.

CDBASE may be seen by the programmer as an unlimited number of
sequential streams organized in the form of a linked list. Physically
CDBASE is formed by a direct access diskfile with fixed record length
and a memory buffer to enhance IO-Operations.

The system CDBASE is optimized for typical FE-Analysis. Typically there
exist large data volumes which are organized in a sequential manner. It
is quite more often that data is changed than the data structure
itself. That's why some operations are not possible in CDBASE.

CDBASE may be called from FORTRAN or C. This description is valid for
the version 4.0 (developed since summer 1994) which is the base for the
32-bit SOFiSTiK 95 Release.


{red}Properties:{/red}


  - Up to 64 physical data base files each up to 256 GigaByte
    (one of them is a scratch)

  - For each data base 2^63 differnet keys possible

  - Unlimited number of records

  - varying record lengths within a key possible
    (not recommended for compatibility reasons to rational databases)

  - Write records to the start (Delete) or to the end (Append) or
    relative to the readpointer (Replace). Insert is not available!

  - Read records from the beginning or relative to the readpointer

  - Read and Replace parts of the records. Insert is not available!

  - Read and write records of the same index independantly.

  - Multitasking supported with locking and time stamping


Each write process should be done immediately. This ensures consistent
data in nearly all cases. For multitasking access however a lazy write
will improve over all performance considerably. Last not least reading
will use databuffer allowing complete incore access from a client.

Locking is done via special entries in the database and the
possibilities provided by the operating system (lockd / SHARE etc.) The
lowest level ensures that writing of directory entries or requesting
dataspace is only possible by a single process at the same time.

The next level locks a complete key. If you write to a key you will
lock implicitly all records within the key. Other processes may lock
other keys at the same time. You may lock a key explicitly by a call,
then have to remove the lock explicitly by an other call. The implicit
locks created by a writing process, is implictly released by a read
from the same process.

Only if a process frees all his locks he is allowed to read new
directory items from the data base. This is a measure to prevent the
database from accessing the directory structures to often. If the
process creates a new key, the directory is of course updated at once.

The locking can be done "shared" for reading (several locks possible for
the same key) or "exclusive" (only one process may access the key) Due
to the automatic locking mechanisms the discipline of the programmer is
not required in most cases.

To prevent classical dead-lock situations, each process running on a
time out will free all his locks and then retry the lock for the last
required key. When ending a program all locks have to be freed. This
might be a problem in the case of unexpected signals or interrupts. A
program to clear all locks (DBINFO) is available.

Local needed keys are stored in separate scratch files for each process.
these files are only written if necessary (lazy write)
;=====================================================================R

!TOPIC 102 Vorbemerkung
;Kapitel B

{red}Vorbemerkung{/red}
                                                 {link}101{-link}-> English Text{/link}
                                                 {link}122{-link}-> SOFiSTiK-Data{/link}


Die Datenbank der SOFiSTiK Programme wird mit einer Eigenentwicklung zur
indexsequentiellen Datenverwaltung realisiert. Dies bedeutet, dass der Zugriff
auf Daten über einen zweistufigen Schlüssel (Kennwort, Index) erfolgt, der
sequentiell in Sätzen (Records) geschrieben und gelesen wird.

Logisch (für den Programmierer) bildet CDBASE eine unbeschränkte Anzahl von
verketteten Listen beliebigen Inhalts. Physikalisch ist CDBASE eine Datei
fester (optimaler) Recordlänge und einem Hauptspeicherbereich zur
Beschleunigung der IO-Operationen.

Das System CDBASE ist für FE-Anwendungen optimiert. Typisch hierfür sind grosse
Datenmengen, die weitgehend sequentiell verarbeitet werden. Geändert werden
normalerweise nur der Inhalt von Daten, nicht jedoch deren Struktur. Deshalb
sind verschiedene Operationen nicht vorgesehen.

CDBASE kann von FORTRAN oder C angesprochen werden. Diese Beschreibung gilt für
die im Sommer 1994 entwickelte Version 4.00 mit einigen wesentlichen
Neuentwicklungen.


{red}Eigenschaften:{/red}


  - Bis zu acht physikalische Datenbasen mit bis zu 2 GigaByte

  - Je Datenbasis 263 verschiedene Kennwort-Schlüssel möglich

  - Anzahl Records je Kennwort nur durch physikalische Grösse beschränkt

  - beliebige variable Recordlänge innerhalb eines Kennworts
    (Zur Umsetzung in relationale Tabellen ist jedoch eine feste
     Recordlänge sinnvoll zu vereinbaren.)

  - Schreiben   von  Sätzen an den Anfang (löscht Index) an das Ende
    (Anfügen)  oder  vor  der  aktuellen  Lese-Position  (Ersetzen
    von Daten innerhalb eines Records ohne dessen Länge zu verändern).

  - Lesen von Sätzen von vorn, von der aktuellen Position oder von
    der aktuellen Position zurück (z.B. letzten Satz noch einmal).

  - Lesen und Ersetzen von Sätzen auch teilweise.

  - Unabhängiges Schreiben und Lesen vom gleichen Index

  - Multitasking Fähigkeiten durch Lock auf Index oder Datei und
    Aktualisierungsinformationen

  - Begriffe:

      Index  ist der Schlüssel unter dem Daten abgelegt werden
      Record ist der logische Record eines Schreib/Lesevorgangs
      Item   ist ein Wert eines Records


Gegenüber dem alten Prinzip einer vollständigen Zwischenpufferung ist das  neue
Entwurfsprinzip nun erstens, jeden Schreibvorgang unmittelbar auszuführen. (Das
Betriebssystem  kann  natürlich noch mal zwischenpuffern).  Beim  Lesen  jedoch
sollte  als zweites Ziel eine effektivere incore-Speicherung ausgenützt  werden
können.  Es  sollte also nur noch in ganz seltenen  Fällen  eine  inkonsistente
Datenbank bei Programmabstürzen entstehen.

Das  Locking  erfolgt  über  die von UNIX bzw.  DOS  zur  Verfügung  gestellten
Mechanismen  der bereichsweisen Locks und zusätzlichen Einträgen in der  Datei.

Als  unterste  Stufe  soll  sichergestellt  werden,  dass  Schreibvorgänge   auf
Directory-Einträge  oder das Belegen eines neuen Records nur von einem  Prozess
gleichzeitig erfolgen kann.

Die zweite Stufe ist das Sperren einzelner Schlüssel. Bei jedem
Schreiben eines Index wird der ganze Index durch einen Eintrag in seinem
Inhaltsverzeichnis gesperrt. Mehrere Prozesse können dabei vollkommen
unabhängig voneinander unterschiedliche Indices beschreiben. Die Sperre
muss explizit vom Programm wieder freigegeben werden wenn sie explizit
angefordert wurde. Es ist jedoch auch ein automatisches Locking
vorgesehen, dass beim Schreiben aktiviert wird und beim Lesen des
geleichen Schlüssels wieder freigibt. Während einer Sperre können andere
Prozesse auf diesen Index weder schreibend, wenn "exclusive" gelockt
wurde auch nicht lesend zugreifen.

Erst  nach  der  Freigabe  aller seiner Locks kann  ein  Prozess  das  aktuelle
Inhaltsverzeichnis  von  der Datei wieder aktualisieren. Damit wird  vor  allem
verhindert,  dass  ein Prozess sich dauernd auf der Datei  nach  neuen  Inhalten
erkundigen  muss. Wenn er einen neuen Index anlegt, wird die  Directory-Struktur
für diesen einen Index abgeglichen.

Sollte  sich  die  klassische Dead-Lock Situation ergeben,  dass  zwei  Prozesse
aufeinander  warten,  so gibt der Prozess, der als erstes  auf  einen  Time-Out
läuft,  alle  seine  locks  frei und wartet  anschliessend  mit  einem  einzigen
Lock-Wunsch. Beim Beenden eines Programms müssen alle Locks freigegeben werden.
Ein  Reparatur-Programm  zur zwangsweisen Beendigung alle Locks  (DBINFO)  ist
natürlich vorhanden.

Lokale Hilfskennworte müssen auf einer Prozesseigenen Scratch-Datei ausgelagert
werden!

!TOPIC 104 cdb_init

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDINIT  (FILENAME,INDEX){/red}
          In:  CHARACTER FILENAME(*)
          In:  INTEGER   Index
          Out: INTEGER   Index=Returnvalue

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}int sof_cdb_init  ( char* FileName, int Index);{/red}


The database FileName will be opened and accessible via Index. It
becomes the active database. This function has to be called before
any other activity is allowed. It will create a scratch database
during the first call.


   FileName      is the complete filename including extension
                 conforming to the rules of the hosting
                 operating system.

   Index = 0     initialise CDBASE and open scratch data base only
   Index = 99    test if NAME is a valid database and open the base
                 if possible. Return with the assigned index.
                 If the file does not exist, it will be created.
   Index = 96    open a scratch database, filename is the path to
                 use or NULL.
   Index = 95    open in read-only mode
   Index = 94    create a new data base (STATUS=NEW)

   Returnvalue:  Index for further access
                 (<0 if error, see clib1.h for meaning of error codes)
                 ( 0 if not a database when called with Index = 99)

   {link}106{-link}sof_cdb_flush{/link}
   {link}107{-link}sof_cdb_close{/link}

   {blue}password protected database{/blue}

   Databases from Version 5* may be protected by a password with up to
   8 characters. Thus they are of course not accessible from older
   versions of the DLLs.

   Set CDBASEVER=500 resp 501 BEFORE creating the database.

   new functions:

{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDSETPW (INDEX,OLDPW,NEWPW,IER){/red}
          {red}SUBROUTINE CDCHECKPW (INDEX,PW,IER){/red}

{blue}C:{/blue}   {red}cd_err_type sof_cdb_setpassword( int index,
                  const char *oldpassword, const char *password );{/red}

       set a password to the CDBASE index.
       oldpassword      old password or "" if not already defined
       password         the new password or "" if to be deleted

       return           0  ok
                        1  file not created with version 5.x
                        2  could not get a file lock
                        3  wrong old password
                        4  wrong format of password

       {red}cd_err_type sof_cdb_checkpassword( int index, const char *password );{/red}

       check database index for correct password
       password        password or "" if no password expected

       return           0 ok or non protected database
                        1 wrong password

!TOPIC 105 cdb_use

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDUSE (Index,Lockstatus){/red}
          In: INTEGER  Index
          In: INTEGER  Lockstatus

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}void sof_cdb_use ( int Index, int LockStatus );{/red}


Select the active database and associate a locking behavior


   Index      = Index of the Database (-1 = current Index)
   LockStatus = 0  do not change lock status
                1  absolute File locking
                   (to be applied before first access!)
                2  accumulative Record locking
                   (Records keep locked until CDFLUSH)
               -1  release Filelocking
               -2  automatic Record locking
                   (Record locks are removed when reaching EOF)

   {link}108{-link}sof_cdb_status{/link}

;=====================================================================R
!TOPIC 106 cdb_flush

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDFLUSH (INDEX){/red}
          In:  INTEGER   Index

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}void sof_cdb_flush (int Index);{/red}


Release all locks. All memory for directories and data is released
The files remain opened and may be accessed as before. Only after
this call the directory structure is reread which allows the access to
newly defined keys. (Index = 0 for all files)


  {link}107{-link}sof_cdb_close{/link}
  {link}104{-link}sof_cdb_init{/link}

!TOPIC 108 cdb_status

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDSTAT (Index,ISTAT){/red}
          In:  INTEGER Index
          Out: INTEGER ISTAT (Returnvalue)

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}int sof_cdb_status ( int Index );{/red}


the current status of the file with Index is returned

    Index       Index of DB
    Returnvalue Stat Bitpattern
                CD_STAT_AKTIV   (1) CDBase is active
                CD_STAT_OPEN    (2) Index is connected to file
                CD_STAT_SWAP    (4) File has ByteSwap
                CD_STAT_READ    (8) File has been read
                CD_STAT_WRITE  (16) File has been written
                CD_STAT_LOCK   (32) File has active locks

    If called with ( index = -1 ), than the Returnvalue will be the
    index of the active database. If the system is not yet opened, a
    value of -1 is returned.

   {link}105{-link}sof_cdb_use{/link}
   {link}115{-link}sof_cdb_kexist{/link}
   {link}116{-link}sof_cdb_getupdate{/link}

!TOPIC 109 cdb_lock

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDLOCK (KWH,KWL){/red}
          {red}SUBROUTINE CDLOCKX (Index,KWH,KWL){/red}
          In:  INTEGER KWH
          In:  INTEGER KWL

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}void sof_cdb_lock ( int kwh, int kwl );{/red}
          {red}void sof_cdb_lock_ex ( int index, int kwh, int kwl );{/red}


Key kwh/kwl will be locked.(kwh/kwl = 0/0 is not allowed).
The lock has to be released explicitly with sof_cdb_free( kwh, kwl) or
sof_cdb_close. This lock ist not changed via calls to sof_cdb_getb or
sof_cdb_putb.

This function is needed for the consistent realisiation of undividable
access. (to increment a counter for example)

         This requires:
                  sof_cdb_lock( 0, 99 );
                  sof_cdb_getb( 0, 99, ... );
                          // Increment value
                  sof_cdb_putb( 0, 99, ... ,-1);
                  sof_cdb_free( 0, 99 );

   The locking may be switched off for single-task environments by
   setting the environment variable {link}121{-link}CDACCESS{/link}.


   {link}111{-link}sof_cdb_free{/link}
   {link}106{-link}sof_cdb_flush{/link}


!TOPIC 111 cdb_free

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDFREE (KWH,KWL){/red}
          {red}SUBROUTINE CDFREEX (Index,KWH,KWL){/red}
          In:  INTEGER KWH
          In:  INTEGER KWL

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}void sof_cdb_free ( int kwh, int kwl );{/red}
          {red}void sof_cdb_free_ex ( int index, int kwh, int kwl );{/red}


The lock of kwh/kwl is released. (kwh/kwl = 0/0 will release all locks)


Attention: Keys locked explicitly with sof_cdb_lock will not be
           released via a 0/0 call, but only with the explicit kwh/kwl
           combination.


   {link}109{-link}sof_cdb_lock{/link}

!TOPIC 114 cdb_kenq

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDKENQ(KWH,KWL,Request){/red}
          {red}SUBROUTINE CDKENQX(Index,KWH,KWL,Request){/red}
          In/Out:  INTEGER KWH
          In/Out:  INTEGER KWL
          In:      INTEGER Request

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}void sof_cdb_kenq ( int *kwh, int *kwl, int Request );{/red}
          {red}void sof_cdb_kenq_ex ( int index, int *kwh, int *kwl, int Request );{/red}


You will get information about the key kwh/kwl. The Result is returned
in the same memory locations. Returns 0/0 if nothing available.

    Request = CD_ENQ_EXTREMA   (0) possible maximum values
              CD_ENQ_PREV     (-1) next lower key to kwh/kwl
              CD_ENQ_NEXT     (+1) next higher key to kwh/kwl
              CD_ENQ_MIN      (-2) lowest defined key kwl for given kwh
                                   if no key defined at all: kwl=0 only
              CD_ENQ_MAX      (+2) highest defined key kwl for given kwh
                                   if no key defined at all: kwl=0 only
              CD_ENQ_MIN2     (-3) lowest defined key kwl for given kwh
              CD_ENQ_MAX2     (+3) highest defined key kwl for given kwh

              CD_ENQ_DAD      (+9) Daddy for this key

              The following calls will also return empty keys, i.e.
              keys currently having no data due to a delete operation.

              CD_ENQ_PREVX    (-5) next lower key to kwh/kwl
              CD_ENQ_NEXTX    (+5) next higher key to kwh/kwl
              CD_ENQ_MINX     (-6) lowest defined key kwl for given kwh
              CD_ENQ_MAXX     (+6) highest defined key kwl for given kwh

  {link}113{-link}sof_cdb_del{/link}
  {link}112{-link}sof_cdb_kdef{/link}
  {link}115{-link}sof_cdb_kexist{/link}

!TOPIC 115 cdb_kexist

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDKEXIST(KWH,KWL,IE){/red}

!TOPIC 117 cdb_getb

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDGET (ICDB,KWH,KWL,Data,Lwlen,Pos,IE){/red}
          {red}SUBROUTINE CDGETL  (KWH,KWL,Data,Lwlen,Pos,IE){/red}
          In:      INTEGER ICDB
          In:      INTEGER KWH
          In:      INTEGER KWL
          Out:     INTEGER/REAL Data(*)
          In/OUT:  INTEGER Lwlen
          In:      INTEGER Pos
          Out:     INTEGER IE=Returnvalue

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}int sof_cdb_get ( int icdb, int kwh, int kwl,
                     void *Data, int *RecLen, int Pos);{/red}

          {red}int sof_cdb_getb ( int kwh, int kwl,
                     void *Data, int *RecLen, int Pos);{/red}

          see also {link}118{-link}sof_cdb_put{/link}
                   {link}116{-link}sof_cdb_kexist{/link}
                   {link}119{-link}sof_cdb_rewind{/link}
                   {link}199{-link}sof_cdb_pos{/link}


{red}The structure of each key may be changed without notice!{/red}

A record is read from the active database or the read pointer is
set to a specific position (seek).  Only keys with their directory
in memory will be found. To get access to the actual complete set
of keys call sof_cdb_flush before.

With the first reading a lock will be set to this key which is released
after reaching the end of the key.

  icdb            index of database
  kwh / kwl       key ( 0/0 is not allowed )
  Data            Starting address of the data
  RecLen          max. length for Data in Bytes
                  will be overwritten with the actual Length of the
                  item (may be shorter or longer)
                  = 0 setting only the pointer for the next read
  Lwlen           max. length for Data in IntegerWords (FORTRAN only)
                  = 0 setting only the pointer for the next read
  Pos             Position indicator
                  < 0 Position Pos Positions before current read
                      pointer ( -1 = the last record again).
                      if Reclen>0 the read pointer will be
                      restored to the current position
                  = 0 Position to first Item (REWIND)
                  > 0 Read next item from current read pointer
                      read pointer will advance by one item.
  Returnvalue     Errorcondition
                    CD_ERR_NONE       (0) no error
                    CD_ERR_TOOLONG    (1) Item is longer than Data
                    CD_ERR_DATAEND    (2) End of file reached
                    CD_ERR_NOTFOUND   (3) key does not exist

*  The Record is always transfered via a pointer to a structure or
   the first element of an array. The length of the structure has
   to be calculated by the size_off Operator in C or the function 
   MLEN(NI,NR) available within the CDBASE-Library. There are 
   also parameters available for FORTRAN 

*  END-OF-FILE or variable length of an item is easily handled. You
   may try a blocksize and reread the record with the exact amount
   of memory. Due to the automatic locking each read beyond EOF
   will check the data base for new records which may have been
   appended in the meantime.

!TOPIC 118 cdb_putb

                                                           {link}103{-link}-> Interface{/link}
{blue}FORTRAN:{/blue}  {red}SUBROUTINE CDPUT (ICDB,KWH,KWL,Data,Lwlen,Pos,IE){/red}
          {red}SUBROUTINE CDPUTL  (KWH,KWL,Data,Lwlen,Pos,IE){/red}
          In:      INTEGER ICDB
          In:      INTEGER KWH
          In:      INTEGER KWL
          In:      INTEGER/REAL Data(*)
          In:      INTEGER RecLen,Lwlen
          In:      INTEGER Pos
          Out:     INTEGER IE=Returnvalue

{blue}C:{/blue}        {red}int sof_cdb_put ( int icdb, int kwh, int kwl,
                     void *Data, int *RecLen, int Pos);{/red}

          {red}int sof_cdb_putb (int kwh, int kwl,
                    void *Data, int *RecLen, int Pos);{/red}

          see also {link}117{-link}sof_cdb_get{/link}
                   {link}119{-link}sof_cdb_rewind{/link}
                   {link}199{-link}sof_cdb_pos{/link}


{red}The structure of each key may be changed without notice!
We strongly discourage from writing directly to the database.
It is encouraged to use an input file instead.{/red}

An record of the indicated index will be written to the active database.
With the first writing access a write lock will be automatically set,
which is automatically released if the same process starts reading the
same index.

  icdb            index of database
  kwh / kwl       key ( 0/0 is not allowed )
  Data            Starting address of the data
  RecLen          Length of Data in Bytes
  Lwlen           Length for Data in IntegerWords (FORTRAN only)
  Pos             Position indicator
                  < 0 Rewrite Item Pos Positions before current read
                      pointer ( -1 = the last record again).
                  = 0 Write first Item (REWIND)
                      deleting all existing items
                      (will just delete the key if RecLen=0)
                  > 0 Write next item at the end of the key
  Returnvalue     Errorcondition
                    CD_ERR_NONE       (0) no error
                    CD_ERR_TOOLONG    (1) Item is longer than actual
                                          size (If Pos<0)
                    CD_ERR_DATAEND    (2) Position not within file
                    CD_ERR_NOTFOUND   (3) key does not exist

REWRITE IN PLACE: You may change the values of the item as long
as the length of the item is not increased. The reason for that is the
organisation as a fixed linked list, which keeps the data base well organized
and insures fast processing.

!TOPIC 121 Environment and additional Hints


{red}Environment variables{/red}                              {link}103{-link}-> CDBASE Interface{/link}

CDBASE uses some Variables of the SOFiSTiK-Environment.

    CDACCESS=MULTI      multitasking enabled (default)
    CDACCESS=SINGLE     multitasking disabled, no locks apply

    CDBASETEMP=...      Location of the scratch cdbase file



{red}Compatibility between different plattforms:{/red}

To account for the different worlds: Big endian (f.e. Sparc,  Motorola)
and little endian (Intel, Dec). CDBASE defines a special item in the
master record to detect the correct version and apply a byteswap
mechanism on the base of the length of the integer. CDBASE distinguishs
between a {red}raw{/red} format outside the process and a {red}native{/red} format of the
process. For a direct access to the database raw will be the format of
the file, while native is that of the process.


As the swap is done on a 4-Byte basis automatically, there will be no
further action needed, as long as the following conventions are followed:

All data is equaly 4-Bytes int (long Integer / floats). User characters
[str] are stored therefor by an arithmetic instruction in long integers:

            int icode = 65536 * character(2) + character(1)

where character is the unicode representation of the character. An array
with m int elements can hold 2*m-1 characters, cause we want to have a
zero entry at the end of the string. Thus most strings having an even
number of characters require on extra int element thus allowing an
additional character, not usable however.

If you do not follow these rules you may

 - Refuse to work with such files (Function CDSTAT)

 - Reswap the data with your own functions.


Before creating the database you have to specify the variable CDBASEVER in the SOFiSTiK.DEF file.

    CDBASEVER=5xx
    password protection now possible

    CDBASEVER=501
    maximum 256 GB, same space requirements as version 400
  default version, if not specified with environment variable CDBASEVER

    CDBASEVER=503
    maximum 1024 GB, Directory entries need more space.


;=====================================================================R

!TOPIC 122 SOFiSTiK Data

{red}SOFiSTiK-Data{/red}
                                                   {link}123{-link}-> SOFiSTiK Syntax{/link}
                                                   {link}125{-link}-> SOFiSTiK Units{/link}


SOFiSTiK database is organized with the following the main index key "kwh":


  CTRL : kwh:   0        {link}128{-link}Control data{/link}            Errortransfer:    {link}127{-link}Control data{/link}
  MATE : kwh:   1        {link}130{-link}Material{/link}
  BORE : kwh:   2        {link}140{-link}Soilprofiles{/link}            AXIS : kwh:   3   {link}141{-link}Geometric Axis{/link}
  TEND   kwh:   4        {link}201{-link}Prestressing Schemes{/link}    AREA : kwh:   5   {link}202{-link}Geometric Area{/link}
  CON  : kwh:   8        {link}142{-link}Steel connections{/link}
  SECT : kwh:   9        {link}143{-link}Cross sections{/link}
  SYST : kwh:  10        {link}148{-link}Controlinfo{/link}
         kwh:  11        {link}149{-link}Primary Groups{/link}
         kwh:  37        {link}204{-link}Secondary Groups{/link}
         kwh:  17        {link}222{-link}Total masses{/link}
  LC   : kwh:  12 to  14 {link}150{-link}Loadcaseinfo{/link}
         kwh:  15        {link}156{-link}Construction stages{/link}
         kwh:  16        {link}223{-link}Performance criteria{/link}
         kwh:  18        {link}157{-link}Viewing info{/link}
         kwh:  19        {link}213{-link}Balances of Flow{/link}
  NODE : kwh:  20 to  29 {link}158{-link}Nodes{/link}
  G??? : kwh:  30 to  39 {link}163{-link}Structural Elements{/link}
  TEND : kwh:  40 to  49 {link}206{-link}Tendons{/link}
         kwh:  50 to  59 {link}122{-link}reserved{/link}
         kwh:  60 to  69 {link}122{-link}reserved{/link}
         kwh:  70 to  79 {link}122{-link}reserved{/link}
  HIST   kwh:  80 to  89 {link}169{-link}Time History{/link}
  EIGE   kwh:  90 to  99 {link}170{-link}Eigenvalues{/link}
  BEAM : kwh: 100 to 119 {link}171{-link}Beamelements{/link}
  DSLN : kwh: 120 to 129 {link}171{-link}Design elements{/link}
  BSCT : kwh: 140 to 149 {link}171{-link}Sections{/link}
  TRUS : kwh: 150 to 159 {link}182{-link}Truss elements{/link}
  CABL : kwh: 160 to 169 {link}183{-link}Cable elements{/link}
  SPRI : kwh: 170 to 179 {link}184{-link}Springs, Dampers, Masses{/link}
  BOUN : kwh: 180 to 186 {link}185{-link}Boundary elements{/link}
  RSET : kwh: 187 to 189 {link}211{-link}Result Sets{/link}
  LINK : kwh: 190 to 199 {link}200{-link}Link elements{/link}
  QUAD : kwh: 200 to 299 {link}187{-link}QUAD elements{/link}
  BRIC : kwh: 300 to 399 {link}195{-link}BRIC elements{/link}
         kwh: 400 to 489 {link}199{-link}Substructures{/link}
  PIPE : kwh: 490 to 499 {link}186{-link}Pipe elements{/link}
         kwh: 900 to 999 {link}205{-link}Bridge Segments{/link}


For the last digit of kwh there exist the convention:
     k = 0     Topology (not dependant of load case)
     k = 1     Loading
     k = 2     Results
     k = 5     Design stresses
     k = 6     Reinforcements
     k = 9     Hydraulic / Temperature


For the second index key it is common to use a loadcase or a material
or cross section number. When using text always use chr to pack.

All Items for a key should have a similar structure. Each Item has the
general sequence: Integervalues, floatvalues, strings.
Character-Set is unicode resp. ANSI (8-Bit Unicode).
Strings are stored twofold.
General strings are packed two characters in one Word to allow for byte
swapping. Keywords or identifiers with a maximum of 4 Characters are
packed in a single word.
All described values are stringent in interpretation and their sequence,
however values may be omitted at the end and may be extended at any time
So each programmer should be aware of varying length of items and take
care of missing values.

Please be aware that data should always be written in ascending order of ids,
otherwise it can't be accessed with @key.

Header Records are defined as follows:


   The Sorting-Item (Elementnumber etc.) has to be zero.
   They preceed any other record of that type.
   The first record defines maximum values and absolute sums
   The second record if existent defines the minimum values, if the
   second record does not exist, then the first record contains
   positive absolut maximum values.


All Coordinate-systems follow the German DIN 1080. Differences to the US
conventions are mainly:

   Sign of Bending moments in beams
   Index of moments in plates and their signs

SCRATCH-Keys:

Use of keys in a scratch-database. As the scratch-Database is local to
any process, its use is relatively free. However as all modules use the
scratch-database from its caller, there might be conflicts. That's why
there are some basic rules as follows:

The mechanism to allow OK/CANCEL is to make a copy of any record in the
scratch area which is then either copied to the main database or
discarded (deleted). The same procedure is used by all batch programs
or calls redefining data. They make a copy of the content in the scratch
database discarding obsoleted data and reinstall the index from there.

Rule 1:
The data in the scratch of those keys should always match the original
data structure and content.

Rule 2:
A very special local scratch with KWL=0 may be used in rare cases, but
only within the scope of one routine and has to be deleted on exit.

Rule 3:
Local scratch keys which contains local or cooked values are not allowed
to share the same index. They have to use either negative values of KWH
or KWH=0 or KWH>999.

Rule 4:
All used scratch values within the dlls have to be described in this
document, all Keys 0/0/negative are reserved for the usage of the DLL.

;=====================================================================R

!TOPIC 123 Syntax

  {red}Syntax of this description{/red}
                                                  {link}122{-link}--> SOFiSTiK Data{/link}
                                                  {link}125{-link}--> SOFiSTiK Units{/link}

  The syntax of the following description of associated structures
  is as follows:

  lines starting with  ;  are comments or control commands
  lines starting with  !  are commands for the help-compiler

  All other lines are visible in the Help-System. From those lines
  some have more specific meanings. All those lines start with a
  specific text and may be continued with a \ in the last column
  if necessary. Those lines have a fixed sequence of string items
  which are separated by blancs. If one string item has different
  appearing in different languages it will be in the form

     generic|english

  1. Lines starting with @Rec: define the description of a
     particular record. Multiple @Rec: may be described together
     if no other lines are between the @Rec:.
     Lines starting with @RECM: are used for the name of the union and the KWH defines 
     Lines starting with @RECU: are somehow equivalent, but the 
     FORTRAN structure is a UNION (without SEQUENCE) which is
     extendable, but not suitable for EQUIVALENCE.

     The first string is:

         number/key[:selector1[:selector2[:selector3]]]

         number      is a numeric value defining the fist key
         key         is a numeric value defining the second key OR
                          ID  indicating a chr identifier or
                          IDL indicating a lexical bhr identifier or
                          NR indicating "any number" or
                          LC indicating "any loadcase" or
                          any other text
         selector1   is a string indicating the value of the first
                     item of the record to be matched as follows:
                          *      = any value
                          +      = any positive value
                          -      = any negative value
                          Z+     = any positive value or zero
                          Z-     = any negative value or zero
                          Z!     = any value but zero
                          chr    = packed text
                          nn     = numeric value including ? as wild
                                   (e.g. 10?01, 1??? , 1001)
         selector2   is a string indicating the value of the second
                     item of the record to be matched as above.
         selector3   is a string indicating the value of the third
                     item of the record to be matched as above.

     The rest is the mnemonic and the verbal description of the record

     Example:  @Rec: 009/NR:0 SECT | Sectional Values        :V200501 \
                                   | Querschnittswerte

     The generic description defines the name of the structure. Descriptions
     may be continued in consequent lines if a line encounters a backslash.

     At the end of the first line a string starting with :V indicates the
     version number of that entry to be incremented for any change in the
     structure or content of that item.

     Records defined with @Rec:: are only internal, they are not
     visible to the standard user.

  2. Lines starting with @Dad define the Daddy of a record

     Example:  @Dad: 12/LC

  3. Lines with "@" as the first non blanc character define an item
     of a record. The syntax is as follows:

     First string:  @number=   Identifier Integer Item
                    @number#   Standard Integer Item
                    @number:   Standard Float Item
                    @number+   Standard Item to be added when merging
                    @number~   Standard Item to be averaged when merging
                    number is the offset of the item as follows:
                    The first part of the structure is composed by int
                    values starting with an offset of 0. To select a
                    specific record (e.g. via @KEY in CADINP) the integer
                    values are used.
                    Then we have a second block of real values starting
                    generally with an offset of 1. However there is
                    sometimes the case that the first real value has
                    the offset of 0. (e.g. 102/LC). Elements of this
                    second block may be detected either by an offset
                    less equal than the last one or by the 'number:'
                    A special string may be appended for specialities
                    for header records:
                    @number!abs(nn)  The value is the absolute maximum
                                     of all values at relative offset nn
                    @number!max(nn)  The value is the positive maximum
                                     of all values at relative offset nn
                    @number!mix(nn)  There are two records with max/min
                                     of all values at relative offset nn
                    The offset is relative to the real offset including
                    the shifts described above and may be ommitted if 0

     Second string: ItemCharacter
                    Name of variable in structures, 4 leading characters
                    also to be used for selecting items within CADINP
                    The String "-" stands for internal, non printable
                    dummy items.
                    For arrays or structures we have the following
                    conventions:

                       arrays:
                         p(8)    p[8]    :  p         8[-]
                         or equivalent   :  p         [-,-,-,-,-,-,-,-]
                         T(3,4)  T[4][3] :  T         4[-,-,-]
                         arb(0:4,20)     :  arb(0)    20*[1081,1092,*,*,*]
                         arb(0:4,0:19)   :  arb(0,0)  20*[1081,1092,*,*,*]

                       arrays start with [0] for C and (1) for FORTRAN.
                       For FORTRAN however a start with 0 may be defined
                       via the values in paranthesis.

                       structure:
                                        lpt[p,x,y,z]  63[*,1001,1001,1001]

                    A combination is only allowed for the sequence:

                       name(0)[stru,stru2] 3*[-,-]

     Third string:  Multiplier[Representlist] of item
                    Multiplier     : integer number to repeat item
                                     or * to indicate infinite repeat
                                     omitted if equal 1.
                    Representatlist: [representation,representation..]
                    Representation : [int]   = integer value (1 word)
                                     [bhr]   = 4 Characters lexically packed
                                     [chr]   = 4 Characters packed
                                     [str*n] = Unicode-String max n chars
                                               (i.e. requires n/2+1 words)
                                     [-]     = float value (1 word) undimensioned
                                     [nn]    = float value with Dimension nn
                                     [*]     = float value with unknown
                                               or dependant Dimension
                                     [nnf],[*f] = explicit float value (32 Bit)
                                     [nnd],[*d] = explicit double value (64 Bit)
                                                  these options are reserved for
                                                  internal use!

      Rest:         TabIdent | english_description | deutscher_text  @textref

                    The TabIdent is the name to be used as headder in tables
                    If omitted it is identical to the ItemCharacter.

                    The next two parts are descriptions of the item
                    in english / german used only in the CDBASE.CHM

                    The last text starts with a @ and defines the unique
                    translatable designation based on 
                       the sofistik.err        with  @1nnn.
                       the sofistik_leg.err    with  @2nnn.
                       the result.err          with  @3nnn.
                    As the ident is always expected to be appended to the text, 
                    we do not need to repeat that information.

      Examples:

      ex:      @0=  NR         [int]   Number |Nodenumber                 @1301
      ex:      @1:  ux        [1003]   u-X    |Deformation |Verschiebung  @1362
      ex:      @2:  uy        [1003]   u-Y    |Deformation v-y \
                                              |Verschiebung v-y           @1362
      ex:      @3:  uz        [1003]   u-Z    |Deformation v-z \
                                              |Verschiebung v-z           @1362
      ex:      @4+  Px        [1151]   P-X    |Force PXX |Kraft PXX       @1362
      ex:      @5+  Py        [1151]   P-Y    |Force PYY |Kraft PYY       @1362
      ex:      @6+  Pz        [1051]   P-Z    |Force PZZ |Kraft PZZ       @1362


  3. Lines with "#" as the first non blanc character define a specific
     meaning of a value of an item:

     First string:  #number
                    number is the value of the item
                    +      holds for all positive values
                    -      holds for all negative values

      Rest string:  Description of the meaning to be used in dialogs
                    or long variable names (spaces convert to underline)

      Example:      #1       |Displacements |Verschiebungen
      Example:      #0       |Maximum values |Maximalwerte

      For the generation of the headder files it is also possible to
      write:        #define name_of_parameter  value  description

      Example:      #define SYST_ROST  3  |girder |Trägerrost/Platte


  4. Lines with "&" or "%" as the first non blanc character define a
     specific meaning of a bit pattern or a decimal encoding of an item:

     First string:

        &number    number is value of the binary bits to be tested
        %number    number is value of the decimal digits to be tested
                   (? are wildcard digits)


     Rest string:  Description of the meaning to be used in dialogs

     Example:      &1       Bit 1   has meaning
     Example:      &3       Bit 1+2 together have meaning
     Example:      &2?      The decimal digit 2 at the second from
                            left has this meaning

  5. There is also the possibility to specify to which headder file the compiled
     structures should be written (including extra data written directly)
     a comment of the following form will switch to a different output stream:
     for FORTRAN      ; * F-INCLUDE cdbtypegeo.f90
     for C            ; * C-INCLUDE cdbtypegeo.h
     
     These headder files include not only the structures, but also those #define
     specified in this description. All these are attached to the structure 
     defined before. As a special rule, all #defines between the above switch
     and the next record definition will be directly copied to the headder.
     After an internal record Rec::, defines will be ignored.

  6. Lines starting with "; @RecDesc:" define the description of a record or recordgroup
     please note the ";" at line start!
     number/key like in @Rec
     
     Example:  ; @RecDesc: 12/LC  Load cases


The contents of this description are also available for those programs
(cdbserver, cadinp) needing more detailed information than the structure
itself in a special database "CDBASE.CDB". The items within that CDB are
created by a compiler from the cdbase.txt and can be only found in
cdbase.cdb.
In that special database the structure of each record type is saved with
the same key-combination KWH/KWL as for the real database. If KWL may be
of any number (eg. LC or NR). The structure is defined in KWH/-999.
A summary and the description to this data will be in -999/-999 in cdbase.cdb.

More specific structures are generated from this description automatically.

; * C-INCLUDE cdbtypesys.h
The header-files created from this description are controlled by the
following comments containing control infos:

   1.   ; * F-INCLUDE name.f90
   2.   ; * C-INCLUDE name.h

Items 1/2 select the given filename to receive the type-definitions.
An Item 1/2 without a name will stop the automatic creation of structures.
Every include file may be activated several times.

For special cases where we want to specify an explicit or additional
info to the include files we have the lines

   3.   ; & F-INCLUDE info for include file not visible in help
   4.   ; & C-INCLUDE info for header file not visible in help
   5.   ; + F-INCLUDE
   6.   ; + C-INCLUDE
   7.   ; - F-INCLUDE
   8.   ; - C-INCLUDE
   9.   ; ( F-INCLUDE name of the file

Items 3/4 copy the rest of the line as is to the file.
The types 5/6 will copy all following lines up to the next line of type 7/8.
Item 9 will generate the KWH parameter for the fortran file.
do this right before closing the module of this file

!TOPIC 125 Explicit Units

{red}Explicit Units:{/red}
                                                  {link}126{-link}--> Implicit Units{/link}
                                                  {link}122{-link}--> SOFiSTiK Data{/link}
                                                  {link}123{-link}--> SOFiSTiK Syntax{/link}


Every software has to work in a consistent set of units. There are
several choices possible:

   kg, m, sec, W    - a classical system with a small drawback of
                      having very large stresses

So there are variants, exchanging the m to mm. We have selected a
system, where all Units in the database should be solely:

      {red}t, m, sec, radian, kN as well as kW and degree Kelvin!{/red}

Only those units which should be interpretated as a description (like
the concrete Class "C 20" are kept within their original units.

However, there is one tricky exception:
Although weights are depending on the location: force = mass * gravity
they are defined in kN/m3 or lb/ft3 as forces in the design codes.
So these values are saved as nominal weights 10 times the mass in metric tons:

    78.5 [kN/m3]  = 490 [lb/ft3] => 78.5 in database

So we have a few special units 79,158,159,258,259,280 (marked with a G)
which include a conversion with a simplified metric gravity constant of 10.0
for kN or a true official constant of 9.80665 [m/sec2]:

    1091 = [79=kN/m3],[159=kg/m3],[259=lb/ft3]
    1188 = [158=kg/m],[258=lb/ft]     
    1189 = [159=kg/m3],[259=lb/ft3]   deprecated!

So we have three conversions and a general rule:

   -  to get the density, always divide the database weight values by 10.0
   -  there are also explicit masses which have been converted to tons
   -  to get precise loadings multiply the mass value with 
      9.80665 or the true local gravity (see 10/1) 
   -  to work as an engineer, use the preset defined weight data as it is

As we had taken Watt for thermal problems, be carefull to apply a
factor of 1000. when converting mechanical power to heat-power.
DOLFYN is working in the kg,m,sec System. We have to convert
power, weights and loadings from the data base. (marked with X)

Input and output of values in specific Units are performed with
special functions and numbers indicating the type of the data as
follows. In general it is strongly advised to use only {link}126{-link}Implicit Units{/link}.

!TOPIC 126 Implicit Units

{red}Implicit Units:{/red}
                                                  {link}125{-link}--> Explicit Units{/link}
                                                  {link}122{-link}--> SOFiSTiK Data{/link}
                                                  {link}123{-link}--> SOFiSTiK Syntax{/link}


Based on the explicit units we define implicit units (>1000) behaving
different in different environments. This is the factor and the
precission of the format.

The environments are:

                                        Geometry   Sections   Forces
     0  = Default Model                  [m]        [m]       [kN]
     1  = German General Engineering     [m]        [cm]      [kN]
     2  = German Structural Steelwork    [m]        [mm]      [kN]
          --------------------------------------------------------
     3  = Bridges                        [m]        [m]       [MN]
     4  = Soilmechanics                  [m]        [m]       [kN]
     5  = Structural Engineering         [m]        [mm]      [kN]
     6  = Mechanical Engineering         [mm]       [mm]      [kN]
     7  = Tiny structures                [mm]       [mm]      [N]
     8  = imperial US Units Bridges      [ft]       [in]      [kip]
     9  = imperial US Units Buildings    [in]       [in]      [kip]

    Notation:
    The standard notation to be used in all printouts and input is also
    given in the following table. Local coordinates are addresses via
    lower case characters, global coordinates with capital characters.
    Where the case is not significant, double characters should be used
    instead.
    e.g.           P-X  or PXX  for global forces
                   P-x  or PX   for local forces

    Further indices to be used

               -n -t    for normalized/normal and transvers
               -a -l    for axial and lateral
                  -t    for torsion
                  -c    for characteristic
                  -d    for design

    For better readability the printout should use a - to separate main
    Designation from the index. However this is not mandatory, so we
    have:

    Beam-forces:     My, Mz, Mt, Vy, Vz, N, Mb, Mt2
    Shell-forces     m-xx, m-yy, m-xy, v-x, v-y, n-xx, n-yy, n-xy
    displacements:   u, u-t, u-X (global), u-x (local)
    rotations:       phi, phi-X, u-xx, urx
    stresses:        sig-x, sig-y, sig-z, sig-I, tau-xy, tau-xz, tau-yz

    If space is restricted or for input literals the - may be omitted.
    For CADINP we have no case and a historical limit of 4 characters.
    Variable names do not allow for any special characters like -

    So there will be at least two names for the same item for a very
    long time. It is the courtesy of every CADINP-program to allow the
    specification of both versions.

    As CADINP Input should be somehow unique with its definitions, the SI
    Units 0 to 6 prefer to have the same defaults. The current list has a
     (*)  for those items where only set 6 (pure SI) deviates.
      *   for those items not having the same units for sets 0 to 5
     (!)  is specified for those, where variants are agreed on and special
          checks have been implemented for the correct usage.

 ============================================================================

     3                       Angle in radian                     (rad)
     4                       Angle in milli-radian               (mrad)
     5     205               Angle in degree                     (°)
     8                       percent                             (o/o),(%)
     9                       permille                            (o/oo)

                                      IBVERS = Version number (internal)
                                               to be changed if format
                                               of file has been altered.
                                               + 256*(Control PLABA 0-15)
     @1#  NEQ      [int]    | Number of unknowns | Anzahl Gleichungen
     @2#  NVBTYP   [int]    | Solver control     | Kontrollwert Solver
                              100*Number of blocks + IVBTYP
                              IVBTYP = Type of solver
                                         0 = direct skyline solver
                                         1 = iterative sparse solver
                                         2 = direct sparse solver
                                         9 = block solver
     @3#  NWA      [int]    | Block Size (words) | Blockgrösse (Worte)
                              size of system or stiffness matrix
     @4#  MBAND    [int]    | maximum bandwidth  | Bandweite
                              or size of preconditioning matrix
     @5#  NWG      [int]    | geom. matrix size  | Blockgr. Geometr. Steifigkeit
     @6#  NWB      [int]    | mass matrix size   | Blockgr. Massenmatrix
     @7#  NWC      [int]    | damping matrix size| Blockgr. Daempfungsmatrix
     @8#  sp_typ_0 [int]    | type of matrix 0   | Typ der 0. Matrix (system)
     @9#  sp_typ_1 [int]    | type of matrix 1   | Typ der 1. Matrix (stiffness)
    @10#  sp_typ_2 [int]    | type of matrix 2   | Typ der 2. Matrix (geometric)
    @11#  sp_typ_3 [int]    | type of matrix 3   | Typ der 3. Matrix (mass)
    @12#  sp_typ_4 [int]    | type of matrix 4   | Typ der 4. Matrix (damping)
    @13#  ctrl_tri [int]    | solver control vals| Solver-Kontrollwerte
    @14#  ctrl_red [int]    | solver control vals| Solver-Kontrollwerte
    @15#  ctrl_eig [int]    | solver control vals| Solver-Kontrollwerte
                              for block solver:  0 = not existent
                                                 1 = assembled
                                                 2 = factorized
                              for sparse solver: typ of sparse-structure
                                                 0 = diagonal
                                                 1 = sparse etc.

     second record for block solver:

          MBL(NBLOCK)    *[int]    Last equation for each block

     following:

          MAXB(NEQB+1)   *[int]    Skyline of blocks (NBLOCK Records)

     following:

          R(NEQ)         *[-]      Last displacement vector for
                                   nonlinear analysis

All these values are mirrored in the $D1 resp. $C1 files within the first
16 Words (64 Bytes) to allow to check the validity of an external file.
The first 6 values (0:5) will be checked against at startup. If system
is not yet fully solved a negative value of IPTYP will indicate this.
To enforce a new equation system to be solved either the CDBASE Control
Record or the $D1-Header may be set to unreasonable values.

    To be functional, these PDFs need so called "Named-Destinations" for every record name.

    1.  Buy the plugin "name it" from www.merlin-os.co.uk for an acrobat full version.

        b) edit the csv-file (delete all but the recordnames, change these to become the record name only)
        c) import the csv file.

;    @RecDesc:   0/100  Global CADINP Variable
{red}
     @Rec: 000/100           CTRL_VAR | Global_CADINP_Variable                  :V201310
{/red}
     @0#  NAME     4[chr]    |name of variable  |Namen der Variablen
     @4#  IND      [int]     |index for arrays  |Index für arrays
     @5#  VAL      [-]       |value of variable |Wert der Variablen
     @6#  SCOPE    [int]     |name of scope     |Name eines Bereichs
                              scope is used to structure the variables
                              for the GUI, the name of the scope is
                              saved in a special record with NAME==0
                              - public scopes are from 0 to 1000000
                              - scope 999999 is used to save function
                                definitions, but such a definition is
                                possible for all scopes
                              - scope 1000000 is used for literals
                              - scope 9000000 is used for sections
                              - scope ID of a 3/ID is used for an axis
     @7#  DIM      [int]     |unit of variable  |Einheit der Variablen
     @8#  TXT      [str*32]  |Comment on variable | Kommentar zur Variable

     access to those variable should be done only with the functions of
     CADARI (for more details see there)

     If the unit DIM is zero, the variable has to be specified in the 
     expected units of the intended purpose, i.e. [mm] for sectional
     coordinates or [cm2] for reinforcement areas.
     If the unit DIM is >0 the value of the variable has been converted
     to the data base units, and any input or output should convert
     accordingly.

     Remark: Old definitions have been with a length of 24 :
          NAME     4[chr]    |name of variable  |Namen der Variablen
          IND      [int]     |index for arrays  |Index für arrays
          VAL      [-]       |value of variable |Wert der Variablen
          SCOPE    [int]     |name of scope     |Name eines Bereichs
          TXT      [str*32]  |Comment on variable | Kommentar zur Variable
     Remark: Very old definitions have been with a length of 4 :
          NAME     2[chr]    |name of variable  |Namen der Variablen
          IND      [int]     |index for arrays  |Index für arrays
          VAL      [-]       |value of variable |Wert der Variablen

                           Special Hint:
                           During the time of the introduction of a new design code, it may
                           happen that there are two versions of the same material available.
                           This will be flagged by some additional chars to the class value. 
                           Internal in the aqu_mat outines the material types of the old
                           fashioned classes will become negative to allow a proper selection 
                           within the dialogues.
                           If the material from an existing database can not be found in the 
                           tables, a second try with the negative type might find it.

                           Bit pattern of used design codes (based on material types):
                           #define CODE_TYPE_CONCRETE          4  =  B2  = concrete                          (e.g. EN 1992)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_STEEL             8  =  B3  = structural steel                  (e.g. EN 1993)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_COMPOSITE        16  =  B4  = composite steel/concrete material (e.g. EN 1994)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_TIMBER           32  =  B5  = timber                            (e.g. EN 1995)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_BRICKWORK        64  =  B6  = brickwork                         (e.g. EN 1996)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_SOIL            128  =  B7  = soil material                     (e.g. EN 1997)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_SEISMIC         256  =  B8  = seismic / earthquake              (e.g. EN 1998) not for materials
                           #define CODE_TYPE_ALUMINIUM       512  =  B9  = aluminium                         (e.g. EN 1999)
                           #define CODE_TYPE_ALLMAT          764         = all code types based on materials

                           Additional bit pattern of material types (without corresponding to a design code):
                           #define MAT_TYPE_GENERIC            1  =  B0  = generic material
                           #define MAT_TYPE_LAYER              2  =  B1  = layered material
                           #define MAT_TYPE_REINFORCEMENT   1024  =  B10 = reinforcement steel
                           #define MAT_TYPE_PRESTRESSING    2048  =  B11 = prestressing steel

     @2#  Class    [int]    | Classification   | Güteklasse
                              <0  class in roman numbers or characters
                                  = ansi-value of first char
                                  + 256*ansi-value of 2nd char
                                  + 65536*ansi-value of 3rd char
                                  + 65536*256*ansi-value of 4th char
                                    ansi values < 32 are roman numbers!
                              >0  class in arabian numbers +
                                  appended chars or national variants
                                  +65536*ansi-value of first char
                                  +65536*256*ansi-value of second char
                                   first char < 32 is used for EC and
                                   national variants by country codes!
                                   (confer Record {link}148{-link}10/1{/link})

                              f.e. BST 500 SA =>
                                        type  = 2010
                                        class = (65*256+83)*65536+500
                                   S 500 (EC2-49) =>
                                        type  = 2000
                                        class = (1)*65536+500

    Remark:
    The standard work law for steel has up to 5 vertices:
        strain    stress
        0.0         0.0
        fe/Es       fe
        epse        fy          or fe/Es-epse (if epse<0)
        eps         ft
        1.0         ft          for fully plastic analysis

     @Rec: 001/NR:3  MAT_ULTI | StressStrainLaw (Ultimate Limit state)          :V200501 \
                              | Arbeitslinie einer Materialdefinition Bruch
     @Rec: 001/NR:4  MAT_NONL | StressStrainLaw (Nonlinear Mean Values)         :V200501 \
                              | mittlere Arbeitslinie für nichtlineare Rechnung
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |Identification     | Kennziffer
     @1#  Temp     [int]    |Temperature        | Temperatur
     @2#  Type     [int]    |Type of law        | Art des Gesetzes
                               #define WLAW_TYP_USER                              0 = user defined
                               >0 = standard curve (default is established in SOF_AQMAT_WLAW
                                    the following values are mostly informative
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_LINEAR                           1 =   linear
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_BILINEAR                         2 =   bilinear
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TRILINEAR                        3 =   trilinear
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_IDEAL_PLASTIC                    4 =   ideal plastic (reserved)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_LINEAR_CONCRETE                 10 = S linear concrete (selectable)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_BILINEAR_CONCRETE               11 =   bilinear concrete
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_PARABOLA_RECTANGULAR            12 = S parabola rectangular (C)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_PARABOLA_3RD_ORDER              13 =   general parabola 3rd order
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_DEFORMATION_A_WITH_DECAY        14 = S deformation type (A) with decay
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_DEFORMATION_B_WITHOUT_DECAY     15 = S deformation type (B) without decay
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_MEAN_DESIGN_VALUES_R            16 =   mean design values type R (e.g. for lightweight concrete)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_MEAN_DESIGN_VALUES_RS           17 =   mean design values type RS (e.g. for lightweight concrete)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_HIGH_TEMP_CONCRETE_LIN_DECAY    18 =   high temperature concrete with linear decay
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_HIGH_TEMP_CONCRETE_NONL_DECAY   19 =   high temperature concrete with nonlinear decay
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_PURE_ELASTIC_PLASTIC            20 =   pure elastic/plastic (reserved)
                                    for reinforcing steel only:
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TENSION_STIFFENING_I            21 = S Tension Stiffening type I
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TENSION_STIFFENING_II           22 = S Tension Stiffening type II
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TENSION_STIFFENING_I_SHORT      23 = S Tension Stiffening type I  for short time loadings
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TENSION_STIFFENING_II_SHORT     24 = S Tension Stiffening type II for short time loadings
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TENSION_STIFFENING_I_FCTM       25 =   Tension Stiffening type I with cracking at 0.7 fctm
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_TENSION_STIFFENING_I_SHORT_FCTM 26 =   Tension Stiffening type I  for short time loadings with cracking at 0.7 fctm
                                                                           27,28,29 = reserved for tension stiffening
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_HIGH_TEMPERATURE_STEEL          30 =   high temperature steel
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_STAINLESS_STEEL                 31 =   stainless steel (reserved)

                               #define WLAW_TYPE_MAX                            127 =   Maximum number of possible types

                               #define WLAW_TYPE_APPLY_TENSILE_FOR_CONCRETE     128 = + Apply tensile stress strain law for concrete
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_LINEAR_PERTURBATION              0 =   law should be continued outside defined values (linear perturbation)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_CONTINUED_OUTSIDE              256 = + law should be continued outside defined values (constant)
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_VALID_WITHIN_STRAIN            512 = + law only valid within defined strain values
                               #define WLAW_TYPE_SHARP_BENDS                   1024 = + 1024*bitpattern of sharp bends (1-20)
                                                                                        (first and last point always set)
                                                                                        1024*2^0 = 1024      = first
                                                                                        1024*2^1 = 2048      = second
                                                                                        1024*2^2 = 4096      = third
                                                                                        ...
                                                                                        1024*2^19= 536870912 = 20th

     @0:  scm      [-]      Safety       |Safety factor
     @1:  epst     [1081]   TempStrain   |Elongation at TEMP if TEMP>0
                   [1081]   CreepStrain  |simplified creep strain if TEMP = 0
                   [8]      muet         |Reinforcement ratio As/Aceff for tension stiffening
     @2:  epss     [1081]   TempShift    |Shift of strains TEMP>0 (-TempStrain)
                   [-]      ECM0         |Tangent Stiffness Concrete   for tension stiffening
     @3:  fctm     [-]      FCTM         |Tensile Strength  Concrete   for tension stiffening
     @4:  arb(0) 20*[1081,1092,1090,-,-] |Function values    | Funktionswerte

                   up to 20 Blocks with 5 float-values containing:

                      EPS    [1081]   |Strain             | Dehnung
                      SIG    [1092]   |Stress             | Spannung
                      E      [1090]   |Stiffness          | Steifigkeit
                      E'     [-]      |Stiffness          | Steifigkeit
                      E''    [-]      |Stiffness          | Steifigkeit

                             For a strain less than EPS holds:
                               sig = SIG+EPS*E+EPS**2*E'+EPS**3*E''

                             Hint: Values @0 to @3 are optional, i.e.
                                   Older versions do not have those
                                   values, thus the number of vertices
                                   is  n = INT(len/5)
                                   starting at position x = len-5*n

     Important Hint:
     As there are stress strain laws applying a safety factor on the
     total stress, there are also especially for reinforcement types
     applying the factor only on the maximum stress.
     The method chosen so far has been to scale the stress strain law
     to have a unique factor (which is hard to understand)
     We now supply the posssibility to have those curves with the
     safety factor already build in, with a negative SCM value.
     This has to be checked in the design routines and should be dealt
     there appropriately.

{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]                  |Identification      |Kennziffer

     @2#  IBT      [int]    Mechanism     |Type of bedding mechanism
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_UNSP  0  unspecific
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_2DSS  1  plain stress condition
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_2DSN  2  plain strain condition
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_HSPC  3  3D halfspace condition
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_CIRH  4  circular hole
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_SPHC  5  spherical cavity
                                              #define MAT_BED_IBT_RIGD  6  rigid frictional interface
     @1:  C        [1097]   Bedding         |Bedding Coefficient             |Bettungszahl
     @2:  CT       [1097]   TangBedding     |Tangential Bedding              |tangent. Bettung
     @3:  RISS     [1092]   Rupture         |rupture stress                  |Riss-Spannung
     @4:  FLIE     [1092]   Yield           |yield   stress                  |Fliess-Spannung
     @5:  MUE      [-]      Friction        |friction coefficient            |Reibbeiwert
     @6:  KOH      [1092]   Cohesion        |cohesion                        |Kohäsion
     @7:  DIL      [-]      Dilatancy       |dilatancy coefficient           |Dilatanzbeiwert
     @8:  GAM      [1184]   Mass            |mass of bedding                 |Bodenmasse
     @9:  H        [1001]   RefLength       |reference length                |Bezugslänge
     @10: Rfac     [-]      StrengthRedFact |shear strength reduction factor |Abminderungsfaktor für (Schub-)Festigkeit

                            The normal stress is given by
                              sig = C*(u-normal+DIL*u-cross)
                              sig < FLIE ; sig > -FLIE
                              sig = 0   if sig > RISS
                            the shear stress is limited to
                              tau < MUE * sig + KOH

{/red}

                                           #define MAT_HYD_FOUR                  4  Fourier isotrop
                                           #define MAT_HYD_AFOUR                 5  Fourier anisotrop (obsolete)
                                           #define MAT_HYD_EC4S                  6  EC4 Steel         (obsolete)
                                           #define MAT_HYD_EC4C                  7  EC4 Concrete      (obsolete)
                                           #define MAT_HYD_HYDR_VOLU_STRESS      8  Volumetric Stress dependant multiplier ( Hydraulic )
                                           #define MAT_HYD_HYDR_NORMAL_STRESS    9  Normal Stress dependant multiplier     ( Hydraulic )
                                           #define MAT_HYD_HYDR_TANGENT_STRESS  10  Tangent Stress dependant multiplier    ( Hydraulic )
                                           #define MAT_HYD_TEMP_VOLU_STRESS     12  Volumetric Stress dependant multiplier ( Temperature, obsolete )
                                           #define MAT_HYD_TEMP_NORMAL_STRESS   13  Normal Stress dependant multiplier     ( Temperature, obsolete )
                                           #define MAT_HYD_TEMP_TANGENT_STRESS  14  Tangent Stress dependant multiplier    ( Temperature, obsolete )
                                           #define MAT_HYD_JONA                 16  Hydratation Jonasson
                                           #define MAT_HYD_HSCM                 17  Hydratation Shrinkage Core
                                           #define MAT_HYD_WESC                 18  Hydratation Wesche

     @1:  D        [*]      Parameter     |special Parameter |besonderer Parameter
                                            - Fractile to select generated values
                                              0 = lower values, 1 = higher values
                                            - thickness [1001] for nodal materials NR=0
                                            - maximum heat production for MAT_HYD_JONA...MAT_HYD_WESC (#16-#18)
     @2:  C        [*]      Capacity      |Storage Capacity  |Speicherkoeffizient
                                            - reference temperature [°] for MAT_HYD_JONA...MAT_HYD_WESC (#16-#18)
     @3:  N        [*]      Porosity      |Porosity/humidity |Porosität/Feuchtigkeit
                                            - porosity n [8] for MAT_HYD_ADARC...MAT_HYD_MISS   (#1-#3)
                                            - humidity n [8] for MAT_HYD_FOUR...MAT_HYD_EC4C    (#4-#7)
                                            - reference time tk [92] for MAT_HYD_JONA...MAT_HYD_WESC (#16-#18)
     @4:  K       6[*]      Conductivity  |Conductivity      |Leitfähigkeit
                                           for isotrope material:
                                               Kxx = Kyy = Kzz = K(1)
                                           for unisotrope material:
                                               Kxx = K(1) ; Kyy = K(2) ; Kzz = K(3)
                                               Kxy = K(4) ; Kxz = K(5) ; Kyz = K(6)
                                           for Forchheimer:
                                               a   = K(1) ; b   = K(2)
                                           for Missbach:
                                               c   = K(1) ; m   = K(2)
                                           for Jonasson:
                                               Qmax= D    ; tk  = N    ; Tref = C
                                               a   = K(1) ; b   = K(2)
                                           for Shrinkage Core:
                                               Qmax= D    ; tk  = N    ; Tref = C
                                               a   = K(1)
                                           for Wesche:
                                               Qmax= D    ; tk  = N    ; Tref = C
                                               a   = K(1) ; b   = K(2) ; c   = K(3)
     @10: KLOC    6[*]      Conductivity  |Conductivity      |Leitfähigkeit
                            in the anisotropic directions original directions

     Important Hint:
     Thermal-Data created from version before 2014 uses a kg-m-sec system (i.e. Watt)
     while from 2014 on a consistend unit set is used in kW. Old Data has a length of
     10 or 17 reals, the interpolation fraction is saved at position @10 instead of @1.
     

     There are items for elements (NR>0) as well as for the nodes (NR=0 / ISP(2)>0) 
     For the latter there are as many items as nodes!

     The materials are in independant classes defined by

           MAT_HYD_ADARC           ...MAT_HYD_MISS                (#1-#3)   Hydraulic Constants
           MAT_HYD_FOUR            ...MAT_HYD_EC4C                (#4-#7)   Thermal constants
           MAT_HYD_HYDR_VOLU_STRESS...MAT_HYD_TEMP_TANGENT_STRESS (#8-#14)  Stress dependant features

     Materials of different classes may coexist.

     The stress multipliers of type #8 are defined for all items,
     while #9 and #10 use the directions of principal stresses and
     thus have only C,N and KXX defined.

     Supplier for special data to be specified with MEXT.   

     Some data (TYPE>100) in this record is managed in exposition classes (subtypes)
     which are addressable by individual polygon edges.

     Other program assign a certain condition to all edges with that exp-reference
     without any need to refere to that data. But it is recommended to apply the
     default values given here.

     There may be default values defined in the INI-files. There we have:
     [Exposition]
     EXP1=cnom:2.5,crw:0.30,.... entries in any order
     EXP2=cnom:3.5,crw:0.20,.... entries in any order

                              #0 = constant

     Each Record specifies the material values which are valid below/after
     the given S-ordinate on the axis:
     - the first record (ILAY=0) defines the start of materials (surface).
     - optional intermediate layers (ILAY=1) are marked by a sequence of records with monotonic increasing S
     - a terminating record (ILAY=2) is obligatory and marks the end of the profile.

{red}
     @Rec: 002/NR:1002   BORE_BLA | BoreProfileTransverse                       :V200501 \
                                  | Querbettung
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier 1002
     @1:  Z1       [-]      |parameter s on start | Parameter s Anfang
     @2:  Z2       [-]      |parameter s on end   | Parameter s Ende
     @3:  K0       [1096]   |constant bedding     | Konstante Bettung
     @4:  K1       [1096]   |parabolic bedding    | Parabel Bettung
     @5:  K2       [1096]   |linear bedding       | lineare Bettung
     @6:  K3       [1096]   |quadratic bedding    | quadratische Bettung
     @7:  F0       [-]      |peripher Distribution| Umfangsverteilung
     @8:  F1       [-]
     @9:  F2       [-]
     @10: PM1      [1153]   |maximum value on upper ordinate \
                            | Maximalwert obere Ordinate
     @11: PM2      [1153]   |maximum value on lower ordinate \
                            | Maximalwert untere Ordinate
     @12: P0       [-]      |peripher Distribution| Umfangsverteilung II
     @13: P1       [-]
     @14: P2       [-]
     @15: P3       [-]

     Bedding at S1 equals to K0
     Bedding at S2 equals to K0+K1+K2+K3

     Peripher distribution is either

             F0 + F1 * cos(phi) + F2 * cos(2phi)

     or (if P0-P3 is defined)

             p=phi/90
             P0*(1-p)+P1*(p)      0 < phi < 90
             P1*(2-p)+P2*(p-1)   90 < phi < 180
             P2*(3-p)+P3*(p-2)  180 < phi < 270
             P3*(4-p)+P0*(p-3)  270 < phi < 360

     The lateral pressure is given by

             sig = KQ*sigz + K-lat*(u-lat+TAND*u-axial)

     the frictional axial stress is limited to

             tau = K-axial*u-axial < TAND * sig + C0
