;    @RecDesc:   3/ID  Geometric Axis
{red}
     @Rec: 03/ID:0   AXIS   | Geometric Axis                                    :V201509 \
                            | Geometrische Achsen
{/red}

     @0#  ID0      [int]    |identifier 0
     @1#  ID1      [int]    |subtype of axis
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_NONE  0 = no specific type
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_AXIS  1 = structural axis (e.g. A--A)
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_LANE 10 = central lane of (bridge) alignment axis
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_BGEO 11 = secondary lane of (bridge) alignment axis
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_TEND 12 = tendon geometry
                                     ID2 must be set accordingly
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_POST 15 = cut line for postprocessing
                             #define AXIS_SUBTYPE_AUXI 19 = auxiliary geometry (e.g used internally or for geometric constructions)

     @2#  ID2      [int]    | AXIS_SUBTYPE_POST: group number of cut-line
                              For Tendons (ID1 == AXIS_SUBTYPE_TEND):
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_SPLUS_REF          1 =  Reference geometry from SOFiPLUS
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_SUPP_LINES         2 =  Supporting lines       (top points)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_FOREIGN_REFAXIS    3 =  Foreign reference axis (not generated by tendon.exe)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_FOREIGN_DUCT       4 =  Foreign duct curve     (not generated by tendon.exe)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_FOREIGN_TEND       5 =  Foreign tendon curve   (not generated by tendon.exe)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_TND_GEOX           6 =  Exported curve         (tendon.exe -> GEOX)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_NATIVE_REFAXIS     7 =  Native reference axis  (tendon.exe generated)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_NATIVE_DUCT        8 =  Native duct curve      (tendon.exe generated)
                                 #define AXIS_TEND_TYPE_NATIVE_TEND        9 =  Native tendon curve    (tendon.exe generated)

     @3#  ID3      [int]    | AXIS_SUBTYPE_POST: >0 = explicit material to cut , <=0 = all materials
     @4#  ID4      [int]    | reserved
     @5#  ID5      [int]    | reserved

     @1:  TEXT     [str*32] |Designation of Line        |Bezeichnung Linie

     Describes a geometric curve in space with additional properties like
     placements, secondary axes and variables. Geometric axes are independant
     from any topological structure (structural points (30/NR), structural lines(31/NR)).
     User-defined axes are denominated by a 4 byte encoded character [chr] at 3/ID.
     Internal, automatically defined axes are identified by an integer in the
     range of ID = [1000000,9999999]. These internal axes cannot be accessed or
     modified directly by the user.

     User-defined axes will usually not be deleted when a a new structural
     system is initialized. Internal axes will always be deleted in this case.
     
     For legacy reasons, there are also some reserved names ending with a lower
     case letter:
                  AAAt to ZZZt  TENDON internal

{red}
     @Rec: 03/ID:- AXIS_REF | Reference to another Geometry  
{/red}
     @0#  IGM      [int]    |negative value of the master geometry 03/abs(IGM)
     @1#  IGS      [int]    |optional identifier of a secondary axis
     @2:  SMIN     [-]      |min parameter on referenced axis
     @3:  SMAX     [-]      |max parameter on referenced axis

     Every 03/ID may inherit its geometric properties from another 3/ID.
     Every 31/NR may inherit its geometric properties from 3/ID.


{red}
     @Rec: 03/ID:??  AXIS_GEO |Geometric properties                             :V200801
{/red}
     @0#  ILN      [int]    |Code of geometry     |Geometrieschlüssel
                            #define GAX_GEO_DEFAULT    1 = arc or linear in 3D
                                                           GPG = radius
                            #define GAX_GEO_PROJECT    2 = Alignement plan + elevation
                                                           GPG = Klothoid-Parameter
                                                                 0 = circular arc
                                                           GPA = radius elevation
                            #define GAX_GEO_SPLINE     3 = cubic spline
                            #define GAX_GEO_EXSPLI     4 = exponent. spline
                                                           GPG = coefficient
                            #define GAX_GEO_BEZIER     5 = Bezier curve
                                                           GPG = order of Splines
                                                           GPA = true arc length at start
                            #define GAX_GEO_NURBS      6 = Nurbs curve dim=3
                                                           GPG = order of Splines
                                                           GPA = true arc length at start
                            #define GAX_GEO_NURBX      7 = Nurbs curve dim=6
                                                           GPG = order of Splines
                                                           GPA = true arc length at start
                            #define GAX_GEO_DATA       8 = unspecified data
                                                           will be converted to 3
                            #define GAX_GEO_NORM       9 = global downward direction
                            #define GAX_GEO_CIRC      11 = full circle
                            #define GAX_GEO_CBEZIER   15 = closed BEZIER
                            #define GAX_GEO_CNURBS    16 = closed NURBS
                            #define GAX_GEO_PROJ_CLO  20 = Klothoid
                            #define GAX_GEO_PROJ_CUB  21 = Cubic spiral
                            #define GAX_GEO_PROJ_BLO  22 = Bloss
                            #define GAX_GEO_PROJ_SIN  24 = Sinusoidal
                            #define GAX_GEO_PROJ_COS  25 = Cosinusoidal
                            #define GAX_GEO_NURBS_KN  90 = Nurbs knot values
                            #define GAX_GEO_NURBS_CPT 91 = Nurbs control points
     @1:  GPG      [1001]   |geometry parameter 1 |Geometrieparameter 1
     @2:  GPA      [1001]   |geometry parameter 2 |Geometrieparameter 2
     @3:  DD       [1001]   |arc length           |Bogenlaenge
     @4:  S1       [-]      |parameter s on start |parameter s am Anfang
     @5:  XYZ1    3[1001]   |Ordinate of start    |Koordinaten Startpunkt
     @8:  DXYZ1   3[-]      |Tangent of start     |Tangente Startpunkt
    @11:  RG1      [1009]   |in-plane curvature   |Krümmung
    @12:  RA1      [1009]   |vertical curvature   |Krümmung im Aufriss
    @13:  S2       [-]      |parameter s on end   |parameter s am Ende
    @14:  XYZ2    3[1001]   |Ordinate of endpoint |Koordinaten Endpunkt
    @17:  DXYZ2   3[-]      |Tangent of endpoint  |Tangent end point
    @20:  RG2      [1009]   |in-plane curvature   |Krümmung
    @21:  RA2      [1009]   |vertical curvature   |Krümmung im Aufriss
    @22:  XAT      [1001]   |relat. startordinate |Relative Start-Ordinate
                             (if 20 <= ILN <= 29)

    These records define curve segments of different types.
    Any curve may have multiple segments even with sharp bends.

    The local coordinate system has the x-axis along the curve.
    The local z-axis is specified by a code "9" BEFORE the other geometric
    data. This vector defines a component in the downward direction in
    values DXYZ1. DD has to be zero and S1=S2 for that item.

    This structure is fully identical to that of {link}165{-link}31/NR{/link}.

    The subtype GAX_GEO_PROJECT is always in the horizontal plane. The
    gravity direction IACHS of 10/0 defines the orientation, but we
    add a :9 info for compatibility reasons.
    If RG1 is not equal RG2 we have a transition curve with parameter GPG,
    LTOT = GPG*ABS(GPG)*(RG2-RG1) and the relative Ordinate XAT.

    Otherwise we have a circular arc with GPG as radius or zero.
    The derivatives are normalized in the horizontal plane, the vertical
    value is measured with respect to the true length.
  
  For Bezier or Nurbs curves (type ILN=5,6,7), the parameter GPA stores the true arc
    length of the curve at start of the segment to allow for a faster evaluation.

     @Rec: 03/ID:101  AXIS_ATB | Geometric segments of axis plan view           :V200701
{/red}
     @0#  ID0      [int]    |ident=101
     @1#  ID1      [int]    |specification type
                               &1  = (B0) station specified
                               &2  = (B1) length  specified
                               &4  = (B2) clothoidal parameters specified
                               &8  = (B3) Tangent specified
                               &16 = (B4) XYZ specified, calculate tangent
                               &32 = (B5) generated data point
     @2#  ID2      [int]    |type of transition curve to be used
                               #0  = clothoid
                               #1  = cubic parabola
                               #2  = bloss curve transition
                               #3  = bi-quadratic (Schramm) transition
                               #4  = sinusoidal
                               #5  = cosinusoidal
     @0:  S        [-]      |Station value at tangent  |Stationswert im Tangentenpunkt
     @1:  L(0)    5[1001]   |Length of segment         |Längen des Segments
                               l(0) = total ; l(1) = straight (START - TS)
                               l(2) = leadin spiral  (TS - SC)
                               l(3) = circular arc   (SC - CS)
                               l(4) = leadout spiral (CS - ST)
     @5:  R(0)    5[1001]   |Radius mid & start & end  |Radius Mitte & Anfang & Ende
                             Clothoidal Param. A1,A2
     @10: XYZ     3[1001]   |Startpoint of tangent     |Startpunkt der Tangente
     @13: DIR     3[-]      |Tangential direction      |Richtung der Tangente
     @16: D       2[1001]   |Distance to point on curve (start/end)
     @18: TAU      [1200]   |deflection angle
     @19: TXT      [chr]    |Identifier of this sequence

     A definition of n segments is decribed by (n+1) tangents = data records in general.
     Each segments has 4 elements described by a straight line, a leadin spiral, a circular
     arc and a lead out spiral, the length of these four elements of each segment are
     contained always in the second data record. However for a definition based on tangents
     there might be an extra straight segment after the last arc.

     The ATB-coordinates are always oriented in the projected coordinate system, i.e.
     XYZ(1) is mapped to the real XYZ(IACHS1), and XYZ(3) is always perpendicular.
     The radius is converted according to the view direction when creating ILN==2 data.

                             (construction phases are controlled via groups only)
     @5#  NOS     2[int]    |Number of section before and behind that placement
     @7#  SEGT     [chr]    |identifier of a segment see (900/0) behind that placement

     @0:  S        [-]      |Parameter s of this section
     @1:  Y        [1001]   |additional transverse offset
     @2:  Z        [1001]   |additional vertical offset
     @3:  ALF      [1200]   |Rotation about global Z     | Verdrehung um global Z
     @4:  ALFX     [1200]   |Rotation about local axis x | Verdrehung um Längsachse x
     @5:  ALFY     [1200]   |Rotation about transverse y | Verdrehung um Querachse y
     @6:  ALFZ     [1200]   |Rotation about vertical   z | Verdrehung um Vertikalachse z
     @7:  INCR     [1200]   |Inclination to the right +y | Querneigung nach rechts +y
     @8:  INCL     [1200]   |Inclination to the left  -y | Querneigung nach links -y
     @9:  SRULE   5[chr]    |Formula string to evaluate the value S
    @14:  TEXT   [str*32]   |Designation of Placement

     A placement is a plane cutting through the primary or secondary axis
     The spans are then defined between the support-placements as follows:
     The first support has always a xsi of 1.0, the startface gets a xsi of 0.0,
     the endface has a xsi > last support point.

     This record is also used to describe any points relative to the axis.
     This record is also used to describe segments along the axis.

     Remark: A cross fall according to DIN is negative in both directions
             if the elevation becomes smaller to the outer direction.
             So INCR = +dH/dy = -dz/dy ; INCL = -dH/dy = +dz/dy

{red}
     @Rec: 03/ID:104  AXIS_ITS | Secondary axis definition                     :V200705
{/red}
     @0#  ID0      [int]    |Ident=104
     @1#  IDS      [int]    |Enum of secondary axis (1='A' to 26 ='Z')
                             allowing to identify the secondary axis by e.g. "AXID.A"
     @2#  IREF     [int]    |Reference to external axis geometry
     @3#  NPT      [int]    |offset for structural points along the axis
                             added to the number of :103 as an offset
     @4#  GRP      [int]    |group number (:103 is always added as an offset)
     @1:  Y        [1001]   |constant or maximum value of y offset
     @2:  Z        [1001]   |constant or maximum value of z offset
     @3:  Y_V     4[chr]    |variable name for y offset (see :110)
     @7:  Z_V     4[chr]    |variable name for z offset (see :110)
     @11: TEXT    [str*32]  |Designation (only for first point of a sequence)

     This record describes parameters of a secondary axis associated to a primary axis.
     A secondary axis can be defined by a constant offset, by a variable distribution
     or by reference to an external geometry. 
     In case of an external geometry, the parametrization of the external geometry must be
     synchronized with the primal axis.

{/red}
     @0#  ID0      [int]    |ident=107

                               0  = center

                              &1024  generated placement

     @4#  GRP      [int]    |group number behind that placement
                             (construction phases are controlled via groups only)
     @5#  NOS     2[int]    |Number of section before and behind that placement
     @7#  IB0      [int]    |general bit-mask
                              &1-&16 free
                              &32   Interpolate Inclination to the right INCR
                              &64   Interpolate Inclination to the left INCL
     @8#  IDP      [chr]    |identifier of this placement
                             has to be unique within one axis
     @9#  SEGT     [chr]    |identifier of a segment see (900/0) behind that placement
     @10# RES     6[int]    |reserved

     @0:  S        [-]      |Parameter s of this section
     @1:  Y        [1001]   |additional transverse offset
     @2:  Z        [1001]   |additional vertical offset
     @3:  ALF      [1200]   |Rotation about global Z     | Verdrehung um global Z (see comments below)
     @4:  ALFX     [1200]   |Rotation about local axis x | Verdrehung um Längsachse x
     @5:  ALFY     [1200]   |Rotation about transverse y | Verdrehung um Querachse y
     @6:  ALFZ     [1200]   |Rotation about vertical   z | Verdrehung um Vertikalachse z
     @7:  INCR     [1200]   |Inclination to the right +y | Querneigung nach rechts +y
     @8:  INCL     [1200]   |Inclination to the left  -y | Querneigung nach links -y
     @9:  SRULE   5[chr]    |Formula string to evaluate the value S
    @14:  TEXT   [str*32]   |Designation of placement

     A placement is a plane cutting through the primary or secondary axis
     The spans are then defined between the support-placements as follows:
     The first support has always a xsi of 1.0, the startface gets a xsi of 0.0,
     the endface has a xsi > last support point.

     The parameter ALF defines as an alternative to ALFZ the orientation of the placement in
     the global XY-plane. It defines the angle of the placement normal from the global X-axis
     mathematically positive around Z. The default value of 0.0 deactivates this parameter.
     To define an angle of 0.0 to the X-axis, a value of 2Pi must be set.

     This record is also used to describe any points relative to the axis.
     This record is also used to describe segments along the axis.
     This record may be followed by a 039/NR:999 GUId-Record.

     Remark: A cross fall according to DIN is negative in both directions
             if the elevation becomes smaller to the outer direction.
             So INCR = +dH/dy = -dz/dy ; INCL = -dH/dy = +dz/dy

!TOPIC 202  5 Geometric Area


  ****  ****  ****                               {link}141{-link}3/*  Geometric Axis{/link}
  *  *  *  *  *                                  {link}202{-link}5/*  Geometric Surface{/link}
  *  *  *  *  *                                  {link}163{-link}Structural Elements{/link}
  *  *  *  *  ****                               {link}164{-link}30/* Structural points{/link}
  *  *  *  *     *                               {link}165{-link}31/* Structural lines{/link}
  *  *  *  *     *                               {link}166{-link}32/* Structural surfaces{/link}
  ****  ****  ****                               {link}167{-link}33/* Structural volumes{/link}
                                                 {link}163{-link}39/* Structural streams{/link}
;    @RecDesc:   5/ID    Geometric Area      

{red}
     @Rec: 05/ID:0   AREA   | Geometric Area                                    :V200704 \
                            | Geometrische Fläche
{/red}

     @0#  ID0     [int]     |identifier 0
     @1#  NG      [int]     |Type of surface representation
                              0 = nearly flat plane with z=f(s,t)
                              1 = surface mesh (obsoleted)
                              2 = surface grid
                              3 = bicubic B-splines m x n grid
                              4 = bilinear coons patch (see 32/12)
                              5 = bicubic  coons patch (see 32/12)
                              6 = yet annother coon (reserved)
                              7 = NURBS-surface non rational
                              8 = NURBS-surface rational (with weights)
                              9 = NURBS-surface rational including thickness
                             10 = unstructured mesh
                             11 = rotational surface GID1 around GID2
                             12 = sweep surface GID1 along GID2
     @2#  GID1    [chr]     |Axis identifier of first reference axis
     @3#  GID2    [chr]     |Axis identifier of second reference axis
     @4#  mgri    [int]     |number of data/control points in s of mesh
     @5#  ngri    [int]     |number of data/control points in t of mesh
     @6#  mspl    [int]     |degree of B-spline in s direction
     @7#  nspl    [int]     |degree of B-spline in t direction
     @8#  sflg    [int]     |property options of surface
                                #0  nearly plane shape
                                &1:  skewed shape (<60° between u-v direction)
                                &4:  curved boundary(>120° change of direction)
                                &16: ratio height/MAX(width)>0.5
     @1:  T      4[-,-,-]   |Transformation
                              T(1:3,1) = local direction u
                              T(1:3,2) = local direction v
                              T(1:3,3) = local normal direction n
                              T(1:3,4) = center coordinates [1001]
    @13:  PAR(0)  16[-]     |additional Parameters|Zus. Parameter
    @29:  BOX 3[1001,1001]  |boundig box xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,zmin,zmax

    @35:  TEXT    [str*32]  |Designation of Line        |Bezeichnung Linie

    The local right-handed coordinate system of the surface is given
    with the u-v axis within the plane and the n-axis normal on the
    surface towards the viewer if the outer boundary is seen
    counter-clockwise. While for B-Splines and coons patches the u
    and v directions are clearly defined, there are especially in 3D
    variant ways of selecting the arbitrary u-axis of a plane.

    If GID2 is not specified for a rotating or sweep curve, it is a
    straight axis starting at (x,y,z) in the direction (sx,sy,sz).

    Parameters are defined as follows:
       (0)    =  TOTAL AREA IN PROJECTION
       (1:2)  =  uMIN,uMAX   maximum and minimum parameters
       (3:4)  =  vMIN,vMAX   maximum and minimum parameters
       (5:6)  =  hMIN,hMAX   maximum and minimum elevation
                             = maxmin of radii for revolution areas
       (7:8)  =  TMIN,TMAX   maximum and minimum thickness

                 For planar and least square regions there are:
       (9:15) =    coefficients of least square

                 For rotational surfaces there are:
       (11)   =    sfak  scaling factor from plane to meridian
                         s = sfak*u / s=sfak*R
       (12)   =    cfak  mapping paramater
                           0.0 = cylindrical projection
                          >0.0 = conical projection (angle of cone)
       (13)   =    rmax  scaling from t-value to real world
                          fixed radius for cylinder / spheres
      (14:15) =    cos(cfak),sin(cfak)

       BOX(2,3)  Bounding box of surface in 3D

     ATTENTION!
     This record will be changed automatically by SOF_FLIB_GARINIT
     Only for rotational surfaces or imported special nonuniform nurbs
     a definition by another program is allowed and recommended.

     Every 32/NR may inherit its geometric properties from 5/ID.

     Unstructured meshes are not yet supported, but the data is then
     a collection of triangular elements, defined by AREA_PTS

{red}
     @Rec: 005/ID:10  AREA_CPT | Control points of area                         :V200704
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]    |Identification of control point data = 10
     @1:  XPAR    *[-]     |spline grid and coefficients
                              TU(MAXNNP_3210)   = knots in s direction
                              TV(MAXNNP_3210)   = knots in t direction
                              CSPL(MAXCSP_3210) = control points
                              Fitpackformat   : sgrid(ngri,mgri,4)
                                                index i=1:4 for x,y,z,t
                              opennurbsformat : sgrid(4,ngri,mgri),
                                                tgrid(ngri,mgri)
                                                index i=1:4 for x,y,z,weight
{red}
     @Rec: 005/ID:11  AREA_PTS | AreaPointonSurface                              :V200704
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]    |Identification of surface description = 11
     @1#  it      [int]    |Type of point
                              0 = generated surface mesh
                              1 = given surface mesh
                              2 = coarse surface grid data
                              3 = Control points of bicubic splines
                              4 = occupied by bilinear coons
                              5 = occupied by bicubic  coons
                              6 = occupied by yet another coon
                              7 = Control points of nurbs
                              8 = Control points of nurbs (reserved see :10)
                              9 = KNOT values of nurbs at item x
                                   m,x,w for u-direction if m>=0
                                   n,x,w for v-direction if n>=0
                             10 = node of an unstructured mesh
                                   m == 0 for scattered data point
                                   m >  0 counter for elements, i.e. a triangle
                                          has three records with same m-value
     @2#  m       [int]    |Rasterlocation of mesh (0 < m < mgri )
     @3#  n       [int]    |Rasterlocation of mesh (0 < n < ngri )
     @0:  W       [-]      |the weight of NURBS control point
                            or muliplicity for the KNOT vectors
     @1:  X       [1001]   |X-ordinate           |Koordinate X
     @2:  Y       [1001]   |Y-ordinate           |Koordinate Y
     @3:  Z       [1001]   |Z-ordinate           |Koordinate Z
     @4:  T       [1010]   |Thickness            |Dicke

     surface mesh and grid points are in a fixed sequence
         (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) ...
         (0,1), (1,1), (2,1) ...
         (0,2), (1,2), (2,2) ...

     A surface mesh (it=0) is only generated for the other types of
     description. So we have either it=0 or it=1 grids but not both.
     all other it (2 to 7) or revolution surfaces however are allowed
     to have an it=0/-1/-2 grid too (for visualisation purpose).

     An unstructured mesh (it<0) consists of arbitrary triangles or
     quadrilaterals and nodes. However for those regions we need to
     know the sequence of the nodes along the boundaries. Thus m and
     n are used to give the relative location n along the edge m.

     It is also possible to have unstructured data points within a
     regular mesh describing the thickness of the surface.

{red}
     @Rec: 005/ID:12  AREA_CPI   | COONsPatchInfo                               :V200702
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]    |Identification of COONs blending edges 12
     @1#  it      [int]    |Type of blending
                              0 = bilinear QUAD patch only
                              1 = bilinear blending (default)
                              2 = bicubic blending
     @2#  iu0     [int]    |No of geometry line for u=umin (left)
                            or No of geometry point 1 for (0,0)
     @3#  iu1     [int]    |No of geometry line for u=umax (right)
                            or No of geometry point 2 for (1,0)
     @4#  iv0     [int]    |No of geometry line for v=vmin (lower)
                            or No of geometry point 3 for (0,1)
     @5#  iv1     [int]    |No of geometry line for v=vmax (upper)
                            or No of geometry point 4 for (1,1)
                               0 for a trinagular fit.
     @1:  sp     4[-,-,-]  |Length parameters for the edges iu0,iu1,iv0,iv1
                            in the form 4(true length,Station1,Station2)
                            (S1>S2 if orientation is in reverse direction)
     @13: uv     2[-,-]    |umin,umax,vmin,vmax of the parameter plane
     @17: cxyz   4[-,-,-]  |Coordinates of the corner points C1,C2,C3,C4
     @29: tinc   8[-,-,-]  |inclinations for a bicubic patch as vectors
                            in the endpoints of all 4 lines (see below)
     @53: twist  4[-,-,-]  |Twist of x,y,z-Ordinate at corner C1 (0,0)
                            Twist of x,y,z-Ordinate at corner C2 (1,0)
                            Twist of x,y,z-Ordinate at corner C3 (1,1)
                            Twist of x,y,z-Ordinate at corner C4 (0,1)

     For the coons patches geometry we need four outer boundaries that
     are blended. In most cases these are identical to the real outer
     boundaries, but in special cases these may be selected seperately.
     This record is needed if the number of outer edges is not 4 or
     the type of coons patch is not bilinear.

                   ^ inc3                ^ inc4
              C4 o-|--------- iv1 -------|-o C3
                --> inc6                   --> inc8
                 |            v|           |
                iu0            |->u       iu1
                 |                         |
                --> inc5                  --> inc7
              C1 o-|--------- iv1 -------|-o C2
                   ^ inc1                ^ inc2

     For more details see FARIN / Curves and surfaces for CAGD

{red}
     @Rec: 008/ID:0 CON_0   | Connection Headder                                :V200501
{/red}
     @0=  IDS      [int]    | Identification = 0
     @1#  TYP      [int]    | Type of connection
                               #0   = USER  User defined free connection
                               #1   = B2C   Beam to Column connection
                               #2   = B2CA  B2C with angle cleats
                               #3   = B2CS  B2C shear with angle cleats
                               #4   = BSP   Beam splice
                               #5   = B2B   Beam to beam connection
                               #6   = B2BA  B2B with angle cleats
                               #7   = EPSP  End plate splice / Roof joint
                               #8   = FND   Footing plate connection
                               #9   = TSP   Tube splice
                               #10  = TKN   Truss K-node
                               #11  = TPW   Truss Plate connection
                              +1000 = BRACED FRAME
                              +2000 = CHECK  COMPRESSION
                              +4000 = CAPACITY DESIGN FOR WELDS
     @2#  MAT      [int]    | Materialnumber for all plates
     @1:  TEXT     [str*32] | designation of connection  | Bezeichnung Verbindung

     Connections and all parts of the connections are defined by an ID [chr].
     A connection itself may have multiple instances in the system. Any ID =
     position has the same parameters and geometric data for all instances.

     An instance of an connection needs always a GTP (30/NR) to establish the
     orientation of the local coordinate system and the connecting elements
     (see 030/NR:8 GPT_CON)

     An 8/ID may contain:
        - :0 a node of connections defined by
             - several member connections, each composed by
               - :10 a geometric offset and orientation including haunches
                     and the web and flange connection definitions
               - :11 an optional endplate definition
               - :12 an optional pinplate definition
             - :20 several additional plates / stiffeners
        - :1 several bolt diameters of the same type
        - :2 exactly one welding type
        - :3 exactly one cleat angle or latch types

     For rectangular plates:     <------  B  ------>    ----   ----
                                 |                 |     h0     mx
                                 |  X  X     X  X  |    ----
                                 | =============== |     h1    ----
                                 |  X  X  |  X  X  |    ---
                                 |        |        |
                                 |        |        |     h2
                                 |        |        |
                                 |        |        |
                                 |  X  X  |  X  X  |    ---
                                 | =============== |     h3
                                 |  X  X     X  X  |    ---
                                 |                 |
                                 |-----------------|
                                       <--W0->
                                    <W1>     <W1>

     Plate type #3 is with a constant width B all around the steel shape.
     Thus for a tube or a hollow section with smoothed edges, the end plate
     will have the same shape and a hole in the middle.

!TOPIC 143  9

Cross Sections are contained in multiple records all with 3 Integers and up to 32 regular floats. 
The first integer defines the type of information.

The sections may be saved with several level of Details (see AQU_SAVE_TEMPLATE in dlib/aqu_ref.f90)
    LOD 0        most compact data (used for export or minimum storage capacity)
                 Steel sections are only presented by the ID 12
    LOD 1	 compact definition (used to save in the SDB)
                 Steel sections are contained with a 99:100 Block with compact data
    LOD 2	 raw definition (used to calculate the LOAD 3)
                 arcs are resolved with generated points, holes ar not yet analyzed
The following levels are generated in AQUA
    LOD 3        all polygon data including holes has been generated, but still masterdata 
                 This is the level required to generate th FE-mesh (see AQUA/AQUSGEO.F90)
    LOD 4        All sectional values have been calculated for all construction stages
                 NEFF-Splits have been applied, 

The sequence of records in LOD 4 is always:
         009/NR:0     SectionalValues (total section)
         009/NR:4     SectionalValues (shear) 
         009/NR:5     SectionalValues (warping)
         009/NR:8     Transformation info
         009/NR:18:0  CS-Headderinfo (list of construction stages if defined)
         009/NR:91    Mat-Headderinfo (list of solid materials for composite sections)
     n * 009/NR:2     SectionalValues (total part of section)
         009/NR:1     SectionalValues (effective section)
     n * 009/NR:3     SectionalValues (effective part of section)

Records with id 2/3 are only present for composite sections. 


  ****   ****  ****                              {link}130{-link}Material{/link}
  *  *   *  *  *  *                              {link}142{-link}Steel connections{/link}
  *  *   *  *  *  *                              {link}143{-link}-->Sectional values{/link}

                                                 {link}144{-link}-->Definitions{/link}

     @0=  ID       [int]    |Identification    | Kennziffer
                             #define SECT_ID_INVALID             -1 = section without calculated data (invalid geometry)
                             #define SECT_ID_RAWDATA             -2 = section without calculated data (raw data)
                             #define SECT_ID_SUBDATA_INIT        -3 = section without calculated data (sub data construction stage)
                             #define SECT_ID_SUBDATA_CALCULATION -4 = section with calculated shear data (sub data construction stage)
     @1#  MNo      [int]    |Materialnumber of sections     \
                            | Materialnummer Querschnitt
     @2#  MRf      [int]    |Materialnumber of Reinforcement\
                            | Materialnummer Bewehrung

     @1:  A        [1012]   |Area                           \
                            | Querschnittsfläche
     @2:  Ay       [1012]   |Sheardeformation area Y        \
                            | Schubverformungsfläche Y
     @3:  Az       [1012]   |Sheardeformation area Z        \
                            | Schubverformungsfläche Z
     @4:  It       [1014]   |Torsional moment of inertia    \
                            | Torsionsträgheitsmoment
     @5:  Iy       [1014]   |Moments of inertia y-y         \
                            | Flächenträgheitsmoment y-y
     @6:  Iz       [1014]   |Moments of inertia z-z         \
                            | Flächenträgheitsmoment z-z
     @7:  Iyz      [1014]   |Moments of inertia y-z         \
                            | Flächenträgheitsmoment y-z
     @8:  ys       [1011]   |y-Ordinate Center of elasticity \
                            | y-Ordinate elastischer Schwerpunkt
     @9:  zs       [1011]   |z-Ordinate Center of elasticity \
                            | z-Ordinate elastischer Schwerpunkt
    @10:  ysc      [1011]   |y-Ordinate of Shear-Center     \
                            | y-Ordinate Schubmittelpunkt
    @11:  zsc      [1011]   |z-Ordinate of Shear-Center     \
                            | z-Ordinate Schubmittelpunkt
    @12:  EM       [1090]   |Elasticity Modulus             \
                            | Elastizitätsmodul
    @13:  GM       [1090]   |Shear Modulus                  \
                            | Schubmodul
    @14:  gam      [1091]   |Nominal weight                 \
                            | Nominales Eigengewicht

    for the non effective global sectional values we have two centers:
        ys,zs   are the reference points ysn,zsn for the normal force,
                i.e. a normal force acting in this point creates a uniform stress
        ysc,zsc are the reference points ysb,zsb for the bending stress

    for the partial effective sectional values we have three extra values:
    i.e. @15  Aeff(y)  = effective area for evaluating ys and Iz
    i.e. @16  Aeff(z)  = effective area for evaluating zs and Iy
    i.e. @17  Aeff(yz) = effective area for evaluating Iyz


Cross sections may be used for beams and pipes (conf. ID=4). For the
hydraulic sections the static values are not used of course. 
The main element will be of type 102 with the roughness and leakage.

For construction stages their might be multiple instances of sectional
information. In that case their will be a record of subtype 18 dividing
those data.


        0  MNo MRF    Master gross section
           ...        18  NoCS0 NoCSD  Titel of construction stage 0
           ...                         selective elements belonging to this CS0
           ...        18  NoCS1 NoCSD1 Titel of construction stage 1
           ...                         selective elements belonging to this CS1
           ...        18  NoCS1 NoCSD2 Sub Titel of construction stage 1
           ...                         selective elements belonging to this CS1
           ...                         but with a different NoCSD value
           ...        18  NoCS2 NoCSD  Titel of construction stage 2
           ...                         selective elements belonging to this CS2
        0  MNo MRF    Sectional data for construction stage CS0
           ...        copy of all sectional elements including
           ...        specific values for this construction stage
        0  MNo MRF    Sectional data for construction stage CS1
           ...        copy of all sectional elements including
           ...        specific values for this construction stage
        0  MNo MRF    Sectional data for construction stage CS2
           ...        copy of all sectional elements including
           ...        specific values for this construction stage


To access the data for a specific construction stage we have thus two possibilities:

- If we are working with the master data block:
  -- for a first read, collect the NoCSi-values in an array
     (index is augmented if NOCSi is larger than the last one)
  -- for the second read skip all data behind a :18/:19,,99 record with
     CSi < NoCSi (may exit in most cases) or CSi > NoCSDi (if NoCSDi>0)

- If we are working with the consecutive data-blocks:
  -- when reading the first block, collect the NoCSi-values in an array
  -- count the records with ID==0 until you reach the nth occurence
  -- continue reading until EOF or the next ID==0 is reached

                                  #define PROF_RECTANGULAR_BAR   15
                                  #define PROF_BAR_TUBE_PIPE     16 = Circular Bar, Tube or pipe

                                internal types of AQU_PROF
                         iref = selected reference point
                                  #define PROF_REF_STD  0  = origin
                                  #define PROF_REF_S    1  = center of elasticity
                                  #define PROF_REF_SM   2  = shear center
                                  #define PROF_REF_OR   3  = y : right   z : upper 
                                  #define PROF_REF_OL   4  = y : left    z : upper 
                                  #define PROF_REF_OM   5  = y : middle  z : upper 
                                  #define PROF_REF_R    6  = y : right   z : middle
                                  #define PROF_REF_L    7  = y : left    z : middle
                                  #define PROF_REF_M    8  = y : middle  z : middle
                                  #define PROF_REF_UR   9  = y : right   z : lower
                                  #define PROF_REF_UL  10  = y : left    z : lower
                                  #define PROF_REF_UM  11  = y : middle  z : lower
                         ivtp = selected representation bits
                                  #define PROF_PROP_SOLID                 16 = B4  = thick walled, thin walled if not set
                                  #define PROF_PROP_HALF                  32 = B5  = half divided section
                                  #define PROF_PROP_MIRROR_ORIGIN         64 = B6  = mirrored to origin
                                  #define PROF_PROP_MIRROR_Y_AXIS        128 = B7  = mirrored to y-axis
                                  #define PROF_PROP_MIRROR_Z_AXIS        256 = B8  = mirrored to z-axis
                                  #define PROF_PROP_FLIP_TO_Y_AXIS       192 = B6+B7 = flip y-y
                                  #define PROF_PROP_FLIP_TO_Z_AXIS       320 = B6+B8 = flip z-z
                                  #define PROF_PROP_MIRROR_4_ITEMS       448 = B6:B8 = special: 4 items
                                  #define PROF_PROP_CUSTOM_SHAPE         512 = B9  = modified by user
                                  #define PROF_PROP_CALCULATION         1024 = B10 = with calculation (no standard profile)
                                  #define PROF_PROP_SIMPLIFIED_WIND     2048 = B11 = deprecated: simplified wind drag coeff.
                                  #define PROF_PROP_IMPERIAL_UNITS      4096 = B12 = section is in imperial units
                                  #define PROF_PROP_SELECTOR_METRIC     8192 = B13 = but selector in metric units
                                  #define PROF_PROP_R_AS_K_FOR_HAUNCH  16384 = B14 = use k and k1 for a haunch for AISC
                                  #define PROF_PROP_RECORD_PROF        32768 = B15 = PROF record only, without SECT record
                                  #define PROF_PROP_ERRORFLAG          65536 = B16 = errorflag overlapping mirror
                          #define SECT_PROF_PROP_MULT  64
     @0:  Typ   [chr]    |type of section    |Profilbezeichnung
     @1:  Z1    [-]      |nominal first size
     @2:  Z2    [-]      |nominal second size
     @3:  Z3    [-]      |thickness or weight selector
                           Z1 is in most cases an integer value (eg. HEB 300)
                           Z2 is in most cases an integer value (eg. SH 300 200)
                              in some cases, it might be a value with 1 to 3 optional digits
                              (eg. ROHR 200.5 x 12.3 or PIPE 16x0.625 and PIPE 12.75x0.375)
                           Z3 may be (encoded by flags in the shape definition AQU_PROF.F90)
                              - a thickness in mm with always 1 digit
                              - a thickness in 1/16 or 1/8 inch with always 3 digits
                              - a weight in kg/m  with always 1 digit
                              - a weight in lb/ft with always 1 digit
     @4:  alf   [1200]   |Rotation angle                              |Drehwinkel
     @5:  It    [1014]   |Tabulated torsional inertia                 |Tabellierte Torsionsträgheit It
     @6:  ysc   [1011]   |Tabulated shear center y                    |Tabellierter Schubmittelpunkt y
     @7:  zsc   [1011]   |Tabulated shear center z                    |Tabellierter Schubmittelpunkt z

     @9:  b     [1011]   |Width                                       |Breite

     @11: t     [1011]   |Thickness of flange                         |Flanschdicke
     @12: r1    [1011]   |First radius                                |Erster Ausrundungsradius
     @13: r2    [1011]   |Second radius                               |Zweiter Ausrundungsradius
     @14: yoff  [1011]   |Y coordinate of offset                      |Y-Koordinate Versatz
     @15: zoff  [1011]   |Z coordinate of offset                      |Z-Koordinate Versatz
     @16: CM    [1016]   |Tabulated warping resistance                |Tabellierter Wölbwiderstand
     @17: WMIN  [1012]   |Characteristic warping 1                    |Charakteristische Verwölbung 1
     @18: WMAX  [1012]   |Characteristic warping 2                    |Charakteristische Verwölbung 2
     @19: WT    [1018]   |Torsional resistance                        |Torsionswiderstand
     @20: AY    [1012]   |Shear area Ay                               |Schubfläche Ay
     @21: AZ    [1012]   |Shear area Az                               |Schubfläche Az
     @22: RID   [chr]    |User defined ident                          |Kurzbezeichnung
     @23: WU1   [1011]   |Bolt position 1                             |Wurzelmaß w1
     @24: WU2   [1011]   |Bolt position 2                             |Wurzelmaß w2
     @25: WU3   [1011]   |Bolt position 3                             |Wurzelmaß w3
     @26: YREF  [1011]   |Y coordinates of reference point            |Y-Koordinate des Referenzpunktes
     @27: ZREF  [1011]   |Z coordinates of reference point            |Z-Koordinate des Referenzpunktes
     @28: b2    [1011]   |Width lower part                            |Breite unterer Teil
     @29: t2    [1011]   |Lower flange thickness                      |Untere Flanschdicke
     @30: BEZ   8*[chr]  |Character of shape                          |Bezeichnung lang
     @38: Vypl  [1102]   |Characteristic plastic shear force Vy       !Charakteristische plastische Querkraft Vy
     @39: Vzpl  [1102]   |Characteristic plastic shear force Vz       !Charakteristische plastische Querkraft Vz
     @40: Mtpl  [1103]   |Characteristic plastic torsional moment Mt  !Charakteristische plastisches Moment Mt
     @41: Mt2pl [1103]   |Characteristic plastic torsional moment Mt2 !Charakteristische plastisches Moment Mt2
     @42: Mbpl  [1103]   |Characteristic plastic warping moment Mb    !Charakteristische plastisches Wölbmoment Mb

     For mirrored sections, the origin of the coordinate system is assumed to be on the symmetry axis, 
     thus yref/zref define the distance of the two elements.
     The tabulated shear center ysc, zsc is referenced to the elastic center (=distance).
     For flipped, rotated or mirrored shapes ysc and zsc still contain the tabulated value in its original configuration. 
     Thus the transformations have to be applied when requiring the real value.

{red}
     @Rec:   009/NR:80   SECT_CW | Hydrodynamic coefficients (WIND/Wave loading)   :V201301
{/red}
     @0=  ID    [int]    |Identification 80
     @1#  iref  [int]    |Reference of coefficients
                            #0   =  default curve (e.g. generated for Steel shapes)
                                    using projection type as 3 
                            #1   =  Reference is B
                                    py = cy * B * p
                                    pz = cz * B * p
                                    mt = ct * B * B * p
                            #2   =  Reference is H
                                    py = cy * H * p
                                    pz = cz * H * p
                                    mt = ct * H * H * p
                            #3   =  user curve projection BH
                                    py = cy * H * p
                                    pz = cz * B * p
                                    mt = ct * H * B * p
                            #4   =  bridge curve projection HB
                                    py = cy * H * p
                                    pz = cz * B * p
                                    mt = ct * B * B * p
     @2#  alf   [int]    |angle of attack in degrees
                             0   = flow in -y direction (from left)
                            90   = flow in -z direction (upwards)
                           -90   = flow in +z direction (downwards)
                           180   = flow in +y direction (from right)
     @1:  cy    [-]      |wind reaction coefficient in y-direction
     @2:  cz    [-]      |wind reaction coefficient in z-direction
     @3:  ct    [-]      |wind reaction coefficient for torsional moment
     @4:  chyd  [-]      |hydrodynamic coefficient (Morrison equation)
     @5:  clat  [-]      |lateral wind reaction coefficient
     @6:  S     [-]      |Strouhal number
     @7:  ag    [1200]   |angle of attack in degrees 
                          (used to detect old data without chyd)
     @8:  b2h   [-]      |ratio of B2H needed for WBH and BH with derivativa

                         cy,cz and ct are dimensionless coefficients
                         The lineload due to wind action is (REF HB)

                            py = -cy * (zmax-zmin) * q
                            pz = -cz * (ymax-ymin) * q
                            mt = -ct * (zmax-zmin) * (zmax-zmin) * q

                         Thus a positive value of cz means uplift, a
                         positive value of cy indicates a force to the
                         right side.

     The values cy,cz,ct may be defined by an expression 99:105

     @2#  IRTS  [int]    |Subtype of reference definition for the points:
                           #define REF_IRTS_ABSOLUTE_COORD      0 = absolute coordinates (if P1==P2==0)
                                                                    relative polar coordinates to point P1 (if P2=0)
                                                                    otherwise relative y to P1 and z to P2
                           #define REF_IRTS_RELATIVE_NOSCALE    1 = relative do not scale at all     (TREF1 -TTT)
                                                                    i.e. the reference has fixed values

                                                                    i.e. the reference has a fixed offset

                                                                  = keep old z for single point modus (REF=0)

     @1:  REF  200[chr]  |Identifier of references (0 = not defined)
                              REF(1)     = point-id P1
                              REF(2)     = point-id P2 or angle
                              REF(3)     = point-id P3
                              REF(4)     = <0 (identifier for variable length format)
                              REF(5:200) = (max 3) Formula strings (64[chr]) separated by 00
                                           for y-value,z-value,angle / radius

                              special:     REF(1:3)<0 use negative coordinates (mirror)
                                          '0000'      absolute coordinates (origin)

                              obsoleted:
                              REF(04:11) = Formula expression *32 for y-value
                              REF(12:19) = Formula expression *32 for z-value
                              REF(20:27) = Formula expression *32 for angle
                                           CADINP allowed only for 8 characters

                              Hint: the record may be shorter, ie. without any formulas
                                    the historic structure with point-ids REF(1:3) only
                                    is also possible, recommended is to specify 7 values
                                    with REF(5:7)==0 for that case.

     Any geometric coordinate may be defined with reference to other sectional
     points or polygon vertices. This is described with prefixes 009/nr:099.
     The structure of this information is closely related to the structure to
     come next in the CDBASE, but as it appears before there is some overhead
     for efficency reasons. For the interpolation of sections or the generation
     of templates we allow a nested reference structure.

     Each coordinate of a point may have up to three references.

         1. a reference point P1
         2. a direction point or an angle P2
         3. an external extra coordinate point P3
              - may be specified in CADINP / taken from template section
              - may be given by a variable/formula reference
              - may be given by a geometric axis relative to central axis
                the formula expression is @ID_OF_AXIS

     The base cases are (opt.formula = formula is optional)

     B0X = carthesian references explicit or relative to other points

         B00  99/101/0  0,0,0,-1,"opt.y-formula","opt.z-formula",0
                        new coordinates have absolute coordinates
         B01  99/101/0  REF-Y,0,0,-1,"opt.y-formula","opt.z-formula",0
                        allowed shortcut for REF-Y==REF-Z
         B02  99/101/0  REF-Y,REF-Z,0,-1,"opt.y-formula","opt.z-formula",0
                        new coordinates have the same or explicit (formula)
                        offset to the reference point(s). The special
                        reference point '0000' may be specified for
                        absolute coordinates.

     B1X = local references - line mode

              local coordinates relative to single point + angle
         B10  99/101/4  REF-P,angle,0,-1,"opt.1-form","opt.2-form","angle-form"
                        new coordinates have the same or explicitly defined polar offset
                        to the reference point. If a formula for the angle is specified,
                        the angle will be saved instead of reference P2.

              local coordinates relative along a line P1-P2
         B11  99/101/1  REF-P1,REF-P2,0,-1,"opt.1-form","opt.2-form",0
         B12  99/101/2  REF-P1,REF-P2,0,-1,"opt.1-form","opt.2-form",0
         B13  99/101/3  REF-P1,REF-P2,0,-1,"opt.1-form","opt.2-form",0
                        for those cases the polar coordinate system is defined
                        by the orientation and scaling of line P1-P2

     B2X = geometric construction references (extended line mode)

              coordinates on a line P1-P2 or P1+angle triggered by point REF-P3
         B25  99/101/5  REF-P1,REF-P2,REF-P3,-1,"opt.y-form",0,0   align for y=y(P3|y-form)
         B26  99/101/6  REF-P1,REF-P2,REF-P3,-1,0,"opt.z-form",0   align for z=z(P3|z-form)
         B27  99/101/7  REF-P1,REF-P2,REF-P3,-1,0,0,0              align perpendicular from P3
                        for those cases the coordinate values are calculated from
                        coordinates P3 with a projection on line P1-P2. If neither
                        P3 nor formulas are given, the old offset is used instead (==B15/B16)

              carthesian relative coordinates along a polar direction
         B28  99/101/37 REF-P1,angle,REF_P3,-1,"opt.y-form",0,"angle-form" align for fixed y
         B29  99/101/38 REF-P1,angle,REF_P0,-1,0,"opt.z-form","angle-form" align for fixed z
                        The third reference is pointing to the point itself!

{red}
     @Rec:   009/NR:100  SECT_SPT | SectionStressPoint (SPT/QSP)                  :V200805
     @Rec:: 1009/NR:100  SSCT_SPT | SectionFemPoint                               :V202502
     @Rec:   009/NR:101  SECT_PPT | SectionPolygonPoint (POLY/QPOL)               :V200910
     @Rec:: 1009/NR:101  SSCT_PPT | SectionFemPolygonPoint                        :V202502
     @Rec::  009/NR:310  SECT_PTC | PartialIntegrationPoint of shear cut          :V202502
     @Rec:: 1009/NR:310  SSCT_PTC | PartialCutIntegrationPoint of shear cut       :V202502
{/red}
     @0=  ID    [int]    |Identification 100/101
     @1#  MNo   [int]    |Material number       |Materialnummer
                          # 0 | Geometry Point     | Geometriepunkt
                          < 0 Special construction points, with bitpattern for 100
                           B0 | Bearing position   | Lagerposition
                           B1 | Surveying posit.   | Vermessungspunkt
                           B2 | Tendon position    | Spannstranglage
                          < 0 Inserted vertex from finite element generation
     @2#  IDP   [int]    |Number*256 + Bitpattern

                           meaning for (:100)     
                           ------------------     
                           #define SPT_IDP_IN           1 =  B0 = within section         
                           #define SPT_IDP_C2T          2 =  B1 = original c/t point     
                           #define SPT_IDP_NEFF_Y       4 =  B2 = non effective secondary bending (y,Mz) (generated info)            
                           #define SPT_IDP_NEFF_Z       8 =  B3 = non effective primary bending   (z,My) (generated info)            
                           #define SPT_IDP_NEFF_N      16 =  B4 = non effective normal force        (N)  (generated info)          
                           #define SPT_IDP_FEM         32 =  B5 = FEM nodes (0=QUAD middle) or
                                                                  FEM weight point (gauss point in corner, following a QUAD middle)        
                           #define SPT_IDP_GENERATED   64 =  B6 = generated point      (generated info)   
                           #define SPT_IDP_FIBRE      128 =  B7 = FEM integration fibre  
                           #define SPT_IDP_NUMBER     256 = *B8 = internal QUAD number / internal NODE number

                              meaning for (:101)
                              ------------------
                           #define PPT_IDP_IN           1 =  B0 = inner boundary
                                                        2 =  B1 = free (former: expl. non effective)
                           #define PPT_IDP_NEFF_Y       4 =  B2 = non effective secondary bending (y,Mz) (generated info)            
                           #define PPT_IDP_NEFF_Z       8 =  B3 = non effective primary bending   (z,My) (generated info)            
                           #define PPT_IDP_NEFF_N      16 =  B4 = non effective normal force        (N)  (generated info)          
                           #define PPT_IDP_TP          32 =  B5 = tangential point (TP), fillet point
                           #define PPT_IDP_GENERATED   64 =  B6 = generated point      (generated info)
                           #define PPT_IDP_LAST       128 =  B7 = last vertex (=1.)    (generated info)
                           #define PPT_IDP_POLYGON    256 = *B8 = polygon number

                           #define PPT_IDP_GENERATED_POLYGON  100 = first generated polygon number

     @3#  TNr   [chr]    |Designation              |Bezeichnung
                          Hint: It is expected for Interpolation that all vertices have
                                a unique identifier. However for some cases points will
                                not have an identifier, because they are of no importance
                                A leading ~ may be used to specify unique identifiers
                                for vertices of minor importance.
                          Hint: Points with negative MNo do not have an ID but a node or
                                element number instead which can't be treated as LIT() 
     @1:  y     [1011]   |y-ordinate            |y-Koordinate
     @2:  z     [1011]   |z-ordinate            |z-Koordinate
     @3:  RT    [1011]   |Radius of circular arc ; first radius of ellipse (:101) ; effective thickness (:100) \
                         |Radius im Kreisogen ; erster Radius der Ellipse  (:101) ; Effektive Dicke     (:100)
     @4:  Wty   [1018]   |Resistance Torsion    |Torsionswiderstand
     @5:  WVyy  [1017]   |Resistance y-shear    |Schubwiderstand Vy
     @6:  WVzy  [1017]   |Resistance z-shear    |Schubwiderstand Vz
     @7:  Wt2y  [1018]   |Resistance 2nd Torsion|sek.Torsionswiderstand
     @8:  Wtz   [1018]   |Resistance Torsion    |Torsionswiderstand
     @9:  WVyz  [1017]   |Resistance y-shear    |Schubwiderstand Vy
     @10: WVzz  [1017]   |Resistance z-shear    |Schubwiderstand Vz
     @11: Wt2z  [1018]   |Resistance 2nd Torsion|sek.Torsionswiderstand
     @12: W0    [1012]   |unit warping          |Einheitsverwölbung
     @13: epsr  [-]      |non effective strain ratio (0 < epsr <= 1)
     @14: exp   [-]      |property set          |Eigenschaftssatz
                          older Version: air [-] air contact ratio (0.0 <= air <= 1.0)
     @15: RT2   [1011]   |second radius of ellipse   (:101) ; unused (:100) \
                         |zweiter Radius der Ellipse (:101) ; unused (:100)
                          -99999. = not used (no ellipse)


  Resistances are unit stress due to force 1 with their components tau-yx (4-7) and tau-zx (8-11)
  As the total shear is obtained by a norm (square root), but a positive shear stress cannot 
  account for correct sway and favorable effects, the values may have a sign associated by a
  reference direction. Polygon vertcies use the direction of the edge, stress points (:100)
  use either the Vz-direction or an angle saved in the exp-item (0=z-axis,90=y-axis) 

  used only for stress location points: (older versions up to 2024: fix:temp1 @15-@22 !)

     @16: fix   [1011]   |location of fix point |Abstand Festhaltung
                          for b/t-ratios (cmp. 9/NR:103 fixa/fixb)
     @17: sigd  [1092]   |max. dynamic allowed stress range sig-d(-1) \
                         |max. erlaubte Schwingbreite sigma sig-d(-1)
     @18: taud  [1092]   |max dynamic allowed stress range tau-d(-1) \
                         |max erlaubte max. Schwingbreite tau-d(-1)
     @19: litd  [chr]    |literal for notch type |Bezeichnung Kerbfall
     @20: sigy  [1092]   |stress perpendicular   |Spannung Querrichtung
                          older Versions (length<(4,19) or (4,20): @13

  used only for FEM integration points and boundaries of FEM:

     @21: Aref  [1012]   |weight (effective area) FE-integration points
     @22: temp  [1215]   |Temperature           |Temperatur
     @23: temp1 [1215]   |maximum temperature in history (for damage)

     The integration points may be in 4 flavours, controlled by CTRL SINT
     1.  Center point only with weight
     2.  Center point without weight, nodal points with weight
     3.  Center and nodal points with weights (lobatto)
     4.  Center point without weight, followed by 4 Gauss-Points with weights 

  A radius is possible for two cases:
     1. a tangent intersection for a fillet or chamfer (IDP&32)
        for the raw definition data we have just one vertex
        for the cooked data after that leading vertex we have
         - all points on the fillet/chamfer with (IDP&64)
         - a second instance of the TP with (IDP&64+32)
     2. for non TP points the radius is only defined for polygon points
        within an arc. Only if both edges on both sides of the vertex
        are curved this value will be set.
        Thus: 1. One given radius for an edge is dominant for the whole arc
              2. Each arc has at least 3 vertices, 1st and last have R==0.0

     For non-effective parts we have also two possibilities:
     1. Points with the bits 4,8,16 are treated in a special way during the
        evaluation in the way that some of the integrals are suppressed.
        The treatement of an edge is defined by logical AND of both vertices.
     2. The older definition used an algorithm based on the sequence of the
        points:
          - For the first point of the polygon set the variable:
                ieff = iand(isp(2),2)
          - To get the effective area only skip all points where
                iand(isp(2),2) != ieff
          - To get the total area skip the points with
                iand(isp(2),ieff) != 0

                          beta = eta*c/t

     fixa and fixb are ordinates relative to the endpoints of the element
     defining the endpoints for c/t checks. There are special meanings:
          -1E+21   = factor of length, is an unused end (suppresses the design check), input was '-distance'
          -99999.0 = condition is determined automatically
          -value   = distance to a fixed end, effective buckling length is extended
          -1E-5    = is a free end
          -1E-13   = factor of length, used for distance to a free end, effective buckling length is extended
          +1E-5    = is a fixed end
          +value   = distance to a fixed end, effective buckling length is shortened
          +1E+10   = is an unused end (suppresses the design check)
          +1E+12   = automatic determination of condition failed (not clear condition)
          +1E+14   = is an unused end (suppresses the design check), input was 'free'
          +1E+16   = is an unused end (suppresses the design check), input was 'fix'
          +1E+21   = factor of length, is an unused end (suppresses the design check), input was '+distance'
     when a panel is intersecting with non effective rectangles it will be
     split into a sequence of elements. The fixa/fixb values have to be
     changed accordingly.

The sub data of the sections mainly contain the FEM results and cut  results in order to speed up the reading of the main data of the section.
The SECT_SUB entry marks in the main data (KWH=9) that some sub data (KWH=1009) are available starting with the same block ID.
The SSCT_SUB entry marks in the sub data (KWH=1009) the start of the block. 
Each following SSCT_SUB entry or SSCT_CS entry ends the block.

{red}
     @Rec:    009/NR:1009  SECT_SUB | SectionalSubDataBlock                 :V202502
     @RecM:  1009/NR:1009  SSCT_SUB | SectionalSubDataBlock                 :V202502
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]  |identifier 1009
     @1#  Block   [int]  |consecutive number of the block      |Laufende Nummer des Blocks
                          separate numbering for each final construction stage
     @2#  Type    [int]  |Type of following items              |Typ der folgenden Elememte
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_MESH_TOPOLOGY       1 = topology of mesh, quad elements                       (SSCT_FEM)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_MESH_NODE           2 = topology of mesh, coordinates of the nodes            (SSCT_NOD)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_NEFFZONE            3 = zones of non effectivity                              (SSCT_SNZ)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_RESULT_MIDD        11 = result points, quad middles and gauss points          (SSCT_SPT (SECT_SPT) with IDP=SPT_IDP_FIBRE)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_RESULT_NODE        12 = result points, node points                            (SSCT_SPT (SECT_SPT) with IDP=SPT_IDP_FIBRE+SPT_IDP_FEM)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_POLYGON            19 = detailed polygons                                     (SSCT_PPT (SECT_PPT) with MNO<0)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_CUT_MIDD           21 = result points of a cut, quad middles and gauss points (SSCT_PTC (SECT_PTC) with IDP=SPT_IDP_FIBRE)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_CUT_NODE           22 = result points of a cut, node points                   (SSCT_PTC (SECT_PTC) with IDP=SPT_IDP_FIBRE+SPT_IDP_FEM)
                          #define SECT_SUB_TYPE_CUT_RF             25 = reinforcements of a cut                               (SSCT_PCP (SECT_PCP), SSCT_LCP (SECT_LCP))
     @3#  TNr     [chr]  |Designation of the block             |Bezeichnung des Blocks
                          "TOPO" for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_MESH_TOPOLOGY = topology of mesh, quad elements
                          "NODE" for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_MESH_NODE     = topology of mesh, coordinates of the nodes
                          "ZONE" for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_NEFFZONE      = zones of non effectivity  
                          "MRES" for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_RESULT_MIDD   = result points, quad middles and gauss points
                          "NRES" for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_RESULT_NODE   = result points, node points 
                          "POLY" for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_POLYGON       = result points, node points 
                          the designation of the cut for Type SECT_SUB_TYPE_CUT_MIDD, SECT_SUB_TYPE_CUT_NODE and SECT_SUB_TYPE_CUT_RF
     @4#  nRec    [int]  |Number of following records          |Anzahl der folgenden Records

A section may be defined via a BREP model according to the 30/NR-32/NR
scheme of structures. In that case there exists an independant
cdbase-file containing all needed values. However the basic geometric
data is stored in the master cdbase with the section number. These
records are identical copies of the 30/NR - 32/NR records within an
envelope defining the type of record.


{red}

     @2=  KWL   [int]    |Identification of record key (=NR)
     @3#  IB   *[int]    |buffer of record contents for record KWH/KWL

                            WCS is the international x-y coordinate system. 
                            The default for plane systems is the german convention with z downwards.

                            Types SYST_IPROB_PLANE_GIRDER_PRESTRESS/SYST_IPROB_PLANE_GIRDER_PRESTRESS_WCS (31/35) allow 
                            for a prestress analysis like a general 3D system, with the following restrictions
                            - no z coordinates
                            - all quad elements are enforced "downside"
                            - no support definition / visualisation in the plane
                            - no general loading in the plane
                            These systems may be treated with a SEPP licence
                            (more complex problems require a 3D analysis and ASE)

                            If the database is not correct, than the
                            value is negative and there is added some
                            value to indicate the reason of the error.
                                  IPROB=-(IPROB+1000*N)

     @7:  TG(1,0)  4[-,-,-] |global CDB-System transformation matrix
                             first three values (TGREF(I,0)) are the
                             ordinates of CDB origin with unit 1001
                             next three values (TGREF(I,1)) are the
                             global components of CDB-X-Axis:
                             (I) CDB:
                                 xx = (x-t(1,0))/Det(T)**(1/3)
                                 yy = (y-t(2,0))/Det(T)**(1/3)
                                 zz = (z-t(3,0))/Det(T)**(1/3)
                                 x = t(1,1)*xx + t(2,1)*yy +  t(3,1)*zz
                                 y = t(1,2)*xx + t(2,2)*yy +  t(3,2)*zz
                                 z = t(1,3)*xx + t(2,3)*yy +  t(3,3)*zz
                             (I) WCS:
                                 x = t(1,1)*x + t(1,2)*y + t(1,3)*z + t(1,0)
                                 y = t(2,1)*x + t(2,2)*y + t(2,3)*z + t(2,0)
                                 z = t(3,1)*x + t(3,2)*y + t(3,3)*z + t(3,0)
                             !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
                             ALL COORDINATES AND TRANSFORMATION MATRICES
                             WITHIN THE CDBASE ARE IN CDBASE-COORDINATES
                             !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
                             IF THE WCS (DRAWING) IS IN MM, THIS IS ALSO
                             TREATED VIA THIS TRANSFORMATION MATRIX. THE
                             MATRIX ITSELF IS THEN SCALED BY A FACTOR
                             !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

;    @RecDesc:   10/1  System Design Code
{red}
     @Rec: 010/1:0    SYST_DES | SystemDesignCode                               :V200502
{/red}
     @0=  id       [int]       | identifier = 0
     @1#  idc      [int]       | Design code enumeration
     @2#  country  [int]       | Country code for variants
                                 values >999 are reserved to encode the code enum 
                                 of a national annexe to the Eurocode
     @3#  code     [int]       | main number or ident of code
     @4#  year     [int]       | Year of publication
     @5#  class    [chr]       | classification (see master.ini)
                                 = enum in old ini-files
     @6#  txt      8[chr]      | specific Text of Design code (32 characters)
                                 = name of the INI-file
     @14# wind     [int]       | enum of a wind classification (see master.ini)
                                 = 100*enum of zone + enum of terrain category
     @15# snow     [int]       | enum of a snow-classification (see master.ini)
     @16# seis     [int]       | enum of a seismic-classification (see master.ini)
     @17# gravity  [1202]      | explicit gravity acceleration constant for site
                                 0.0 uses the 10.0 or 9.80665 depending on design code
     @18# altiobs  [1006]      | obsoleted altitude above sea level | Geländehöhe über NN
     @19# vers     [-]         | Version number of INI-File (21.0)
                                 will be set to a negative value if the ini-file
                                 has been modified by the user.
     @20# longitud  [205]      | longitude of location
     @21# latitude  [205]      | latitude of location
     @22# altitude  [1006]     | altitude above sea level 


     attention for versions:
     Version 200501 had only values id to txt(4). Items #20 to #22 added for 2018.
     Length of TXT has been increased in Version 2022 from 16 to 32 characters

     This record contains data derived from the ini-file of the design code
     The specific design code allows the selection of a special subclass
     of design which has other combination values or requirements than the
     standard.

     eg:
          0 / 0  / 2 / 1992 / 0 / '2 (1992)'   = Original EC2-2
          0 / 49 / 2 / 1992 / 0 / '2-2 (1992)' = EC 2 part 2 with
                                                 german boxed values
          1 / 0  / 0     /   0  / 0 / ' '      = any DIN code
          1 / 0  / 1045  / 1978 / 0 / '1045'   = old DIN 1045
          1 / 0  / 1045  / 2001 / 1 / '1045-1' = new DIN 1045-1, Kat. A
          1 / 0  / 18800 / 1993 / 0 / '18800'  = DIN 18800

     We have defined the following enumeration of country
     and design codes (only 0-99 are usable !)

     Corresponds to [Action] section in design code INI-Files:

{red}
     @Rec: 010/1:1    SYST_ACT | Predefined Actions from INI-file               :V200501
                                (identical structure with 014/ID:1)
{/red}
     @0#   id      [int]    | identifier = 1
     @1#   action  [int]    | ID of the real action = type of action
                              enumeration or chr-encoded free literal
                              the category is not attached here!
     @2#   type    [int]    | 16*Part of action + superposition
                              default superposition of the loadcases
                                #0   permanent   (G,P,C)
                                #1   conditional (Q,S,F)
                                #2   exclusive   (L,T and all other)
                                #3   unsigned  conditional (W)
                                #4   unsigned  exclusive   (W?)
                                #5   permanent exclusive   (AG)
                                     e.g. nonlinear loadcases
                                #6   extended  exclusive
                                     the categories exclude each other
                                &8   load cases within an action may
                                     act separately, e.g.
                                #8   permanent individual load cases
                              Type of action
                                #0   default from superposition
                                #1   permanent action G  (SUP 0)
                                #2   prestress        P
                                #3   variable Action  Q  (SUP 1,2,3,4)
                                #4   accidental       A
                                #5   seismic          AE bzw. E
                              +256*number of textid in sofistik.err
     @1:   gamu    [-]      | safety factor unfavourable \
                            | sicherheit ungünstig
     @2:   gamf    [-]      | safety factor favourable \
                            | sicherheit günstig
     @3:   psi0    [-]      | combination value
     @4:   psi1    [-]      | frequent combination value
     @5:   psi2    [-]      | quasi permanent combination value
     @6:   ps1s    [-]      | non frequent combination value psi1'
     @7:   gama    [-]      | safety factor accidential
     @8:   cat     [chr]    | sub category of action
     @9:   txtref  [int]    | designation_enum in SOFISTIK.ERR
     @10:  txt     [str*32] | explicit designation (in native language)

     Corresponds to [ACTIONS] section in design code INI-Files:

       [ACTIONS]
       # idents of possible actions,gamu,gamf,psi0,psi1,psi2,ps1s,gama,@textref
       G=0,1.30,1.00,1.00,1.00,1.00,1.00,@502
       Q=1,1.50,0.00,1.00,1.00,1.00,0.00,@507
       S=1,1.30,0.00,1.00,1.00,1.00,0.50,@510
       W=2,1.50,0.00,0.30,1.00,1.00,0.00,@509

     The textref @510 defines the default text for this action to be read
     from SOFISTIK.ERR-file from where we get the appropriate language.

     Not all types of actions need to be defined. There are default
     actions available according to EC within the library-functions.
     This function SOF_LCACT_INFO(ICTYP,ACT,IER) returns a structure
     of type LC_ACT for any action type ICTYP with the actual defaults.

     As it is an intended definition that psi0 >= psi1' >= psi1 >= psi2
     Values not defined (e.g. psi1) are taken as the next lower value
     (eg. psi2) which is used for the SNIP-Definitions.

     @0#  id       [int]    | identifier = 2

     @2#  extr     [int]    | Combination rule equation to be used

                               #96  freq() (F)  frequent     | GZG häufig
                               #97  nonf() (N)  non frequent | GZG nicht häufig

                               &1   D  displacements and deformations

                               &16  L  Storage Level
                               &32-128  reserved
                               &256    Class-Selector from the General-Section
                                       0 = no selection
