                                       2 = for second class etc.
     @1:   TXT     8[chr]   | Name of combination \
                            | Name der Kombinationsvorschrift
     @9:   flags   [int]    | flags
                               &1   *  first Action in action group ADA must exist
     @10:  ACT[ID,FAKU,FAKF]  31*[chr,-,-]  | Identifier of action
                                            | unfavourable factor
                                            | favourable factor

      ACT since V202412 moved to S_COM_ACT

     For the action there are a few reserved literals allowing a group of actions
         {G}  = all permanent actions
         {P}  = all prestress actions
         {Q1} = 1st leading variable action
         {Q2} = 2nd leading variable action
         {Q3} = 3rd leading variable action
         {QI} = remaining variable actions
         {E}  = all seismic actions
         {A}  = all accidential actions
     For each action there is the possibility to specify a discrete factor or
     to let MAXIMA choose its own if no such coefficient (<0) is defined
     If you want to use a specific factor from the action you may write instead
     of any number a Literal starting with % like
         %gamm, %gamu, %gamf  %gama = safety factors alone [gam-u|gam-f] , gam-u , gam-f, gam-a
         %psi0, %psi1, %psi2, %ps1s = psi values alone
         %psig, %psiu, %psif        = psi0*[gam-u|gam-f] , psi0*gam-u , psi0*gam-f
         %ps1g, %ps1u, %ps1f        = psi1*[gam-u|gam-f] , psi1*gam-u , psi1*gam-f
         %ps2g, %ps2u, %ps2f        = psi2*[gam-u|gam-f] , psi2*gam-u , psi2*gam-f
         %p1sg, %p1su, %p1sf        = ps1s*[gam-u|gam-f] , ps1s*gam-u , ps1s*gam-f

     thus the default DESI for EC is
         (%gamm*{G}+%gamm*{P}+%gamu*{Q1}+%psiu*{QI})
     and for SIA it is
         (%gamm*{G}+%gamm*{P}+%gamu*{Q1}+%psi0*{QI})

     Correspond to 14/NR:0 definitions:
     Correspond to COMB_sections in design code INI-Files:

     [COMB_Service]                # Servicability
     comb_2400=perm(G,Q,S),Titel1  # standard combination type + LC offset
     comb_2300=freq(G,Q,S),Titel2  # standard combination type + LC offset

     [COMB_Design]                 # Design combination
     comb_2100=desi(G,Q,S)         # standard combination type + LC offset

     [COMB_Accident]               # Accidential combination
     comb_2500=acci(G,Q,A)         # standard combination type + LC offset
     comb_2600=acci,1(G+0.5*Q+0.7*A)   # special explicit combination type
     comb_2700=(0.9-1.1)*G+1.3*Q+0.7*A # special explicit combination type

     [COMB_Fatigue]

     [COMB_Stability]

     comb_3100=desiEF,1D(G,Q,L)  # apply for deformations classes E & F
     comb_3200=desi,1S(G,Q,L)    # apply for elementresults with equation 1
     comb_3300=desiAB,2S(G,Q,L)  # elements with equation 2 for classes A & B

     Hint:
     If no factors are defined in the INI-File, both values will be set
     to -1 (=not specified). They have both to be taken from the action
     definition in that case.
     If only one factor is given in the INI-File, it will become the FAKU
     value. The FAKF value will not be set and should then become 1.0 for
     permanent actions (SYST_ACT:type) and zero for all others.
     If two values are given, the first (lower!) value will become FAKF,
     the second (higher!) the FAKU.
     Any definition of an explicit factor will deactivate all PSI-Values
     for that action!

     @3:  FAKF     [-]      | favourable factor

The maximum primary group number is defined as MAXGRP=999.
The records with LC>0 contains also data for all secondary group definitions.
For these definitions, MBW is the internal element number, and MBW+NUM-1 is
then the last of any selected continuous range.

For each group and each element type will exist a record, if elements
are defined. INFO/FAKS are indentical for all elementtypes of a group.
The assignment of an element to an group is done as follows:

10/0:IGDIV > 0
The group number is the integer result of the division of the element
number by the group divisor. The maximum elementnumber is MAXGRP*IGDIV!

   NGRP=NR/IGDIV

10/0:IGDIV = 0
All groups receive an increasing individual base value. An element number
within those intervalls defines the membership to this group.

   BASE(NGRP) <= NR < BASE(NGRP+1)

Record 12/LC is the father of all other loadcase results. Consecutive
records define all load case dependant control information and those
global load definitions independant from the current mesh definition.
The program SOFILOAD converts this loading to appropriate nodal and
elemental loads.

                            #define LC_CURV_KREF_NODAL_SEQUENCE           144  =  Explicit  Nodal sequence (EDGE)
                            #define LC_CURV_KREF_BEAM_GROUP               145  =  Explicit  Group of BEAMs
                            #define LC_CURV_KREF_QUAD_GROUP               146  =  Explicit  Group of QUADs
                            #define LC_CURV_KREF_BRIC_GROUP               147  =  Explicit  Group of BRICs (Surface)
                            #define LC_CURV_KREF_UNCONDITIONAL_AUTOMATIC  148  =  Unconditional automatic references
                            #define LC_CURV_KREF_CONDITIONAL_AUTOMATIC    149  =  Conditional automatic references (e.g. Load-trains)
     @1#  NREF     [int]   |Reference number  | Referenznummer
                            see 12/LC:10? for encoding
                            For nodal sequences, both nodes are saved as node1+65536*node2
     @2#  TREF     3[chr]  |Reference text for eccentricities in sections (12 characters)
     @5#  TYP      [int]   |type of load     | Lastschlüssel
     @6#  TXT      3[chr]  |Identifiying User Text (12 characters)
     @1:  PRZ      [8]     |Percentage of load covered with elements
     @2:  WIDTH    [1001]  |Tolerance load direction to match elements
     @3:  lpt[p,x,y,z]  63[*,1001,1001,1001]   |loadpts

    Load distribution is given by a linear to cubic distribution
    dependant on the number of load definition points. If the load is
    defined with a reference to a line (#111/114) the load values and
    eccentricities will be interpolated relative to that line.
    This allows also to omit all coordinates, then the load is strictly
    bound to the line and this line will be loaded on its total length
    with a constant load value given at @6.

    The load types 111 to 119 describe a polygon load distribution
    while 141 to 149 describe a spline distribution.

     @Rec: 012/LC:199  GLC_GUID  | Unique identifier of loading member 
{/red}
     @0=  ID     [int]      |identifier 199
     @1#  ORIG   [int]      |Origin of load

                             in the BIM/CAD system
     @5#  TAG    [str*32]   |Load tag: Loads can be taged with the GUID record


Load types in the 12/LC Environment follow a new unique scheme defined
by a load type and a load direction as follows:

     ITYP = 100000 * Extra-Bits + 10000 * PROJECTION + 10 * TYPE + DIRECTION

     Extra-Bits
     For LPTS==0 (one load value only):
                  +1  Linear distribution load value at start
                  +2  Linear distribution load value at end
                  +3  Linear distribution load value at mid
                  +5  Quadratic distribution load value at start
                  +6  Quadratic distribution load value at end
                  +7  Quadratic distribution load value at mid
                  +9  Cubic distribution load value at start
                 +10  Cubic distribution load value at end
                        Bit0 = at start,  Bit1 = at end ; Bit0+1 = at mid
                        Bit2 = quadratic, Bit3 = cubic distribution

     %0????   BLIC = ELEM (projected in element)
     %1????   BLIC = XX   (projected in Y-Z)
     %2????   BLIC = YY   (projected in Z-X)
     %3????   BLIC = ZZ   (projected in X-Y)
     %4????   reserved    (projected in load)
     %5????   BLIC = XXL  (projected in Y-Z, sign of load component)
     %6????   BLIC = YYL  (projected in Z-X, sign of load component)
     %7????   BLIC = ZZL  (projected in X-Y, sign of load component)

     %00?     |special factors          |Faktoren
     %01?     |force                    |Kraft
     %02?     |moment                   |Moment
     %03?     |strain or displacement   |Dehnung oder Verschiebung
     %04?     |curvature or rotation    |Krümmung oder Verdrehung
     %05?     |imperfection             |Vorverformung
     %06?     |temperature              |Temperatur
     %07?     |internal prestress       |innere Vorspannung
               by tendons                durch Spannstränge
     %08?     |external beam prestress  |externe Vorspannung Balken
     %09?     |external quad prestress  |externe Vorspannung QUAD
     %10?     |influence areas QUAD     |Einflussflächen      QUAD
     %20?     |multiphysics             |multiphysics

       %0     |default                  |Voreinstellung
               global gravity for forces
               uniform stress/strain/Temperature
       %1     |local  X-axis local ref. |lokale X-Achse lokale Fläche
       %2     |local  Y-axis local ref. |lokale Y-Achse lokale Fläche
       %3     |local  Z-axis local ref. |lokale Z-Achse lokale Fläche

     For mixed type of boundary conditions (WALLS) the fundamental equation
         value = COEF*(H-HREF) = SC - SP*H
     is taken to have a constant value COEF appended as a last load value
     without ordinates to the end of the list, while H is variant with
     time or location.

{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier
                              #10 = additive function
                              #20 = multiplier function
                                    ---
                              #80 = additional function
                              #88 = FFT function
                                    f = [ abs(H(f)), Re(H(f)), Im(H(f)), phase ]
                              #89 = FFT generated PDS
                                    ---
                              #91 = explicit modal displacements in x-direction
                              #92 = explicit modal displacements in y-direction
                              #93 = explicit modal displacements in z-direction
                              #94 = explicit modal rotation      in xx-direction
                              #95 = explicit modal rotation      in yy-direction
                              #96 = explicit modal rotation      in zz-direction
                              #97 = explicit modal displacments  in any direction
                              #99 = direct modal coordinate (phi*m*phi = 1)
                                    i.e. mode i has the factor from the table f(tt)
                              
     @1:  tt       [-]      |Time/frequency/modenumber  | Zeit/Frequenz/Nummer der Eigenform
     @2:  f        7[-]     |function values            | Funktionswerte

     Functions with a base line correction have a set of six values for f
     a-corr,a-orig,v-corr,v-orig,u-corr,u-orig

     Response spectra may have up to five values for different damping values
     This data is preceeded with a record defining the damping values (013/LC:9).
{red}
     @Rec: 013/LC:11    LC_FSIN  | Harmonic function additive                   :V200501
     @Rec: 013/LC:21    LC_FSINM | Harmonic function multiplier                 :V200501
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier
     @1:  T        [90]     |Time/frequency
     @2:  f1       [-]      |Amplitude value
     @3:  phi1     [90]     |phase value
     @4:  tmin     [90]     |starttime
     @5:  tmax     [90]     |stoptime if > starttime
     @6:  s        [-]      |impactfactor
     @7:  f2       [-]      |Amplitude value for T/2 (Fourier)
     @8:  phi2     [90]     |phase value for f2
     @9:  f3       [-]      |Amplitude value for T/3 (Fourier)
     @10: phi3     [90]     |phase value for f3
     @11: f4       [-]      |Amplitude value for T/4 (Fourier)
     @12: phi4     [90]     |phase value for f4

     In general the function is a fourier series defined as follows:

         F = f1*sin((x-phi1)/T)+f2*sin(2*(x-phi2)/T)+...

         x = (t-tmin)

     If the impact factor is not zero, than the function is:

         F = 1 + f1*sin(x-phi1)/T+f2*sin(2*(x-phi2)/T)+ ...

{red}
     @Rec: 013/LC:12    LC_FSTP  | Periodic stepping function additive   :V200501
     @Rec: 013/LC:22    LC_FSTPM | Periodic stepping function multiplier :V200501
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier
     @1:  T        [90]     |Time/frequency
     @2:  f        [-]      |Amplitude value
     @3:  tc       [90]     |contact time
     @4:  tmin     [90]     |starttime
     @5:  tmax     [90]     |stoptime if > starttime
     @6:  s        [-]      |impactfactor (Sailer/Hüttner/Bachmann)
                              < 0.0 = half sine function (bachmann)
                              > 0.0 = Skipping/Running (Sailer)

{red}
     @Rec: 013/LC:13    LC_FINA | Aperiodic function additive           :V201104
     @Rec: 013/LC:23    LC_FINM | Aperiodic function multiplier         :V201104
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier 13
     @1:  T        [90]     |Total Time
     @2:  f        [-]      |Amplitude value
     @3:  t1       [90]     |Time of constant intensity
     @4:  tmin     [90]     |starttime
     @5:  tmax     [90]     |stoptime = tmin+T
     @6:  typ      [chr]    |Type of function
     @7:  f2       [-]      |Amplitude factor
     @8:  t2       [90]     |lead in time duration
     @9:  f3       [-]      |Amplitude factor
     @10: t3       [90]     |lead out time duration

     There are three standard types of intensity functions:

     COMP: tmin < t < tmin+t2      I(t)=F*(t-tmin)/(t2-tmin)**F1
           tmin+t2 < t < tmax-t3   I(t)=F
           tmax-t3 < t < tmax      I(t)=F*exp(-F2*(t-tmax+t3))
     TRAP: tmin < t < tmin+t2      I(t)=F*(t-tmin)/(t2-tmin)
           tmin+t2 < t < tmax-t3   I(t)=F
           tmax-t3 < t < tmax      I(t)=F*(1-(t-tmax+t3)/t3)
     EXPO: tmin < t < tmax         I(t)=F*(exp(-F1*(t-tmin))-exp(-F2*(t-tmin))

     TRAP is a special case of COMP by setting F2=1 / F3=0
     EXPO is a special case of COMP by setting T1=0

{red}
     @Rec: 013/LC:9??   LC_RESW | Response spectra wind                         :V201502
{/red}
     @0#  TYP      [int]    |Type of spectra 900 - 999
                                     with X=f*L/V
                               #900  User defined
                               #901  Karmann Longitudinal
                               #902  Karman lateral/vertical
                               #903  Eurocode EN1991 longitudinal
                               #904  Eurocode EN1991 lateral/vertical
                                     with X=f*z/V (Monin)
                               #910  generic Monin
                               #911  Kaimal/Panofsky
                               #912  Kaimal/Panofsky lateral
                               #913  Kaimal/Panofsky vertical
                               #914  Olesen

     The num may be used to select between different superpositions.
     Each superposition points to at least one set of actions defined
     in the 14/num records. Multiple sets to be used are specified by
     additional records with num=0 and only up to the second value.

     @Rec: 014/NR:2  LC_ACT_LC | loadcase of action                             :V200501 \

     @0#   id    [int]    | ident = 2 / 82

                             #-  Use all load cases of action (only mathing category)

     @2#   type  [int]    | load case action type
                             #-       Add to previous
                             #0       G  = permanent contribution
                             #1       Q  = conditional contribution
                             #2       W  = unfavourable sign contribution
                             #8       PERC = Permanent individual Loadcases
                             #100     AG = permanent mutually exclusive (obsolete will be set to 301)
                             #101-199 Ai = conditional mutually exclusive
                             #201-299 Xi = unfavourable sign mutually exclusive
                             #301-399 Gi = permanent mutually exclusive
     @1#   fact  [-]      | factor

     The load cases to be combined.
     If no such data is defined, MAXIMA may create a default.

     MAXIMA has the following choices:
     - to select all or a subset of the defined actions with IDT>9999
     - to use all loadcases defined within that action or to collect
       all 12/LC with the matching ID and generate a default combination
     - to copy the definitions to an explicit combination with NR<9999
     - to edit the combination freely
     The restrictions applied are:
     - no load case with an action type given may be used in a non-
       matching action.
     - if a programm sets the list of loadcases of an action it has to
       assure the completeness of numbers itself

     ID (>x20202020) is the 4Byte packed unique character of the type
     of an action. If a sub categrory is selected, the ID contains
     ACTIONID_CATID.
     The default actions and their factors are specified within the
     design-code-INI-file (see 10/1) and have the EC-defaults available
     within the program code as follows:

       01  general loading     17  addit. loading      33  special loading
       02  G  dead load        18  ZG dead load        34  SG dead load
       03  G1 dead load 2      19  Z1 dead load 2      35  S1 dead load 2
       04  G2 dead load 2      20  Z2 dead load 2      36  S2 dead load 2
       05  P  prestress        21  ZP prestress        37  SP prestress
       06  C  creep+shrinkage  22  ZC creep+shrinkage  38  SC creep+shrink
       07  Q  variable load    23  ZQ variable load    39  SQ variable load
       08  L  live load        24  ZL braking          40  SL live load
       09  W  wind             25  ZW wind             41  SW wind
       10  S  Snow             26  ZS snow             42  SS snow
       11  R  Earth pressure   27  ZR water pressure   43  SR earth pressure
       12  F  expect. settl    28  ZF reserved         44  SF unexp. settl.
       13  T  temperature      29  ZT temperature      45  ST temperature
       14  A  impact           30  ZA impact           46  SA impact
       15  B  construction     31  ZB resist.supp.     47  SB assembling
       16  E  seismic          32  ZE seismic          48  SE seismic

     There are two functions available (CDBLF.F90):

         INTEGER FUNCTION LF_TYPE_ENUM(IDACT)   returns the internal
                                                table no (1:255 / chr)
         INTEGER FUNCTION ACT_TYPE_ENUM(IDACT)  returns the action no from
                                                the table above or chr

     Each load case defined within an action may be defined with
     individual factors (which may become the default-values of this
     action.) They are encoded at the 12/LC via SOFILOAD and
     simultaneously initializes a 14/ID if not already done.

     Thus 10/1/1 contains the possible actions, while 14/ID contains
     the selected or defined actions within the current project. This
     record is automatically created via call to (CDBLF.F90):

         INTEGER FUNCTION INIT_CDB_ACT(IDACT,ACT,
     &                                 NEWVAL,NEWTXT,NEWTYP,ICDB)

         SUBROUTINE CDB_ACT_INFO(IDACT,ACT,IER)

     @Rec: 016/0:0    PERF_CAT | Definition of performance categories (=sets of performance criteria)               :V20231222
{/red}
     @0=  id      [int]    |record identifier 
     @1#  etyp    [int]    |element type, for which the criteria applies 
                              #define PERF_CRT_ETYP_LNK             173    element type link/spring/hinge
     @2#  cat     [chr]    |performance category identifier, arbitrary 4-character string
                            predefined categories:
                               #define PERF_CAT_UNSPEC           0     general set of performance criteria
                               (TBD:   PERF_CAT_IDL       0x49444c     = 'IDL'     performance criteria for idealized shape determination)
     @3#  unused 3[int]    |unused
     @1:  title   [str*32] |Designation of category

     #define MAX_PERF_CAT    5   = maximum number of performance categories


{red}
     @Rec: 016/0:1    PERF_CRT | Definition of performance criterion                                                :V20231222
{/red}
     @0=  id      [int]    |record identifier 
     @1#  etyp    [int]    |element type, record identifier PERF_CRT_ETYP_LNK = 173
     @2#  setno   [int]    |set number, unused = 0 
     @3#  cat     [chr]    |performance category, cf. PERF_CAT
                            All criteria labels within a category form a hierarchical sequence.
     @4#  crt     [chr]    |short label of criterion (4-character string), e.g., 'OLE'
     @5#  unused  [int]    |unused
   
     @1:  pidx    [-]      |performance index (ascending magnitude denotes increasing severity)
     @2:  title   [str*32] |Designation of criterion


     Performance criteria, general remarks:
     --------------------------------------
     Performance criteria are grouped by category (-> PERF_CAT). 

     Within each category, a performance criterion is identified by a short label and an associated 
     unique performance index (-> PERF_CRT). 
     
     Within each category, performance labels form a hierarchical sequence. This, e.g., allows for 
     differentiation between, e.g., OLE limit concrete and OLE limit reinforcement.

     Performance criteria of different categories are not related.
          
     The constituting strain thresholds for the criteria within the respective categories 
     are defined separately for each link/spring/hinge element. They are are stored per material number 
     in a subsequent record or subsequent records (in case there is more than one material) (-> PLIM_LNK).

     Within each category, performance criteria form a hierarchy. They are ordered by severity, 
     indicated by magnitude of the performance index. CRIT2 being more severe than CRIT1 is indicated by:
     a) |CRIT2.pidx| > |CRIT1.pidx| 
     
     This implies (-> sanity check) that for ALL [lsc,lst] WHERE [lsc,lst] /= 0.0:
     b) |CRIT2.lsc| >= |CRIT1.lsc| !
         CRIT2.lst  >=  CRIT1.lst  !


{red}
     @Rec: 016/0:173    PLIM_LNK | Definition of link/spring/hinge element performance thresholds (limit strains).  :V20231222
                                 | Attributive set of limit strains for preceding performance criterion PERF_CRT.
{/red}
     @0=  etyp    [int]    |element type, record identifier PERF_CRT_ETYP_LNK = 173
     @1#  wlno    [int]    |work law number Rec: 173/NR:+  SPRI_WL
     @2#  cat     [chr]    |performance category, cf. PERF_CAT
     @3#  crt     [chr]    |short label of criterion (4-character string), cf. PERF_CRT
     @4#  mno     [int]    |material number, for which provided threshold strains strains apply
                            (mno == 0, only for PLIM_LNK_LSTYP_HNG_ROT and PLIM_LNK_LSTYP_HNG_DISP)
     @5#  lstyp   [int]    |type of limit:
                              #define PLIM_LNK_LSTYP_STRAIN     1  = B0 = strain threshold values
                              #define PLIM_LNK_LSTYP_ROT        2  = B1 = hinge rotation threshold values
                              #define PLIM_LNK_LSTYP_DISP       4  = B2 = hinge displacement threshold values
   
     @1:  lsc     [1081]   |Compressive limit strain (< 0.0)
     @2:  lst     [1081]   |Tensile limit strain (> 0.0)
                            (unit for limtyp PLIM_LNK_LIMTYP_ROT: 1004)
                            (unit for limtyp PLIM_LNK_LIMTYP_DISP: 1003)

                            Entries with value 0.0 signal "no limit specified".

     @1:  pidxmx  [-]      |max performance index

  ****  ****  ****                    {link}158{-link}20/* Nodes{/link}
  *  *  *  *  *  *                    {link}159{-link}21/* Kinematic constraints{/link}
  *  *     *  *  *                    {link}160{-link}23/* Nodal loads{/link}
  *  *  ****  *  *                    {link}161{-link}24/* Nodal results{/link}
  *  *  *     *  *                    {link}161{-link}25/* Dynamic nodal results{/link}
  *  *  *     *  *                    {link}161{-link}26/* Nonlinear nodal results{/link}
  ****  ****  ****                    {link}161{-link}27/* Nodal coordinate offsets{/link}
                                      {link}162{-link}29/* Nodal scalar physical values{/link}
;    @RecDesc:   20/0         Nodes 
{red}
     @Rec: 020/00   NODE  | Nodes                                               :V200501
{/red}


     @0=  NR       [int]    | node-number         |Knotennummer
     @1#  INR      [int]    |internal node-number |interne Knotennummer
                              #0 = node not active
     @2#  KFIX     [int]    |degree of freedoms   |Freiheitsgrade
                              old definition:                            #0  |all fixed         |Alle festgehalten
                              #define NODE_KFIX_UX                  1 = Bit0  |displacement uX   |Verschiebung uX
                              #define NODE_KFIX_UY                  2 = Bit1  |displacement uY   |Verschiebung uY
                              #define NODE_KFIX_UZ                  4 = Bit2  |displacement uZ   |Verschiebung uZ
                              #define NODE_KFIX_PHIX                8 = Bit3  |rotation PHIX     |Verdrehung PHIX
                              #define NODE_KFIX_PHIY               16 = Bit4  |rotation PHIY     |Verdrehung PHIY
                              #define NODE_KFIX_PHIZ               32 = Bit5  |rotation PHIZ     |Verdrehung PHIZ
                              #define NODE_KFIX_PHIW               64 = Bit6  |twisting dPHIx/dx |Verwindung dPHIX/dx
                              #define NODE_KFIX_SPLIT_BEAM        128 = Bit7  |split continuous beams flag
                              #define NODE_KFIX_U_SUPPRESSED      256 = Bit8  |ux-uy-uz  may be suppressed
                              #define NODE_KFIX_PHI_SUPPRESSED    512 = Bit9  |phix-phiz may be suppressed
                              #define NODE_KFIX_WARP_SUPPRESSED  1024 = Bit10 |warping   may be suppressed
     @3#  NCOD     [int]    |additional bit code   |Zusatz bit code
                              #define NODE_NCOD_EXPLICIT            1 = Bit0  node is explicitly defined
                                                                        Bit1  not used 
                              #define NODE_NCOD_USED_INTERFACE      4 = Bit2  node is used / is interface
                                                                        Bit3  not used 
                              #define NODE_NCOD_ELASTIC_SUPPORT    16 = Bit4  node has elastic support
                              #define NODE_NCOD_GENERAL_KINE       32 = Bit5  node has a general KINE (hanging node)
                              #define NODE_NCOD_LOCATED_TYPE       64 = Bit6  &64*n node is located on ident nn of type
                                 #define NODE_NCOD_LOCATED_ON_POINT    0 =    node is located on ident nn of type point  (30/NN)
                                 #define NODE_NCOD_LOCATED_ON_LINE     1 =    node is located on ident nn of type line   (31/NN)
                                 #define NODE_NCOD_LOCATED_ON_REGION   2 =    node is located on ident nn of type region (32/NN)
                                 #define NODE_NCOD_LOCATED_ON_VOLUME   3 =    node is located on ident nn of type volume (33/NN)
                              #define NODE_NCOD_LOCATED_IDENT     256 = Bit8  &256*NN  (identification number)
     @1:  XYZ      3[1001]  |X-Y-Z-ordinates    |XYZ-Ordinaten

     Nodes may have any external number, but are in an internal
     sequence defining an optimum bandwidth. The internal number is
     used only in this record. All element nodes or other references
     are on global numbers. So you have to use one or two arrays
     defining the mapping of internal to external nodes:

       INR(MKNOT)  defines the internal number of a node II=INR(NR)
       INRE(NKNOT) defines the reverse mapping, i.e NR=INRE(II)

     Examples: XYZ(IK(i),1:3)  are the coordinates for node i

               DO N=1,MKNOT
               IF(INR(N).NE.0) THEN
                 perform operations on node n in sorted order
               ENDIF
               ENDDO

     Each node derived from a geometric point 32/NR has the external
     number NR.
     For SOFIMESH meshes all nodes being part of the structural mesh
     have the NCOD&2 Bit. For result meshes for p-elements the internal
     nodes do not have this bit and NN is equal the element number
     they are derived from.

                            number of subdomains given by recordlength

     @Rec:: 020/100:-  |subdomains
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier -1
     @1#  KWEL    *[int]    |weight of elements for each subdomain
                            This is the second record !


{red}
     @Rec:: 020/100:+ |nodes of subdomains
{/red}
     @0=  N          [int]         |node-number
     @1#  IK[nd,nn]  *[int,int]    |list of internal node numbers for
                                   each subdomain
                                   IK(1,I) = domain number
                                   IK(2,I) = internal node number


     For each node a complete list of subdomains is provided,
     giving the internal (optimal) node number of each subdomain.
     It is possible to have the same internal node number for all
     subdomains as a first guess.

     Following rules may be derived from this information.

     - Interface nodes belong to more than one subdomain
       Loads on those nodes may be evenly distributed or
       associated only to the highest or lowest subdomain.
     - An element belongs to a subdomain if all of its nodes
       belong to that subdomain and if at least one node
       does not belong to a higher subdomain. The latter
       insures that elements with all nodes on the interface
       are treated only once.

{red}
     @Rec:: 020/n02  |Equation-numbers subdomain n
{/red}
     @0#  ID(NKNOT,NDOF)  *[int]  internal equation numbers


     The number of the current subdomain may be investigated by
     LOGLU(1037) or SOF_FGET_CTRL(CTRL_PVM,II). The values are

       0 = serial solution process
      -1 = pvm master
      >0 = number of subdomain

{red}
     @Rec:  023/LC:*:*     NODE_L |Nodal_loads                                     :V200601
{/red}
     @0=  NR       [int]    |node-number | Knotennummer
                             #- = internal generated nodal loads
                                  (obsoleted e.g. RLAS, BLAS,...)
     @1#  TYP      [int]    |type of load | Lasttyp
                             #define NODE_L_TYP_NODAL_LOAD 0 = nodal loads
                             The nodal loads are the final step for every load definition
                             thus depending on the task not all loads should be used
                             +10000 for user generated loads
                                    the data base does NOT contain the load definition
                                    but a condensed print should not show this data
                             +20000 for program generated loads
                                    the data base contains the load definition in 12/LC
                                    so a print with ECHO EXTR is optional
                             +30000 for program generated loads
                                    the data base contains the load definition in 
                                    selfweight or other elemental beam/quad loads
                                    so a print or any use other than for WINGRAF or 
                                    MASS generation or loading only with 23/LC is not correct.
                             +?9999 is a synonym for 30000
     @1:  Px       [1190]   |single force X-component  |Einzellast X-Komponente
     @2:  Py       [1190]   |single force Y-component  |Einzellast Y-Komponente
     @3:  Pz       [1190]   |single force Z-component  |Einzellast Z-Komponente
     @4:  Mx       [1194]   |single moment X-component |Einzelmoment X-Komponente
     @5:  My       [1194]   |single moment Y-component |Einzelmoment Y-Komponente
     @6:  Mz       [1194]   |single moment Z-component |Einzelmoment Z-Komponente
     @7:  Mb       [1195]   |warping moment            |Wölbmoment


For axial symmetric systems all nodal load definitions are intended to
be in [kN/m] or [kNm/m], and will be directly converted to [kN] and
[kNm] by the input routines by multiplying with the radius.

Attention: Nodal load records may not always be stored at full size. E.g., if only force components 
are given, the zero moment components (@4 to @7) may be omitted (SOFiLOAD).

STRUCTURAL - Elements


These structural elements (30/NR to 33/NR) are a BREP model for any type
of structure. They can be used as definition of a finite element mesh and
as the contour of a cross section. Properties may vary between different
usages.

We provide also sequential streams (39/NR) to describe structural data
in a raw format as it is encountered in most CAD applications (AutoCAD,
Revit, Rhinoceros). Points and curves are specified with coordinates
only and the mesh generator has to detect the coincidences itself.

If the user wants to specify a boundary condition to a part of an
edge he defines just a coinciding part of that edge with that
boundary condition. The mesh generator will then split the edge
accordingly and assign the properties to the selected part of the
edge.

However in some cases (e.g. duplicate elements at the same location)
the user may wish to assign numbers to selected elements, therefor
the format of these streams allow both types of definitions, but the
resulting structural elements will allways have a BREP identification.

There is no special predefined key for those streams, neither the
KWH (we assume 39 however) nor the second identifier NR. The latter
may be used to separate different layers or types, but the data
definition is intended to allow all data in a single key.

First we have headder records (10,100,101,200,300) which differ from
the corresponding data in 30/31/32/33. They may be define multiple times
overriding or accumulating their definitions.

Then we have special records for every coordinate with a single digit
identifier, specifying the type of that point. All Coordinate data
follows the element where it is used.

All the other keys differ only in the first ID to the 30-33 keys.


    000   a structural point                    conv to 30/NR:0
    0??   extended data for a structural point  maps to 30/NR:??
    100   a structural line                     conv to 31/NR:0
    1??   extended data for a structural line   maps to 31/NR:??
    200   a structural area                     maps to 32/NR:0
    2??   extended data for a structural area   maps to 32/NR:??
    300   a structural volume                   maps to 33/NR:0
    3??   extended data for a structural volume maps to 33/NR:??

The orientation of local coordinate systems is controlled by a structure
of an integer identifier KR, a direction vector DIR(3) and a rotation
along the standard orientation DROT.

The identifier KR is encoded as

    KR = 32*ITRAX_NREF + ITRAX_DROT + ITRAX_ORIENT + ITRAX_VAL

    If ITRAX_NREF > 0 then
       ITRAX_ORIENT=
                                                  1 = orientation of local x-axis 
                                                  2 = orientation of local y-axis
                                                      (not implemented)
       ITRAX_VAL=
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_NODE       0 = reference number is a node
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_LINE       4 = reference number is a line
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_AREA       8 = reference number is an area
    ELSE
       ITRAX_VAL=
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_NONE       0 = not specified (use TUP-vector)
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_YZ         1 = horizontal y of yz-plane
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_ZX         2 = horizontal z of zx-plane
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_XY         3 = horizontal x of xy-plane
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_ZY         4 = horizontal z of zy-plane
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_XZ         5 = horizontal x of xz-plane
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_YX         6 = horizontal y of yx-plane
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_POSX       7 = vertical by pos x-component
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_POSY       8 = vertical by pos y-component
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_POSZ       9 = vertical by pos z-component
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_NEGX      10 = vertical by neg x-component
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_NEGY      11 = vertical by neg y-component
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_NEGZ      12 = vertical by neg z-component

       ITRAX_ORIENT = 
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_RADI      13 = radial direction
                                                      TAL = LOCAL X (QUAD) = LOCAL Y (BEAM)
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_TANG      14 = tangential direction
                                                      TAL = LOCAL Y (QUAD) = LOCAL Z (BEAMS)
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_STRU      15 = inherit from base geometry (e.g. surface isolines)
    ENDIF

    
        ITRAX_DROT =
                     #define GEO_ITRAX_DROT      16 = Rotation is defined

     @Rec: 039/NR:102  SLN_SUPP | Support of Structural lines                   :V201905
     @Rec: 031/NR:102  GLN_SUPP | Support of Structural lines                   :V201905
{/red}

     @0=  ID       [int]    |identifier 102
     @1#  IDS      [int]    | referenced structural element type / macro generation command
                              #0  reference to fixed support
                              #1  reference to a SPT point 30/REF
                              #2  reference to a SLN line  31/REF
                              #3  free (ggf. reference to a SAR line 32/REF)

                              #5  create a parallel coupled line pos. y-direction (right)
                              #6  create a parallel coupled line neg. y-direction (left)
                              #7  create a parallel coupled line in both directions

                              &8  determine material number automatically
                                  from adjacent regions (IDS={5,6,7})
                              &16  The X-Orientation is in reverse direction

                              enforce generation of one of the following element types
                              &128*#1 spring elements
                              &128*#2 boundary elements
                              &128*#3 interface elements
                              defaults to spring/boundary element, determined automatically if nothing specified

     @2#  REF      [int]    |reference identifier
     @3#  NoG      [int]    |number of group
     @4#  NoM      [int]    |number of material
     @5#  IBC      [int]    |Boundary condition / kinematic constraints
                                >0 to be suppressed (added)
                                <0 to be released (subtracted)
                                &1    = global displacement vx
                                &2    = global displacement vy
                                &4    = global displacement vz
                                &8    = global rotation rx
                                &16   = global rotation ry
                                &32   = global rotation rz
                                &64   = warping  wz
                                &128  = local displacement vx
                                &256  = local displacement vy
                                &512  = local displacement vz
                                &1024 = local rotation rx
                                &2048 = local rotation ry
                                &4096 = local rotation rz
                              Only for constraints on a point PT[0]=-1:
                                KP       7 +
                                KPEX  =  7 + 1*8192
                                KPEY  =  7 + 2*8192
                                KPEZ  =  7 + 3*8192
                                KF    = 63 +
                                KFEX  = 63 + 1*8192
                                KFEY  = 63 + 2*8192
                                KFEZ  = 63 + 3*8192
                              Special constraints witout considering a lever arm
                              May violate the equilibrium of moments!
                                KPX0  =  1 + 100000
                                KPY0  =  2 + 100000
                                KPZ0  =  3 + 100000

     @6#  KR       [int]    |local orientation
                             see GEO_ITRAX at top of this page
     @0:  W        [1001]   |width of support     |Stützbreite
     @1:  CA       [1096]   |axial     bedding    |axiale   Bettung
     @2:  CQ       [1096]   |lateral   bedding    |laterale Bettung
     @3:  CM       [1099]   |torsional bedding    |torsions Bettung
     @4:  DRX      [-]      |explicit X direction of support
     @5:  DRY      [-]      |explicit Y direction of support
     @6:  DRZ      [-]      |explicit Z direction of support
     @7:  D        [1001]   |distance to coupled line (IDS={5,6,7})
     @8:  R8       [-]
     @9:  R9       [-]
     @10: FKA      [-]      |factor bedding at start
     @11: FKE      [-]      |factor bedding at end
     @12: TROT     [-]      |Fractional rotation about local x-axis
                             (1.0 = 360 degrees)
     @13: TAL     3[-]      |Vector to be aligned as local z-axis
                             of the local coordinate system (KR)
                             should be set for any radial/tangential
                             reference.
     @14: GUID     [chr*16] |Optional GUID of the support element, if different to
                             general GUID of structural line given at SLN_GUID (39/NR:999)

     This record defines an independant local coordinate system to describe
     the local boundary conditions. The direction of the spring elements
     is governed by rules applied in the following order:

     1. If DRX,DRY,DRZ are set, this direction will be used as explicit direction
        (i.e. the direction remains constant also on curved members)
     2. If KR is given, the records KR,TAL and TROT define a local coordinate
        System along which the supports are aligned. This coordinate system may
        vary along a curved member (see GEO_ITRAX for a description)

     2a) contrary to the description at GEO_ITRAX values of KR={13.14.15}
         have different meanings:
         KR = 13: supports are oriented along the 2nd coordinate axis (LOCY)
         KR = 14: supports are oriented along the 3rd coordinate axis (LOCZ)
         KR = 15: supports are oriented along the 1st coordinate axis (LOCX)
     3. If no direction is given at all, the direction of referenced nodes is taken
     4. If no reference is given, the local x-axis of the structural line is taken

     Any positive value at CA to CM will be taken as explicit value
     for the linear bedding in kN/m/m od kNm/m/rad. If a material
     is defined the constants will be preset from the material constants
     (Explicit bedding constants overrule the value taken from the material
     constants divided by the distance between the lines. In both cases the
     bedding is multiplied with the width of the support)

     This record may be given multiple times (up to 15 instances supported).
     It is also used to describe a reference of a mesh subdivision only
     (where IBC==0,CA:CM=0.0)

                             in the BIM/CAD system

     Remarks:

     Guid("F9168C5E-CEB2-4faa-B6BF-329BF39FA1E4") may be transfered into a
     16-element byte array that contains the value of the GUID.
     [Visual Basic]            Public Function ToByteArray() AByte()
     [C#]                      public byte[] ToByteArray();
     [C++]                     public unsigned char ToByteArray()  __gc[];
     [JScript]                 public function ToByteArray() Byte[];


     An Example of a simple area with some precribed data will be

       :0    a point
       :11   other properties of that same point (e.g. kinematic constraints)
       :0    another point
       :12   other properties of that same point (e.g. kinematic constraints)
       :100  properties of line SLN2
       :91   start point of line SLN2
       :91   intermediate control points
       :91   intermediate control points
       :91   intermediate control points
       :91   end   point of line SLN2
       :200  properties of the area
       :201  properties of the edge 1
       :91   start point of edge
       :91   intermediate control points
       :91   intermediate control points
       :91   intermediate control points
       :91   end   point of edge
       :201  properties of the edge 2
       :91   start point of edge             (may be omitted by a direct
       :91   intermediate control points      reference to :100:GLN2 )
       :91   end   point of edge
       :201  properties of the edge 3
       :91   start point of edge 3
       :91   end   point of edge 3
       :201  properties of the edge 4
       :91   start point of edge 4
       :91   end   point of edge 4

     So we have to continue reading until we find a different type of object
     and have to collect all data of that object before finalizing.
     The other suggestion to preceed with the geometry has the advantage of
     collecting and proceeding data in smaller units, but is more confusing
     in the data processing.

    The local coordinate system of a point has some constraints if the
    point is a column within the interior of a region. In that case the
    local z-axis of the point and the local z-axis of the plane must
    coincide.
    Generated points of interior interface layers (Cnf 32/NR) have NR
    > 1000 and the special TEXT "INTREF".

     A record 030/NR:1 with thickness @4:T=0.0 activates the creation of
     mesh macros for the given point. It will be ignored otherwise.
     The dimension of the column heads, voutes and punching periphery
     may be defined

       - by a rectangular centered equivalent section x * y
       - by a general cross section defined via a record 9/NR
         in this case it is possible to define eccentric arbitrary
         geometry and for the punching section parts of the periphery
         as non effective, but an eqivalent X and Y width is needed
         in that case too.
       - The thickness in record 030/NR:2 describes the maximum thickness
         of the voute in the interior

     This record describes a foundation connected to the strcutural point. All parameters refer to a 
     local coordinate system which is placed in the center of the upper face of the foundation.
     Its z-axis points  downward in gravity direction towards the lower face of the foundation.
     This coordinate system is independant from the coordinate system of the structural point the foundation 
     is connected to.
     The offset of the foundations coordinate system to the structural points coordinate system is defined
     by the eccentricities EX,EY and EZ.

     @0#  ILN      [int]    |Code of geometry | Geometrieschlüssel

; & F-INCLUDE ! COMPATIBLE EFFECTIVE SHORTER LENGTH OF STRUCTURE
; & F-INCLUDE ! LEN_C3101_BUF AT LEAST LEN_CGLN_GEO+1
; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: LEN_C3101_BUF = 256   ! BUFFERLENGTH
; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: LEN_C3101     = 1+21  ! MINLENGTH
; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: MAX_C3101     = 64    ! MAX NO OF SEGMENTS

    These records are parameter-curves of projected arc length s.
    Any curve may have multiple segments even with sharp bends.

    There are different types of curves for ILN==1.

    0. If GPG=GPA=0.0, then a linear geometry is used.
    1. If GPG<>0.0, but GPA=0.0, then a curve is defined in the plane
       defined by the derivatives of the curve at start and the direct
       axis.
    2. If both GPG and GPA are different from zero, than we have a
       3D curve. For IG=1,2 a separate description for the plan view
       and elevation is considered. In this case DD is the projected
       arclength in the xy-plane. 3D splines are treated by independant
       interpolation for all three coordinates. GPG and GPA have no
       distinct meaning in the case of IG=3.

    The local coordinate system has the x-axis along the curve and
    the distance-axis oriented in the horizontal global x-y plane.
    The local y-axis is intended to be within the smoothing plane
    of the curve, but this may be overwritten with a distinct
    optional normal vector for the total curve defined via code "9"
    BEFORE the other geometric data. This vector defines a component
    in the downward direction in values DXYZ1. DD has to be zero and
    S1=S2 for that item. The orientation of the local coordinate
    system which might depend  on other constraints is then selected
    by GLN_GEO_DWN_???? values in GPG.

    Full circles may be described via a code "10" which has as
    the center of the circle at XYZ1 and the vector DXYZ1 as the
    normal to the plane with Norm of the radius. For the easier
    treatement with other programs the description with at least
    two arcs has to be given as well.

    Bezier and Nurbs curves have evenly spaced control points
    attached to the record in CTRLPT. The default are clamped
    conditions and uniform nodes between S1 and S2.
    Nonuniform knots or unclamped conditions have to be defined
    via multiple records with control-points. They are collected
    for the total defined geometry.
    e.g.  RECORD  1  S1 = 0.0 S2 = 1.0  contains at least 2 points
                                        up to the multiplicity+1
          RECORD  2  S1 = 1.0 S2 = 2.0  one point at S2=2.0
                                        two points at S2=1.0/2.0
                                        >2  points at even intervalls
    e.g.  RECORD  1  S1 = 0.0 S2 = 1.0  containing all points for
                                        even knot spacing will create
                                        default multiplicities.

    For geometric operations it is also recommended to create
    multiple records between each zero curvature points.
    For rotating local axes along the curve, ILN==7 has to be used.

     or all midpoints may be supressed.

     Restrictions for constraints with ID==3:
     All prescribed points or lines must be within the region, they
     are not allowed to intersect each other or any boundary of the
     region.

     Constraints subdividing the region in subregions (soil layers)
     with ID==4 will define the property value MAT to be assigned
     to all elements on the left side of the constraining polygon.
     Those elements may intersect other lines.

     For a single point (NB==0) NG defines the edge to which the point
     should be connected if it is close to an edge. If it is also
     close to an point of the boundary, NM defines this point.
     If NM == NA this is used for the special case that we want to
     prescribe a thicknessvalue for a single boundary point.
     The local coordinate system of single points should be in such
     an orientation that the local z-axis coincides with those of
     the region where it belongs to.

{red}
     @Rec: 032/NR:10  GAR_GEO | Geometry of surface                             :V200501
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]    |Identification of surface description 10
     @1#  NG      [int]    |Type of surface representation
                            >0 = surface of revolution with meridian curve NG
                                  #999999 = half Sphere with Radius PAR(13)
                                  #999998 = Cylinder with Radius PAR(13)
                             0 = nearly flat plane with z=f(s,t)
                            -1 = surface mesh
                            -2 = surface grid
                            -3 = bicubic B-splines m x n grid
                            -4 = bilinear coons patch (see 32/12)
                            -5 = bicubic  coons patch (see 32/12)
                            -6 = yet annother coon (reserved)
                            -7 = NURBS-surface non rational
                            -8 = NURBS-surface rational (with weights)
     @2#  mgri    [int]    |number of data/control points in s of mesh
     @3#  ngri    [int]    |number of data/control points in t of mesh
     @4#  mspl    [int]    |degree of B-spline in s direction
                            >mgri = obsoleted FITPACK data with
                                    multiplicity of nodes = 4
     @5#  nspl    [int]    |degree of B-spline in t direction
                            >ngri = obsoleted FITPACK data with
                                    multiplicity of nodes = 4
     @1:  SX      [-]      |plane  direction sx  |Flächenrichtung sx
     @2:  SY      [-]      |plane  direction sy  |Flächenrichtung sy
     @3:  SZ      [-]      |plane  direction sz  |Flächenrichtung sz
     @4:  TX      [-]      |plane  direction tx  |Flächenrichtung tx
     @5:  TY      [-]      |plane  direction ty  |Flächenrichtung ty
     @6:  TZ      [-]      |plane  direction tz  |Flächenrichtung tz
     @7:  NX      [-]      |normal direction nx  |Normalenrichtung nx
     @8:  NY      [-]      |normal direction ny  |Normalenrichtung ny
     @9:  NZ      [-]      |normal direction nz  |Normalenrichtung nz
    @10:  X       [1001]   |X-ordinate Origin    |Koordinate X Ref-P
    @11:  Y       [1001]   |Y-ordinate Origin    |Koordinate Y Ref-P
    @12:  Z       [1001]   |Z-ordinate Origin    |Koordinate Z Ref-P
    @13:  PAR(0)  16[-]    |additional Parameters|Zus. Parameter
    @27:  BOX 3[1001,1001] |boundig box xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,zmin,zmax
    @33:  XPAR    *[-]     |extended parameters  |Zus. Parameter
                            see C3210

    The default of all surfaces is a flat geometry with a least square
    approximation of order 2 of the deviations from that geometry. If
    the boundary has exactly four edges, which are not straight,
    a bilinear coons patch will be selected however.

    The local right-handed coordinate system of the surface is given
    with the s-t axis within the plane and the n-axis normal on the
    surface towards the viewer if the outer boundary is seen
    counter-clockwise. While for B-Splines and coons patches the s
    and t directions are clearly defined, there are especially in 3D
    variant ways of selecting the arbitrary s-axis of a plane:

    A default flat plane system will be established for all types of
    geometry, as it supplies a good starting point for the inverse
    operation of finding a point on the surface.
       itra = 0     The largest eigenvalue of the geometric inertia
       itra = 1     align local s to be within the global yz-plane
                    with the least deviation to the y-axis
       itra = 2     align local s to be within the global zx-plane
                    with the least deviation to the z-axis
       itra = 3     align local s to be within the global xy-plane
                    with the least deviation to the x-axis
       itra = 4     align local s to be within the global yz-plane
                    with the least deviation to the z-axis
       itra = 5     align local s to be within the global zx-plane
                    with the least deviation to the x-axis
       itra = 6     align local s to be within the global xy-plane
                    with the least deviation to the y-axis
       itra = 7     align local s to be in the direction of pos X
       itra = 8     align local s to be in the direction of pos Y
       itra = 9     align local s to be in the direction of pos Z
       itra = 10    align local s to be in the direction of neg X
       itra = 11    align local s to be in the direction of neg Y
       itra = 12    align local s to be in the direction of neg Z
       itra = 13    align s radial with given vector TALNX-TALNZ
       itra = 14    align s tangential with vector TALNX-TALNZ

    The local coordinate system of the QUAD-elements derived herefrom
    will be with the local z-axis from the viewer in the negative n-
    direction, while the local x-axis is identical to the surface
    or aligned to the global coordinate system as given in 32/NR:0.

    The geometry may be also defined by a curve rotating about a local
    axis (sx,sy,sz). s is then the meridian direction, t the tangent
    and n the inward normal direction.

    For more general cases a set of points on the surface is defined.
    They describe a regular M x N  grid of  points to be used for bi-
    cubic splines or similar functions (Nurbs etc).

    Parameters are defined as follows:
       (0)    =  TOTAL AREA IN PROJECTION
       (1:2)  =  uMIN,uMAX   maximum and minimum parameters
       (3:4)  =  vMIN,vMAX   maximum and minimum parameters
       (5:6)  =  hMIN,hMAX   maximum and minimum elevation
                             = maxmin of radii for revolution areas
       (7:8)  =  TMIN,TMAX   maximum and minimum thickness

                 For planar and least square regions there are:
       (9:15) =    coefficients of least square

                 For rotational surfaces there are:
       (11)   =    sfak  scaling factor from plane to meridian
                         s = sfak*u / s=sfak*R
       (12)   =    cfak  mapping paramater
                           0.0 = cylindrical projection
                          >0.0 = conical projection (angle of cone)
       (13)   =    rmax  scaling from t-value to real world
                          fixed radius for cylinder / spheres
      (14:15) =    cos(cfak),sin(cfak)

       BOX(2,3)  Bounding box of surface in 3D

       XPAR   =  SPLINE GRID AND COEFFICIENTS (C3210-Structure/CPLANE.FOR)
                 REAL    TU(MAXNNP_3210) = knots in s direction
                         TV(MAXNNP_3210) = knots in t direction
                         CSPL(MAXCSP_3210) = control points
                         Fitpackformat   : sgrid(ngri,mgri,4)
                                           index i=1:4 for x,y,z,t
                         opennurbsformat : sgrid(4,ngri,mgri),tgrid(ngri,mgri)
                                           index i=1:4 for x,y,z,weight

     ATTENTION!
     This record will be generated automatically by SOF_FLIB_GARINIT
     Only for rotational surfaces or imported special nonuniform nurbs
     a definition by another program is allowed and recommended.
     HINT:
     As the generic surface routines do not know about a global system
     definition or reference nodes, only itra = 1 to 14 are usable for
     the area itself. However the user might establish a default system
     and save the local x-components at 32/NR:0 which will be also used
     as default alignement for all cases with relative orientations.
     Entries itradef*32+15 are used to establish a default orientation
     for planar systems while keeping SURF for curved surfaces.

; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: MAXDEG_3210=32  ! MAX OF DEGREE
; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: MAXGRD_3210=64  ! MAX OF GRID-POINTS
; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: MAXNNP_3210=128 ! GRID+2*(DEG-1)
; & F-INCLUDE       INTEGER, PARAMETER :: MAXCSP_3210=5*(MAXGRD_3210)**2
; + F-INCLUDE

      TYPE C3210   ! 32/NR:10-AREA DEFINITION
           SEQUENCE
           INTEGER IAG(0:5)
           REAL    TA(3,4),PAR(0:15),BOX(2,3)
           REAL    TU(MAXNNP_3210),TV(MAXNNP_3210),CSPL(MAXCSP_3210)
      END TYPE
      INTEGER, PARAMETER :: LEN_C3210=6+34 ! MIN.LENGTH OF C3200

{red}
     @Rec: 032/NR:11    GAR_SURF | UserPointonSurface                           :V200501
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]    |Identification of user surface description 11
     @1#  it      [int]    |Type of point
                             -2 = element of unstructured mesh
                                  having nodes: @2# NODE 4[int]
                             -1 = node of an unstructured mesh
                                  or scattered data point
                              0 = generated surface mesh
                              1 = given surface mesh
                              2 = coarse surface grid data
                              3 = Control points of bicubic splines
                              4 = occupied by bilinear coons
                              5 = occupied by bicubic  coons
                              6 = occupied by yet another coon
                              7 = Control points of nurbs
                              8 = Control points of nurbs (reserved see :10)
                              9 = KNOT values of nurbs
     @2#  m       [int]    |Rasterlocation of mesh 0 < m ( mgri )
     @3#  n       [int]    |Rasterlocation of mesh 0 < n ( ngri )
     @4#  n3      [int]    |the degree of the Spline becoming effective
                               if m>0  for s-direction
                               if n>0  for t-direction
                            or third node number of irregular mesh
     @5#  n4      [int]    |the weight of NURBS control point [-]
                            or fourth node number of irregular mesh
     @1:  X       [1001]   |X-ordinate           |Koordinate X
     @2:  Y       [1001]   |Y-ordinate           |Koordinate Y
     @3:  Z       [1001]   |Z-ordinate           |Koordinate Z
     @4:  T       [1010]   |Thickness            |Dicke

     surface mesh and grid points are in a fixed sequence
         (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) ...
         (0,1), (1,1), (2,1) ...
         (0,2), (1,2), (2,2) ...

     A surface mesh (it=0) is only generated for the other types of
     description. So we have either it=0 or it=1 grids but not both.
     all other it (2 to 7) or revolution surfaces however are allowed
     to have an it=0/-1/-2 grid too (for visualisation purpose).

     An unstructured mesh (it<0) consists of arbitrary triangles or
     quadrilaterals and nodes. However for those regions we need to
     know the sequence of the nodes along the boundaries. Thus m and
     n are used to give the relative location n along the edge m.

     It is also possible to have unstructured data points within a
     regular mesh describing the thickness of the surface.

                            Twist of x,y,z-Ordinate at corner C4 (0,1)

     For the coons patches geometry we need four outer boundaries that
     are blended. In most cases these are identical to the real outer
     boundaries, but in special cases these may be selected seperately.
     This record is needed if the number of outer edges is not 4 or
     the type of coons patch is not bilinear.

                   ^ inc3                ^ inc4
              C4 o-|--------- iv1 -------|-o C3
                --> inc6                   --> inc8
                 |            v|           |
                iu0            |->u       iu1
                 |                         |
                --> inc5                  --> inc7
              C1 o-|--------- iv1 -------|-o C2
                   ^ inc1                ^ inc2

     For more details see FARIN / Curves and surfaces for CAGD

     For structured meshes of any geometric shape there are two special
     records: The type it==0 is the most general case and always needed
     the values iu0 to iu1 define the topological corners of the fit.
     The second optional record it==3 defines four edges used for the fit
     The mesh generator will create the same meshing on opposite edges.

     In case of structured meshes with boundary layers with internal edges,
     there are two records of that type, the first (original) defines the
     geometry and will become desabled for the structured mesh, while the
     second one is not used for the geometry (IT&&16).

                           | &512  = connected to support

     @1:  POS     [1001]   |position of sections

     @12: ext(0) 3[1001,1001,1001] | global extension, local extensions min/max
     @18: vert  63[1001,1001,1001] | vertices in local coordinates r,s,t

     The polyeder selective volume is described by a transformation matrix
         r = tran(1,1)*(x-xref) + tran(2,1)*(y-yref) + tran(3,1)*(z-zref)
         s = tran(1,2)*(x-xref) + tran(2,2)*(y-yref) + tran(3,2)*(z-zref)
         t = tran(1,2)*(x-xref) + tran(2,2)*(y-yref) + tran(3,2)*(z-zref)
     Then we apply a local point in polygon test for (s,t) and a check for
     the t coordinate to be within the third local extension.

{/red}

{red}
     @Rec: 038/NR:10?  GLAR_L   |Load distribution areas  Beamloads             :V200501
{/red}
     @0=  ID      [int]       |Identification 100:103
                                100 = valid for all directions
                                101 = valid only for x direction
                                102 = valid only for y direction
                                103 = valid only for z direction
     @1#  INR     [int]       |nodenumber of 038/NR:1 within region
     @2#  NSEG    [int]       |number of 038/NR:3 segment
     @3:  PA      [-]         |start value of load
     @4:  PE      [-]         |end value of load

     optional (only for ID=101:103):

     @5:  MA      [-]         |start value of torque
     @6:  ME      [-]         |end value of torque


     This data is used to convert loadings within an area to
     node and beam loads which are at the edge or in the interior.
     This item is only valid as long as the nodes and beams
     of the system do not change.

     The masters of the load distribution area may be structural
     regions 32/NR, which are then a geometric surface and not part
     of the structural system (32/NR:0->ITP = 0)
     These areas may contain a structured or unstructured mesh either
     as a member of the global system (32/NR:0->NoG >= 0) or purely
     internal (32/NR:0->NoG < 0). These internal nodes and elements
     are then either given by a regular grid or by 032/NR:11:-1/-2.

     The geometry of the loading area is defined by the 32/NR data.
     The group number of the 32/NR:0 selects also the elements

     Remark, regarding CMD:
             Up to REL2023 SP2: There were two DUCTGRPS. One for activated [112, 0, group1, group2,...] and one for deactivated 
                                deactivated [112, 1, group1, group2,...]
              From REL2023 SP2: There is only one DUCTGRPS record containing both, activated and deactivated groups. For this,
                                in GRPID "pairs" are stored, containing <group Id, command (0:activate, 1:deactivate)>. So
                                it is possible to preserve the order of the input [112, 2, group1, cmd1, group2, cmd2, ...]
                                The CMD 2 is used to distinguish between old and new version.

{red}
     @Rec: 87/LC:+  SLVL_RES  | Structural Storey Level Results                          :V200902
     @Dad: 012/LC
{/red}
     @0=  NR          [int]   |Storey Level ID (34/NR)
     @1=  NR_MODE     [int]   |mode number (=0: resultant values, e.g. from CQC sup.)
                                #0 resultant base shear values
                                >0 base shear values for mode-number NR_MODE
     @2#  STYP       2[chr]   |superposition type
     @1:  PX         [1151]   |base shear in X                                         | Gesamtschubkraft in X
     @2:  PY         [1151]   |base shear in Y                                         | Gesamtschubkraft in Y
     @3:  PZ         [1151]   |total vertical load at and above the storey             | Gesamtvertikalkraft am und oberhalb des Geschosses
     @4:  MX         [1152]   |moment about X                                          | Moment um X
     @5:  MY         [1152]   |moment about Y                                          | Moment um Y
     @6:  MZ         [1152]   |moment about Z                                          | Moment um Z
     @7:  UX         [1003]   |average storey displacement in X (=translations at COM) | mittlere Stockwerksverschiebung in X
     @8:  UY         [1003]   |average storey displacement in Y                        | mittlere Stockwerksverschiebung in Y
     @9:  UZ         [1003]   |average storey displacement in Z                        | mittlere Stockwerksverschiebung in Z
    @10:  RZ         [1004]   |average storey rotation in XY-plane                     | mittlere Stockwerksverdrehung in der XY-Ebene
    @11:  DX         [1003]   |inter-storey drift in X (=difference between top and bottom of storey) | gegenseitige Stockwerksverschiebung in X
    @12:  DY         [1003]   |inter-storey drift in Y                                 | gegenseitige Stockwerksverschiebung in Y
    @13:  DRZ        [1004]   |inter-storey rotation in XY-plane                       | gegenseitige Stockwerksverdrehung in der XY-Ebene
    @14:  DXMAX      [1003]   |maximum inter-storey drift in X                         | maximale gegenseitige Stockwerksverschiebung in X
    @15:  DYMAX      [1003]   |maximum inter-storey drift in Y                         | maximale gegenseitige Stockwerksverschiebung in Y
    @16:  LSAF         [98]   |modal acceleration (only for NR_MODE>0)                 | modale Beschleunigung

     The base shear is a simplified approach which can not handle all the features
     of a full analytical modal analysis. However it is a common approach.
     LSAF is the modal acceleration calculated by
          LSAF = Phi-T * M * a * Sa / Phi-T * M * Phi
     where Phi = Eigenform [m], M = mass vector [t],
           a = base acceleration, Sa = Response-Spectra-Value
     For this mode we have then the inertial forces given by
          Fik = LSAF-i * m-k * Phi-i,k
     The sum of all Fik for any Eigenform i is saved in this record

     The resultant base shear is obtained by a superposition (CQC etc)
     for all modes. The LSAF value of this record is undefined.

{/red}
     @0:  DIAG(NEQ)  *[-] |Diagonals     |Diagonalglieder

     After the triangulisation or factorisation of the stiffness matrix
     the resulting diagonals of the stiffnessmatrix are written to
     cdbase to be used for BDK and other programs of that type.
     The linear stiffness is written to LC=0.
     For iterative solvers the diagonals are not factorized at all and
     thus of lesser practical use.

!TOPIC 171 100

    *  ****  ****                     {link}172{-link}100/* Beam Structures{/link}
   **  *  *  *  *                     {link}173{-link}101/* Beam Loading{/link}
  * *  *  *  *  *                     {link}174{-link}102/* Forces and moments{/link}
    *  *  *  *  *                     {link}175{-link}103/* Stiffness{/link}
    *  *  *  *  *                     {link}176{-link}104/* Eigenstress{/link}
    *  *  *  *  *                     {link}177{-link}105/* Stresses{/link}
    *  ****  ****                     {link}178{-link}106/* Reinforcement{/link}
                                      {link}179{-link}107/* Design results{/link}
                                      {link}180{-link}108/* Shade-effects{/link}
                                      {link}181{-link}109/* Internal Loading pattern{/link}
                                      {link}203{-link}111/* Hinge reactions{/link}
                                      {link}210{-link}115/* Material point reactions{/link}
                                      {link}242{-link}116/* Tendon results{/link}
                                      {link}244{-link}61/*  Design case defintions{/link}

A Beam Element may be defined with reference to a geometric description.
In that case the beams axis and the nodes of the element are connected
to each other by the following rules:

The reference axis of the beam is the straight or curved connection
between the two nodes, defined with a geometric line property. Each
section has its own coordinate system, the origin of which is on the
reference axis of the beam. For the geometric and static model the
section is perpendicular to the reference axis. This approach defines
eccentric beams and haunches in a very natural way.

The effective span of the beam is defined by the connection of other
beams at the node. There will be a shift from the geometric modelling
to the static reference system.



       Node possible at outer geometry
      o-----*----------------------------------------*------o
      |     |                                        |      |
      |  A=s=======================================s==E     | 
      |     |                                        |      |
      *-----o----------------------------------------o------*
      |a |  | Node possible at inner geometry        |  | b |
      |     |                                        |  |   |
      |     |                                        |  |   |

  - The mechanical sections are scaled from 0.0 to DL giving the
    physical span of the beam and the stiffness properties.
    At start and endpoint additional sections with negative
    x-values or values larger than DL may be defined for
    cantilevers.
  - The mechanical start and end sections are connected with
    rigid elements to the nodes. The axial eccentricity is given
    explicitly, while the cross eccentricity defaults to the
    gravity center given by the cross sections coordinate system.
  - loads may be given on the full length including cantilever
  - For intersections of beams we provide virtual cross sections
     - do not apply dead weight loading in neighboured spans
     - you may use higher stiffnessvalues for bending

  In the above example the horizontal beam will have sections

    x = -a    Outer face with    ITYP2 & 256 (=no statics)
    x =  0    support
    ...
    x = DL    support
    x = DL+b  Outer face with    ITYP2 & 256 (=no statics)

  The vertical beam will have the sections

    x =  0    support with       ITYP2 & 512 (=no dead weight)
    x =  h/2  face and physical start of beam (standard)
    ...

  If the nodes are defined at the outer side, both beams will have
  positive eccentricities.


The reference axis is defined in a special line element (31/NR).
It includes properties like geometric curvatures or bedding
constants.

As a standard option (NP=0) the classic approach is used defining
the axis of the beam as the center of gravity. Negative values of
NP indicate the new approach but without a specific geometry.

All distances between sections are measured relative to the beams
reference axis, i.e. for curved eccentric members you might need
to do some extra calculation to get physical correct distances.

{red}
Continuous Beams
{/red}

For many purposes it is desired to have a continuous beam composed
of several individual beams (Stabzug). The approach within in SOFiSTiK
is quite simple concerning the database:

It is mandatory that all beams forming a continuous beam are saved
in the database in the proper sequence, i.e. correctly aligned and
consecutive without other elements in between.
Thus a non monotonic behaviour of SVAL is the only indicator for a
new span within the database, the change of the reference itself is
NOT a forcing event.

As the sequence in the database is also influenced by the group number
it might be necessary to use a special compatible group pattern.
e.g. Girder A with groups 11,12,13, Girder B with groups 21,22,23
and construction stages 11+21 / 12+22 / 13+23.

The continous beam itself may be addressed by the first beam number
and an ordinate along the beam. Special points within (supports etc)
have to be identified by the nodal properties. The most simple case
is to use NCOD&1 Bit for provided or generated nodes. In more complex
cases the definition of a GPT-Record with the same number may be used.

For the input definition of a continuos beam there are the following
possibilities:

1. Automatic detection of a new sequence within all beams in SOFIMSHA and
the CTRL CONT Bitpattern and GRP NREF values for the first beam number
(end-node of a beam has to match the start node of the next beam etc.)
An explicit special hinge condition "end of continuous beam" enforces
the start or the end of a continous beam sequence. Reasons for
that might be a support condition.

2. A special object "continuos beam" in SOFiPLUS

3. A sequence of structural lines all refering to the same master
geometry (3/ID or 31/NR). This also allows to specify different
properties to the segments and to identify support nodes properly.
This results in a monotonic behaviour of SVAL although the references
itself are different.

Eccentricities are measured either to the reference axis (origin of section)
or to the centroid, controlled with +400 in the load type.

For the special loadtype 60 = absolute Temperature the exzentricities
follow a special rule (see also 202/LC)


     Convention: 
     * reference 8?? 
       Y,Z will be ajusted to the negative extreme fiber of the section.
       The distance 0 is the top/leftmost fibre.
     * reference 9?? 
       Y,Z will be ajusted to the positive extreme fiber of the section.
       The distance 0 is the lowest/rightmost fibre
     * reference 0?? and 4?? 
       positive and negative values for the values Y,Z will be 
       always scaled to cover the full thickness.


Prestressing is represented for each tendon with TYP 2070.
PA,PE is the tensioning force at start and end of the intervall.
The eccentricity are measured in the reference coordinate system
and define a cubic spline. Thus the moment My is given by P*z and
the transverse force by P*dz/dx.

Massdistribution is defined via TYP 1010 or 2010.

There is no header record!, the records are assumed to be sorted for the beam number only.

     @0:  X         [1001]  |distance from start |Abstand zu Stabanfang
     @1:  N         [1101]  |normal force        |Normalkraft

     Remark: A T-beam within a plate structure may contain plate
             components which are stored within 102/LC
             In this case a second key 112/LC is stored which has
             the beam components only.

     only for 102/LC and if calculated with STAR2 or ASE:

     @9:  ux        [1003]  |diplacement local x |Verformung lokal x
     @10: uy        [1003]  |diplacement local y |Verformung lokal y

     @30: beta2_w   [1005]  |eas twisting


Remarks:


Depending on the theory of the load case (see {link}150{-link}12/LC{/link}) the forces
are in longitudinal and transversal components (i.e. parallel to the
original beam axis (ITHEO=1/2) or normal and cross components (i.e.
parallel to the deformed beam axis (ITHEO=0/3)

For single point loading there may be two records, the first of them has
a negative beam number.

For 2nd and 3rd order theory the deformations include imperfections.

There is a special record type for LC=0, which includes one more
integer before the first number giving a section number for separate
forces used in AQB/AQUP.
