                             = not defined for reinforcements / tendons

     Maximum loadcases (COMB GMAX) contain the sway values for individual points @9:@10

    @12:  Vb       [1153]   |Bond force           |Verbundschubkraft
    @13:  FAK_VV   [-]      |shear reduction factor = elastic/nonlinear lever
                             obsoleted: utilisation of buckling
    @14:  N_PART   [1101]   |normal force in that part of the section
    @15:  SIGCT    [1092]   |decompression stress |Decompressionsspannung
    @16:  rctrl    [-]      |control value of stress/strain description
                                     #define WORKLAW_LINEAR                    0 = linear stress
                                >0 = nonlinear
                                     10000*(CTRL_INTE) +
                                       100*(WORKLAW_SOLID) +
                                         1*(WORKLAW_REINFORCEMENT)
                                     #define WORKLAW_ELASTIC_NOMINAL                1 = EL    elastic nominal
                                     #define WORKLAW_ELASTIC_DESIGN                 2 = ELD   elastic design
                                     #define WORKLAW_SERVICE_NOMINAL                3 = SL    service nominal
                                     #define WORKLAW_SERVICE_DESIGN                 4 = SLD   service design
                                     #define WORKLAW_ULTIMATE_NOMINAL               5 = UL    ultimate nominal
                                     #define WORKLAW_ULTIMATE_DESIGN                6 = ULD   ultimate design
                                     #define WORKLAW_CALC_MEAN_NOMINAL              7 = CALC  calc. mean nominal
                                     #define WORKLAW_CALC_MEAN_DESIGN               8 = CALD  calc. mean design
                                     #define WORKLAW_FULLY_PLASTIC_NOMINAL          9 = PL    fully plastic nominal
                                     #define WORKLAW_FULLY_PLASTIC_DESIGN          10 = PLD   fully plastic design
                                     #define WORKLAW_PARTIAL_PLASTIC_NOMINAL       11 = PLB   partial plastic (concrete stress block) nominal
                                     #define WORKLAW_PARTIAL_PLASTIC_DESIGN        12 = PLBD  partial plastic (concrete stress block) design
                                     #define WORKLAW_COLUMN_PLASTIC_CHARACTERISTIC 13 = PLC   plastic characteristic full strength for columns
                                     #define WORKLAW_COLUMN_PLASTIC_DESIGN         14 = PLCD  plastic design full strength for columns

                                     CTRL_INTE  Non linear axial strain effects and shear/axial stress interaction
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_NO_EFFECTS           0 =   do not take into account
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_ISOTROPE_REDUCTION   1 =   isotrope reduction of stresses
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_PRANDTL_FLOW_RULE    2 =   Prandtl flow rule for stresses (default for steel)
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_PREFERENCE_SHEAR     3 =   preference of shear stress
                                     additional bits:
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_MAXIMUM_TEMPERATURE  4 = + strength dependant on maximum temperature
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_SECTION_CLASS_E_P    8 = + Section class for E-P (NSTR S0)
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_SECTION_CLASS_P_P   16 = + Section class for P-P (NSTR S1/S2)
                                     #define BEAM_STR_CTRL_INTE_WITHOUT_HARDENING   32 = + deactivate hardening (e.g. for section class 4)

    @17:  ES0      [-]      |strain in center of total section
    @18:  ESY      [-]      |strain gradient in y-direction
    @19:  ESZ      [-]      |strain gradient in z-direction
    @20:  YC       [1011]   |location of center of partial section
    @21:  ZC       [1011]   |location of center of partial section

    @22:  shea[ESW,VYF,VZF,MTF,MT2F]  33[-,1102,1102,1103,1103] | factors of warp and shear per construction stage (MAX_SECT_CS+1)
          ESW      =        |factor for unit warping
          VYF      =        |shear force
          VZF      =        |shear force
          MTF      =        |primary torsional moment
          MT2F     =        |secondary torsional moment

    The stress is controlled by material law and strain distribution
        eps = ES0+ESY*y+ESZ*z+ESW*w0
        tau = Wvy*Vyf + Wvz*Vzf + Wt*Mtf + Wt2*Mt2f
    To allow a proper treating of non-effective parts, the strain ES0 is at yc,zc 
    relative to the elastic center (yref,zref) of the gross section. thus
        eps(y,z) = ES0 + (y-yref-yc)*ESY + (z-zref-zc)*ESZ
    for linear stresses (yc,zc) is the excentricity of the effective center to the
    gross center, for non linear stresses, ES0 is selected based on the normal force.
    for non effective parts, ESY or ESZ terms will be ignored.

    Block of Values @22 to @26 will be repeated for every construction
    stage if those are activated. First entry is the final construction stage.
    Second entry is the first construction stage, third entry is the second construction stage...

    For selected points additional records may be stored. MNR holds
    then the encoded Point-Number and only values 1:6 are defined.

    Hint: Historic formats
          Version 0 : ESW/tau-values starting @20
          Version 1 : ESW/tau-values starting @21, inserted ES00  @20
          Version 2 : ESW/tau-values starting @22, inserted YC,ZC @20:21


{red}
     @Rec: 1105/LC:Z!:+  BEAM_CST |Composite stresses in cross-section of beams              :V202401 
     @Rec: 1125/LC:Z!:+  DSLN_CST |Composite stresses in cross-section of design elements    :V202401
{/red}
     @0=  NR      [int]   |beam/dsln id
                           NR < 0 = jump: left bank
                           NR > 0 = after a jump: right bank , otherwise: continuous
     @1#  MNR     [int]   |material id  
     @2#  WRKLAW  [int]   |worklaw (see 105: rctrl WORKLAW_...)
     @3#  ELMID   [chr]   |cross-section element id     (parent element in case of reinforcement)
     @4#  SUBID   [int]   |cross-section element sub-id (parent element in case of reinforcement)
     @5#  CS      [int]   |construction stage
     @6#  ID1     [int]   |free
     @7#  ID2     [int]   |free
     @8#  ID3     [int]   |free
     @0:  X       [1001]  |distance from start
     @1:  RHO_S   [1299]  |reinforcement degree (only concrete elements)
     @2:  BETA_T  [-]     |tension stiffening factor (only reinforcements)  (see 3)
     @3:  BE1     [1011]  |effective width at start            (see 4)
     @4:  BE2     [1011]  |effective width at end              (see 4)
     @5:  ES0     [-]     |strain at origin of cross-section   (see 1)
     @6:  ESY     [-]     |strain gradient in y-direction      (see 1)
     @7:  ESZ     [-]     |strain gradient in z-direction      (see 1)
     @8:  EW0A    [-]     |strain from warping at start point  (see 1)
     @9:  EW0B    [-]     |strain from warping at end   point  (see 1)
     @10: TAUA    [-]     |shear stress factor a               (see 2)
     @11: TAUB    [-]     |shear stress factor b               (see 2)
     @12: TAUC    [-]     |shear stress factor c               (see 2)
     @13: TAULIN  [-]     |shear stress in perpendicular dir   (see 2)

    (1) Axial strains
            epsilon(y,z) = ES0 + y*ESY + z*ESZ + [(1-s)*EW0A + s*EW0B]
          with
            y,z: being the coordinates in the cross-section (w.r.t. cross-section origin)
                 For thin-walled elements
                  y = (1-s)*yA + s*yB
                  z = (1-s)*zA + s*zB
            s:   being the local parameter along the thin-walled element in [0,1]
                 For reinforcements y,z are to be projected onto the mid-axis

    (2) Shear stresses on mid axis
            tau(s) = TAUA*s*s + TAUB*s + TAUC

        Shear stress perpendicular to mid-axis
            tau(s, xi) = tau(s) + xi*TAULIN
          with
            xi in [-t/2, t/2]
            t:= thickness

        Remark: All values (ES0, ESY,..., TAUC) are already summed up for the current load case
            Examples (with '/"/... marking the 1st/2nd/... lc)
                 ES0  = ES0'          + ES0"          + ... 
                 EW0A = MT2'/IW'*W0A' + MT2"/IW"*W0A" + ... (W0A being the unit warping at start)

    (3) Tension stiffening of reinforcements  (e.g. SLS or fatigue):
        Only if BETA_T > 0.0
        Additional dstrain must be added to the reinforcement strain (see epsilon(y,z) from elastic
        strain planes, see 1). For this the respective concrete parent element is required.

        For compression             strain <= 0:                          dstrain = 0.0
        for tension after crack     strain >= crack_strain (= f_ctm/E_c): dstrain = beta_t * f_ctm/(rho_s * E_s)
        for tension while cracking  0 < strain < crack_strain:            linear interpolation [0, crack_strain] --> [0, beta_t * f_ctm/(rho_s * E_s)]

        with:
          f_ctm := (parent) concrete tension strength
          rho_s := reinforcement degree of the parent element
          E_c   := original Emod of parent concrete (original -> not the reduced Emod, e.g. at supports)
          E_s   := Emod reinforcement

    (4) Effective width (b_eff) acc. to EN 1993-1-5, Tab. 4.1 & 4.2
        Only if BE1 or BE2 > 0.0
        The respective element is to be replaced by one or two shorter elements.
        Bear in mind, that b_eff acts on c not the length, thus the small supporting 
        pieces at start and end (fixA and fixB) must be added:
        
         |---------- length -----------|     complete length
              |-------- c --------|          "effective" length
                                                 
         *====|===================|====*     unreduced panel
        ptA  ptA,fix         ptB,fix  ptB       
                                                
         *====|=====*       *=====|====*     reduced panel
              |-be1-|       |-be2-|          b_eff left/right
         |----|                   |----|     support points
          fixA                     fixB

{red}
     @Rec: 116/LC:Z! BEAM_TF  | Tendon forces in beams                         :V202509 
     @Rec: 136/LC:Z! DSLN_TF  | Tendon forces in design elements               :V202509 
     @Dad: 012/LC
{/red}

     @0=  NR        [int]   |beam/dsln number
                             In case of a result jump:
                               NR < 0 = left bank  (must come first)
                               NR > 0 = right bank
     @1#  TNDNR     [int]   |tendon number
     @2#  RSRVD    4[-]     |reserved
     @1:  X         [1001]  |distance from start
     @2:  P         [1101]  |tendon force 
     @3:  DF_DUCT   [1101]  |duct compensation force (subtracts A_duct from gross section) 
                              - before grouting:  -A_duct * sig_c(t) 
                              - after  grouting:  -A_duct * sig_c(t) 
     @4:  DF_GROU   [1101]  |grouting compensation force (adds A_duct back after grouting) 
                              - before grouting:   0 
                              - after  grouting:   A_duct * (sig_c(t) - sig_c(t_grout)) 
     @5:  DF_TEND   [1101]  |tendon compensation force (subtracts A_p from A_duct) 
                              - before grouting:   0 
                              - after  grouting:  -A_p * (sig_c(t) - sig_c(t_grout)) 
     @6:  EPS_PMT   [1081]  |elastic tendon strain 
     @7:  EPS_CPT   [1081]  |elastic concrete strain at tendon position 
     @8:  N         [1101]  |primary normal force from tendons 
     @9:  VY        [1102]  |primary y-shear force from tendons 
     @10: VZ        [1102]  |primary z-shear force from tendons 
     @11: MT        [1103]  |primary torsional moment from tendons 
     @12: MY        [1104]  |primary bending moment My from tendons 
     @13: MZ        [1104]  |primary bending moment Mz from tendons 
     @14: MB        [1105]  |primary warping moment Mb from tendons 
     @15: MT2       [1103]  |primary 2nd torsional moment from tendons 
          
     Further state variables:
     
     @16: AGE       [93]    |age since prestress    
     @17: RELZ      [-]     |accumulated relaxation 


     Explanations:
     1. Which force is acting?
         In tendon alone                     = P
         For normal force on concrete (e.g.) = N_c,gross + DF_DUCT + DF_GROU + DF_TEND
     
     2. Tendon "base" strain EPS_PMT0 (similar to Zilch):
         How much does the tendon strain exceed the concrete strain?
            eps_pmt0 = EPS_PMT - EPS_CPT             
                     = sig_pmt/E_p    - sig_cpt/E_cm
                     = tendon tension - concrete compression
            sig_cpt  = Stress in concrete due to jacking (if duct and tendon aligned =(DF_DUCT+DF_GROU)/A_duct)
            P_mt     = P0             -  P_creep - P_shrink - P_relax
                     = jacking force  -  losses from creep/shrink/relaxation
  
                             strain plane
                          |  /       
                          | /       deps := tendon strains NOT from P_mt (e.g. self weight, live loads)
                          |´                before grouting: deps=0 (can be neglected)
                         /|          
                        / |          
            eps_pmt0   /  |          
              --------/---|     tendon
                      deps

     @Rec: 170/00          SPRI | Spring-elements                              :V201201 \
                                | Feder-Elemente
{/red}
     @0=  NR       [int]    |springnumber      |Federnummer
     @1#  NODE     2[int]   |start nodenumber     | Anfangsknoten
     @3#  NRQ      [int]    |Material/work law no | Material/Arbeitsliniennr
                             defined only if a special work law to be used
                             0 otherwise.
                             case 1: NRQ > 0 refers to a work law 173/NRQ
                                     with explicit force-displacement
                                     relations.
                             case 2: NRQ < 0 refers to a material 1/-NRQ
                                     with a bedding constant or
                                     with elasticity moduli and distance
     @1:  T        3[-]     |normal direction     | Richtung Federachse
                             X-component, Y-component, Z-component
     @4:  Aref     [-]      |reference area    |Referenzfläche
                             to be used for other physical properties
                             given as distributed values per m2
                              >0  Springelement:
                                  vor,gap,riss,flie acts on P
                                  friction,cohesion acts on PT
                                  Aref is the area perpendicular to n
                              <0  Slip-Element:
                                  vor,gap,riss,flie acts on PT
                                  friction,cohesion acts on P
                                  Aref is the circumferental area
     @5:  cp       [1095]   |spring stiffness  |Federkonstante
     @6:  cq       [1095]   |transverse stiff. |Federkonstante quer
     @7:  cm       [1098]   |torsional stiff.  |Federkonstante Moment
     @8:  PRE      [*]      |prestress         |Vorspannung

          The generic definition of spring forces is [kN=1151,kNm=1152].
          However for axial symmetric systems all values are usually
          defined per arclength: P,M in [kN/m=1153,kNm/m=1154] and CP
          in [kN/m2=1096] or CM [kNm/m=1099].
          As the SOFiSTiK-Database uses fixed units internally, the
          input routine will use Aref to multiply the stiffness and the
          nonlinear effects with the mean radius of the nodes.

          if it is a nonlinear element:

     @9:  GAP      [*]      |slip/gap of spring  |Schlupf/Spiel der Feder
                              GAP > 0.  contact, i.e. linear is open
                              GAP < 0.  slip, linear is closed
     @10: RISS     [*]      |max tension force   |Risslast der Feder
     @11: FLIE     [*]      |yielding load       |Fliesslast der Feder
     @12: MUE      [-]      |friction cross      |Reibbeiwert Querfeder
     @13: COH      [*]      |cohesion cross      |Kohäsion der Querfeder
     @14: DIL      [-]      |dilatancy factor    |Dilatanzfaktor
     @15: GAPQ     [*]      |transverse slip/gap |Schlupf/Spiel Querfeder
                              GAPQ > 0.  contact, i.e. linear is open
                              GAPQ < 0.  slip, linear is closed

          Values for nonlinear effects default to 0.0, which means that the corresponding effect is disabled.
          An actual input of 0.0 for RISS is represented by a value of 1.e-12 in the data base.
          The historic treating for ASE is to treat GAP as a slip, while DYNA is assuming a contact.
          The sign of GAPQ is thus controlling CP and CQ for now.


          if it is also a coupled damping element:

     @16: dp       [*]      |damping constant | Dämpfungskonstante
     @17: dq       [*]      |damping shear    | Querdämpfung
     @18: dm       [*]      |damping moment   | Momentendämpfung
     @19: expp     [-]      |exponent for nonlinear damping dp**expp
     @20: expq     [-]      |exponent for nonlinear damping dq**expq
     @21: expm     [-]      |exponent for nonlinear damping dm**expm

     @22: TB       3[-]     |rotational direction | Drehachse für CM
                             X-component, Y-component, Z-component

     @25# NREF     [int]    |additional bit code   |Zusatz bit code
                              &64*n spring has been derived from
                                       0 = point  (30/NN)
                                       1 = line   (31/NN)
                                       2 = region (32/NN)
                                       3 = volume (33/NN)
                              &256*NN  (identification number of item)

     @1:  P        [1151]   |spring force      | Federkraft

     @4:  PTY      [1151]   |global Y-shear component \

     @9:  vtx      [1003]   |trans. displacement, global X-component \

     @10: vty      [1003]   |trans. displacement, global Y-component \
                            |Verschiebung in Querrichtung,Y-komponente
     @11: vtz      [1003]   |trans. displacement, global Z-component \
                            |Verschiebung in Querrichtung,Z-komponente
     @12: phi      [1004]   |rotation          | Verdrehung
     @13: LEX      [-]      |nonlinear effect  | Plastizierungskenner
                             (as float)
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_NONL_PART_STRESS_STRAIN_LONGITUDINAL    1 = nonlinear part of stress strain curve longitudinal
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_GAP_ACTIVATED                           2 = gap is activated in nonlinear effect   (gap)
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_CRACKED                                 4 = cracked - tension failure  due to CRAC (riss)
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_YIELDED                                 8 = yielded - nonlinear effect due to YIEL (flie)
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_NONL_FRICTION                          16 = friction in nonlinear part        MUE  (mue)
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_NONL_COHESION                          32 = cohesion in nonlinear part        COH  (coh)
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_GAP_TORSIONAL                          64 = GAP  for a nonlinear torsional spring
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_CRACKED_TORSIONAL                     128 = CRAC for a nonlinear torsional spring
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_YIELDED_TORSIONAL                     256 = YIEL for a nonlinear torsional spring
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_NONL_PART_STRESS_STRAIN_TORSIONAL     512 = nonlinear part of stress strain curve torsional
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_SPRING_GEOMETRIC_NONLINEAR           1024 = spring analyzed with geometric nonlinear effect
                             #define SPRI_RES_LEX_MOVING_SPRING                        2048 = moving spring (vtx,vty,vtz show to spring-end)

     if it's a nonlinear problem with worklaws:

     @14: STVP   10[*]      |State variable / Damage Parameter for CP
                               STVP(1) current total deformation value (incl. prestress)
                               STVP(2) Performance level
                             for MTYP=1:3 (PLAS,PISO,HYPE) :
                               STVP(3) hardening shift 1. direction (remaining deformation)
                               STVP(4) hardening shift for 2. direction (compression)
                               STVP(5) deformation zero point of GAP
                               STVP(6) deformation zero point of CRAC
                               STVP(7:10) free reserved for later use
                             for MTYP=4 (PKIN kinematic hardening) :
                               STVP(3) deformation of current (shifted) zero point of work law
                               STVP(4) corresponding force
                               STVP(5) deformation of current (shifted) zero point for unloading
                               STVP(6) corresponding force
                               STVP(7:10) free reserved for later use
     @24: STVM   10[*]      |State variable / Damage Parameter for CM
     @34: STVT   13[*]      |State variable / Damage Parameter for CT

     There is also the data 187/LC containing the global sum of all forces of
     springs with only one node (support springs)

     2. MATRIX%IA(0:N) if(ICT(3)>0)

     @Rec: 173/NR:+  SPRI_WL   | force-displacement / moment-rotation work law                  :V201206 \
{/red}
     @0=  ID       [int]       |Identification     | Kennziffer
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_CP   1  axial reaction        [1155]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_CQ   2  transversal reaction  [1155]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_CM   3  rotational reaction   [1156]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_NX  11  Normal force Nx [1101]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_VY  12  Shear force Vy  [1102]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_VZ  13  Shear force Vz  [1102]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_MT  14  Torsional moment Mt [1103]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_MY  15  Bending moment My [1104]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_MZ  16  Bending moment Mz [1104]
                                 #define SPRI_WL_ID_MB  17  Warping moment Mb [1105] (not supported)

                                  +900 = performance limit definition --> see SPRI_WLP

     @1#  NTYP     [int]       |Type of law        | Art des Gesetzes
                                 #define SPRI_WL_NTYP_USER   0  user defined
                                 #define SPRI_WL_NTYP_LIN    1  linear
                                 #define SPRI_WL_NTYP_BILIN  2  bilinear
                                 #define SPRI_WL_NTYP_TRILIN 3  trilinear
                                 #define SPRI_WL_NTYP_PLAS   4  rigid plastic
                                 + 1024*bitpattern of sharp bends (1-20)
                                   1024=first, 2048=second, 4096=third ...
                                   (first and last point always assumed)

     @1:  PLVL     [1101]        | Normal force reference level
                                   =0.0    : input undefined
                                   =1.e-12 : input 0.0
     @2:  EUR      [*]           | Elastic unloading/reloading stiffness [kN/m],[kNm/rad]
                                   =0.0    : undefined

     CRCK, GAP for SPRI_WL_ID_CP, SPRI_WL_ID_CQ, SPRI_WL_ID_CM, only:
     @3:  CRAC     [1089]        | rupture stress (cracking), [1156] for SPRI_WL_ID_CM
     @4:  GAPP     [1003]        | initial slip in positive direction (magnitude), [1004] for SPRI_WL_ID_CM
     @5:  GAPN     [1003]        | initial slip in negative direction (magnitude), [1004] for SPRI_WL_ID_CM

     FRIC, COH for SPRI_WL_ID_CQ, only:
     @6:  FRIC     [-]           | friction coefficient
     @7:  COH      [1089]        | cohesion

     ALPH, BETA for SPRI_WL_ID_MY, SPRI_WL_ID_MZ, only:
     @8:  ALPH     [-]           | stiffness reduction factor for mod. Takeda model
     @9:  BETA     [-]           | plasticity weight factor for mod. Takeda model
     @10:  PAR     [*]           | further reserved material parameters
     
     @11:  ARB(0) 20*[*,*,*,-,-] | Function values | Funktionswerte

                                up to 20 Blocks with 5 float-values containing:

                                  U   [*]  |displacement [1003]/ rotation [1004]   | Verschiebung/ Verdrehung
                                  F   [*]  |Force/Moment [units see above]         | Kraft/Moment
                                  E   [*]  |Stiffness      | Steifigkeit
                                  E'  [-]  |Stiffness      | Steifigkeit
                                  E'' [-]  |Stiffness      | Steifigkeit

                                For a displacement less than U holds:

                                  F(u) =  F+u*E+u**2*E'+u**3*E''

          For special simplified forms we have only one single data block where

              for a hinge all values are zero                           ntyp=?
              for a linear elastic law there is E only                  ntyp=1
              for a rigid plastic hinge there is F only                 ntyp=4
              for a bilinear law the values E and F are used            ntyp=2
              for a trilinear law the values U, E, E' and F are used    ntyp=3
                    = linear from 0 to U with stiffness E
                    = linear from (U,E*U) with stiffness E'
                    = maximum value F

  A Boundary element as a logic item may comprehend several records
  Only the first record will have the designation all shorter records are
  additional nodes in the element.

  The local coordinate system of such a boundary element is either
  to be taken from the generating structural line 32/nr or defaults
  similar to the beams as follows:

  Plane frames etc. (IPROBTYPE==1):
  Obsoleted:   The local z-axis is identical to the global z-axis.
               So we have the local y-axis as ( -vy, +vx, 0 ) always.
  New 06-2006: The local z-axis is oriented in the plane to the right
               of the longitudinal direction. So the pictures in the
               manual are always valid. We have the same orientation
               as above for the SOFiSTiK-coordinate system, but the
               opposite direction for WKS-frame systems.

  All others based on a local z-axis aligning downward.

{red}
     @RecM: 190/LC:+ LINK_RES  | Link Element Reactions                                         :V202602 \
     @Dad: 012/LC
{/red}
     Remark: Implicit hinges and explicit link elements are conceptionally similar, both connecting the
             local DOFs of two (virtual) nodes, where the mechanical connectivity is ruled by the specified 
             constitutive behavior. The constitutive laws specify the interaction of a subset or all 
             associated local DOFs (up to 6 local DOFs per node).

             Due to this conceptional congruence, implicit hinge and explicit link could potentially be 
             assigned the same materials (= constitutive laws); for the time being, however, implicit 
             hinges are treated as a special flavour of the more general link element. While all constitutive 
             models supported by the implicit hinge can be assigned to an explicit link element, the opposite 
             is not true. 

             Independent of this, we must be able to distinguish results of an implicit hinge (= hosted by beam 
             with number=NR) and results of an explicit link element (possibly with the same number=NR). 
             Therefore, in addition to the implicit hinge results (-> BEAM_HRC) a new data type/ result record 
             is introduced for the explicit link elements (-> LINK_RES).


     @0=       NR        [int]   |element number
     @1#       TYP       [int]   |reaction type (direction)
                                  #define LINK_RES_TYP_FX  11 = force in local x
                                  #define LINK_RES_TYP_FY  12 = force in local y
                                  #define LINK_RES_TYP_FZ  13 = force in local z
                                  #define LINK_RES_TYP_MX  14 = bending moment about local x
                                  #define LINK_RES_TYP_MY  15 = bending moment about local y
                                  #define LINK_RES_TYP_MZ  16 = bending moment about local z
     @2#       MTYP      [int]   |material type, cf. Rec: 173/NR:0  SPRI_WL0
     @3#       IBIT      [int]   |reserved
     @0:       DUMMY     [-]     |reserved 
     @1:       REAC      [*]     |reaction force / moment [kN, kNm]
     @2:       DISP      [*]     |displacement translational / rotational [m, rad]
     @3:       STV     12[*]     |state variables
                                  for MTYP=1:3 (PLAS,PISO,HYPE) :
                                     (1): nonlinear (plastic) displacement/ rotation in neg. direction (compression) [m, rad]
                                     (2): nonlinear (plastic) displacement/ rotation in pos. direction (tension) [m, rad]
                                     (3:12): unused
                                  for MTYP=5:6 (MTAK,PIVO) :
                                     (1): max. deformation in neg. direction (compression) [m, rad]
                                     (2): max. deformation in pos. direction (tension) [m, rad]
                                     (3): force apex of the inner loop for the negative quadrant
                                     (4): deformation apex of the inner loop for the negative quadrant
                                     (5): force apex of the inner loop for the positive quadrant
                                     (6): deformation apex of the inner loop for the positive quadrant
                                     (7): inner loop negative deformation on complete unloading 
                                     (8): inner loop positive deformation on complete unloading 
                                     (9): current targeted point for the negative quadrant (described by deformation only) 
                                     (10): current targeted point for the positive quadrant (described by deformation only) 
                                     (11:12): unused
                                  for MTYP=10 (SPB Single Pendulum Bearing) :  
                                     for device groups 1:
                                     (1): reaction force [-]
                                     (2): back force [-]
                                     (3): penalty forces [-]
                                     (4): deformation (total) [m]
                                     (5:12): unused
                                  for MTYP=11 (TPB Triple Pendulum Bearing) :  
                                     for device groups 1-3:
                                     (1:4): reaction force [-], back force [-], penalty forces [-], deformation [m] device group 1
                                     (5:8): reaction force [-], back force [-], penalty forces [-], deformation [m] device group 2
                                     (9:12): reaction force [-], back force [-], penalty forces [-], deformation [m] device group 3
     @15:      PIDX(0)  6[-]     |0:performance index for category PERF_CAT_UNSPEC, 1-5: performance indices by category, cf. Rec: 16/0:0   PERF_CAT

                               | gruppenfreie Knoteneigenschaften für Quadergebnisse
     @Rec: 211/0:Z+:+ QUAD_NGD | grouped properties of Quad-nodes \
                               | Knotengruppen Knoteneigenschaften für Quadergebnisse
{/red}
     @0=  NG       [int]    |groupnumber |Gruppennummer
     @1#  NR       [int]    |nodenumber  |Knotennummer
          only for 200/2 types:
     @2:  D        [1010]   |minimum thickness of plate on node \
                            |minimale Platten-Dicke im Knoten
     @3:  T        3[-,-,-] |lokal average coordinate system\
                            |gemitteltes lokales Koordinatensystem


     The definition of local coordinate systems for nodes belonging
     to QUAD elements is somehow complicated, but it allows the de-
     finition of all complex structures.

     First, results in nodes may be only averaged if the elements are
     not connected with a third element or a boundary support which
     introduces a jump of the forces or moments. This is detected by
     counting the occurences of edges. All edges accuring more than
     twice define a possible jump. The user my have separated the
     elements at those edges in different groups, but this is not
     allways true. For those cases. We have multiple element results
     for the same group/node location. These are treated as subgroups.

     For each such an instance there will be a negative group selector
     defining the subgroup and the QUAD-elements belonging to that
     subgroup, followed by the property record. The subgroups are
     given in descending order, indicating the last subgroup with
     number 1.

     Example for node 618 connecting elements of group 2 and 3:

          -2002   618   2112 2113
              2   618   D, T-values
          -2001   618   2212 2213
              2   618   D, T-values
              3   618   D, T-Values

     The results are stored with the same pattern, ie. there are
     three records for node 618 in that case.

     211/0 and 200/1 are different: 211/0 saves subgroups using the
     groupnumber, while 200/1 does not use this information to allow
     interpolation of results if the QUAD properties do not change.
     (See ASE/BEMESS Version 2.2-97 from 22.4.98)

                             for example:
                             lokal  x = t(1,1)*x + t(2,1)*y + t(3,1)*z
                             global x = t(1,1)*x + t(1,2)*y + t(1,3)*z

   P-elements are used only for the analysis. If these elements are
   used, separate 200/0 Elements are generated which allow all the
   postprocessing with standard algorithms.

  201/LC   Free loads on Quad-elements have been removed
           SOFILOAD has the option to convert them to 12/LC loadings
{red}
     @Rec: 202/LC  QUAD_LOA | Quad-element loads                                :V200501
{/red}
     @0#  VON      [int]    |start elementnumber |Von Elementnummer
     @1#  BIS      [int]    |end elementnumber   |Bis Elementnummer
     @2#  DEL      [int]    |increment           |Inkrement
                              0 = all elements, values are from primary group selection
                              1 = all elements, values are explicit or from secondary group selection
                             -1 = all elements, as 0, but VON/BIS have been adjusted to defined range
     @3#  TYP      [int]    |type of load        |Lasttyp
                             2????       program generated load
                             1????       user generated load
                             0????       user defined load
                               #00 P     internal load in local components
                               #01 PX    load local x
                               #02 PY    load local y
                               #03 PZ    load local z
                               #04 PXP   load global X related to X
                               #05 PYP   load global Y related to Y
                               #06 PZP   load global Z related to Z
                               #07 PXX   load global X on surface
                               #08 PYY   load global Y on surface
                               #09 PZZ   load global Z on surface
                               #10 PG    load global gravity
                                         (mass distrib. now illegal)
                               #11 EX    strain eps-x
                               #12 EY    strain eps-y
                               #13 EZ    strain eps-z
                               #14 KY    curvature kx
                               #15 KZ    Curvature ky
                               #16 WZ    Displacement of bedding
                               #17 DTXY  temperature increase (TEMP)
                               #18 SWEL  reserviert Quelldruck
                               #19 T     Temperature
                               #20 DTZ   temperature gradient
                               #21 VMX   prestress mxx
                               #22 VMY   prestress myy
                               #23 VMXY  prestress mxy
                               #24 VVX   prestress vx
                               #25 VVY   prestress vy
                               #26 VNX   prestress nxx
                               #27 VNY   prestress nyy
                               #28 VNXY  prestress nxy
                               #31 PHI   reserved for creep
                               #32 PRIM  reserved for primary loadcase
                               #33 V     reserved factor prestress (GEOS)
                               #34 WIND  Factor wind (used by SOFILOAD)
                               #35 SNOW  Factor snow (used by SOFILOAD)
                               #41 EMX   influence mxx
                               #42 EMY   influence myy
                               #43 EMXY  influence mxy
                               #44 EVX   influence vx
                               #45 EVY   influence vy
                               #46 ENX   influence nxx
                               #47 ENY   influence nyy
                               #48 ENXY  influence nxy
                               #50 TEND  prestressing loads from tendons

                               >200      multiphysics BC conditions 3D

     @4#  LNR     [int]     |special option value
                             TYP = 18/31/32   primary loadcasenumber
                             TYP = 33         construction stage number
                             TYP = 34         predefined windpressure index
                                              1 = ebene Flächen
                                              2 + 32*Durchmesser in mm (CYL)
                                              3 + 32*Reynoldszahl      (CYLR)
                                              4 + 32*(10*VTYP) - VBG   (CYLK)
                                              5 + 32*Fouriertyp        (CYLF)
     @0:  P       [*]       |load values
     @1:  dPdX    [*]         p(z) = P + (x-xref) * dPdX
     @2:  dPdY    [*]                  + (y-yref) * dPdY
     @3:  dPdZ    [*]                  + (z-zref) * dPdZ
     @4:  XREF    [1001]    |optional reference point for load value to
                             allow a variant load value in global directions
     @5:  YREF    [1001]
     @6:  ZREF    [1001]
     @7:  TFUN  16[1010,1]  |optional function of load values across the
                             thickness for temperature loadings
                             Convention (see also 102/LC): 
                             * only positive values for the distance TFUN(1,i) will
                               be adjusted to the upper part of the QUAD-element
                               The distance 0 is the topmost fibre
                             * only negative values for the distance TFUN(1,i) will
                               be adjusted to the lower part of the QUAD-element
                               The distance 0 is the lowest fibre
                             * positive and negative values for the distance will
                               be always scaled to cover the full thickness.

     Remark 1: Load values of DTZ are saved with opposite sign to insure compatibility
               with old data definitions in DWG and CDB
     Remark 2: older data format: only one value DPZ at position 1


     Attention special format for loadtype 00 (f.e. wind or external waves by sofiload):

      0:  Q        [1192]   |(wind/wave) pressure |(Stau)druck
      1:  cPx      [-]      | factor tangential = local x
      2:  cPy      [-]      | factor tangential = local y
      3:  cPz      [-]      | factor normal     = local z
      4:  cUx      [1212]   | fluid velocity component
      5:  cUy      [1212]   | fluid velocity component
      6:  cUz      [1212]   | fluid velocity component
      7:  per      [90]     | period for loading
      8:  phip     [90]     | phase  for pressure
      9:  phix     [90]     | phase  for x-component
     10:  phiy     [90]     | phase  for y-component
     11:  phiz     [90]     | phase  for z-component

     The use of this record is within the headder as follows:
         0 - record with maximum/minimum stresses
        -m - header records for all possible material types, allowing WINGRAF to create
             its selection trees fast
     Then there are blocks of data for the elements, each with a headder identifying
     the storage scheme of the hardening parameters.
        -m - exactly one header record
        +n - results of elements

     For elder data the default is:

         [101, 1092, maxval]
         [102,    1, maxval]

            N1  +---------------+  N2

Sectional stresses are calculated by AQB for a FE-section and saved in
the database of the section, but with a reference to the beams where it
is used, thus we have:

     229/LC:0     Total maxima
     229/LC:-NB   First beamsection NB,X using this FE-section
     229/LC:0     Maximum of this beamsection
     229/LC:+NQ   results in center of QUADS
     229/LC:-NB   Second beamsection NB,X using this FE-section
     229/LC:0     Maximum of this beamsection
     229/LC:+NQ   results in center of QUADS

Record provides parameters for display in Wingraf/Resultviewer that are required for 
an analytical slab deflection analysis according to Eurocode 1992-1-1, 7.4.3

The distribution coefficient XI is given within the value range [-1;+1]. A negative value
indicates cracking on the negative (upper) side and a positive value cracking on the
lower side of the slab. A value of zero indicates uncracked state.

LC=0 is the standard value where the results are stored in.

Errors in concrete design are marked as follows:

Cause           ASO     ASOQ    ASU     ASUQ     ASS     ASOI   ASUI
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
shear            v       v       v       v     999999.    v      v
        o/u
other  (2/2)   999999. 999999. 999999. 999999.    v      RW     RW
       (2/3)   999999. 999999. 999999. 999999.    v      RW    999999.
       (3/2)   999999. 999999. 999999. 999999.    v    999999.  RW
       (3/3)   999999. 999999. 999999. 999999.    v    999999. 999999.

       'v' stands for a normal 'value' from the design

All directions are store as packed 4Byte ANSI-strings (FORTRAN: RCHAR)
Their meaning is:

   - the angle of the reinforcement in degrees if explicitly selected
   - or the Literal '   X' resp. '   Y' for automatic selection
   - or the Literal '****' if a reinforcement is not possible

     @Rec: 300/00  BRIC | Bric-elements                                        :V200501 \
                         | BRIC-Elemente
{/red}
     @0=  NR       [int]    |elementnumber  | Elementnummer
     @1#  NODE    8[int]    |nodenumbers    | Knotennummern
     @9#  MAT      [int]    |materialnumber | Materialnummer
     @10# NRA      [int]    |type of element|Ansatz des Elementes
                             bit pattern:
                            #define BRIC_NRA_STANDARD                    0 = |Standard    |Standard
                            #define BRIC_NRA_TETRAEDER                 256 = |Tetraeder
                                                                              otherwise hexaeder
                            #define BRIC_NRA_INTERFACE                 512 = |Interface element
                                                                              (area  1-4 and 5-8 may coincide)
                            #define BRIC_NRA_ERROR                    1024 =     |Multiplier for errors and warnings
                            #define BRIC_NRA_ERROR_IMPROPER_TRANSFORMATION  1 =  |Warning: improper transformation
                            #define BRIC_NRA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_GEOMETRY         2 =  |Error: illegal geometry
                            #define BRIC_NRA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_JACOBI_CENTER    3 =  |Error: illegal Jacobi in Center
                            #define BRIC_NRA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_JACOBI_CORNER    4 =  |Error: illegal Jacobi in Corner
                            #define BRIC_NRA_MULTIPLIER_VOLUME        8192 = |Multiplier for Volume number
     @0:  DET(0)  4[*]      |Values of Jacobian Determinant / Volume

     Tetraeder elements are stored in such a way that K4==0
     and K8=K7=K6=K5. The orientation is those that K1-K5
     are counter clock wise. D0 is the volume of the tetraeder.
     For cubes the colume will be 8.0*D0

     @2:  dPdY    [*]                  + (y-yref) * dPdY
     @3:  dPdZ    [*]                  + (z-zref) * dPdZ

     @5:  YREF    [1001]
     @6:  ZREF    [1001]

     scheme, thus points 1,3,5 and 7 are on the downside, while

                    A s                            A s
        N8  +---------------+  N7      N4  +---------------+  N3
            |       |       |              |       |       |
            |  GP3  |  GP7  |              |  GP4  |  GP8  |
            |       +-------|-->r          |       +-------|-->r
            |  GP1     GP5  |              |  GP2     GP6  |
            |               |              |               |
        N5  +---------------+  N6      N1  +---------------+  N2
                   t<0                            t>0

!TOPIC 212 Influence Lines

Influence lines in ELLA are saved in a separate database .cdi.
The main KWH is the name of the axis, the secondary KWL is the number of the lane.

!TOPIC 900 FORTRAN MODULES

Modules in FORTRAN may contain

- Definitionen of parameters and structures
  from this description the Fortran files CDBTYPE???.F90 in LIB\CDBASE\SRC will
  be generated automatically. They will yield the modules CDB_TYPES_???
  All names are derived from the CDBASE documentation automatically
  (see {link}124{-link}STRUCTURES{/link})

- Global PUBLIC variables and PRIVATE Variables for the module functions

- Functions to work on these structures/variables (Memberfunctions)
  These functions have unique names bound to the module and are
  described within the sources as comments and thus also with DOXYGEN

Modules may be USEd recursively, e.g. the module CDB_LF includes the module
CDB_TYPES_LFC. It is allowed to USE both modules explicitly, but duplicate
definitions are not possible. To avoid conflicts with names, FORTRAN allows
with an ONLY clause to introduce only specific definitions.

It is recommended to use IMPLICIT NONE and to declare all variables to
avoid side effects with global variables in Modules.

For the Convenience of the FORTRAN Programmer quite a lot of functions exist
to access the database.

CDBGEO.F90        Geometry kernel

CDBSYST.F90       Accessing FE-Data
CDBPUTSYST.F90    Creating FE-Data

CDBLF.F90         Loadcase and loadtype definitions
CDBLFT.F90        Loadtrain definitions
